author: akaszynski
body:
## What

The `build-arm` (aarch64) job runs on **every PR** and pays the full `-flto=auto`
+ `-O3` link cost, while the x86_64 PR `build` job was deliberately made
LTO-off/`-O2` for the same gate purpose. Condition the aarch64 PR build the same
way: LTO-off/`-O2` on `pull_request`, optimized `-O3`+LTO on push/release/merge_group.

```yaml
CIBW_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request'
  && 'FVTK_LTO=0 FVTK_GATE_O2=1 FVTK_SOURCE_UNITY=1'
  || 'FVTK_SOURCE_UNITY=1' }}
```

## Why it's safe (shipped wheels unchanged, parity untouched)

- The aarch64 PR wheel is **never published** and is consumed by **no numeric
  gate**: the only job that `needs: build-arm` is `publish`, which is
  `if: github.event_name == 'release'`. On `release`/`push`/`merge_group` the
  ternary yields `FVTK_SOURCE_UNITY=1` only → `-O3` + LTO, byte-for-byte the
  current shipped aarch64 wheel. Only the `pull_request` path changes.
- LTO changes inlining, not FP values; `-O2` vs `-O3` is IEEE-identical without
  `-ffast-math`. `FVTK_SOURCE_UNITY=1` (byte-identical objects) is kept on both
  paths. So bit-exactness is irrelevant to this leg either way — and no bitexact/
  render gate consumes the arm wheel regardless.

## Win

LTO is ~2–3× the link cost (~30–40 min cold vs ~13 min LTO-off per the build
docs). `build-arm` frequently is the PR gate long-pole, so this takes an
estimated ~15–25 min off the PR critical path on a cold/thin-cache run. Pure CI
infra; no source or shipped-behavior change.

## Idiom

Uses the same `${{ <cond> && 'a' || 'b' }}` scalar form already in this workflow
(e.g. `runs-on: ${{ vars.FVTK_RUNNER_LINUX_ARM64 || 'ubuntu-24.04-arm' }}`).

author: machado470
body:
### Motivation

- Remove unsafe physical deletion of charges and replace it with a logical, auditable, tenant-safe cancellation flow to preserve financial history and satisfy operational audit requirements. 
- Keep existing operational flows (payment, timeline, risk) intact while preventing data evaporation and ensuring traceability.

### Description

- Replaced physical `deleteCharge` with `cancelCharge(orgId, chargeId, userId, input)` implemented in `FinanceService`; `cancelCharge` validates `cancellationReason`, enforces concurrency via `expectedUpdatedAt`, blocks cancellation of `PAID` charges, marks status `CANCELED`, and fills `canceledAt`, `canceledByUserId` and `cancellationReason` without deleting the record. 
- Added Prisma fields to `Charge`: `canceledAt: DateTime?`, `cancellationReason: String?`, `canceledByUserId: String?` and included a migration `prisma/migrations/20260623120000_charge_auditable_cancellation/migration.sql`. 
- Controller change: added `POST /finance/charges/:id/cancel` (accepts `CancelChargeDto`) and turned the legacy `DELETE /finance/charges/:id` into a `405`-like `MethodNotAllowedException` with a clear message. 
- Timeline and audit: cancellation emits `CHARGE_CANCELED` via `TimelineService.log` with metadata (`chargeId`, `customerId`, `serviceOrderId`, `amountCents`, `previousStatus`, `nextStatus`, `cancellationReason`, `canceledByUserId`, `canceledAt`) and also records an audit event via `AuditService.log`. 
- BFF/TRPC: replaced `trpc.finance.charges.delete` with `trpc.finance.charges.cancel` that calls `/finance/charges/:id/cancel` and validates `cancellationReason` and optional `expectedUpdatedAt` (no `orgId` from client). 
- Frontend (`FinancesPage`): prompts for a cancellation reason, blocks cancelling `PAID` charges, calls the new `cancel` mutation, and displays cancellation date and reason in the charge detail UI. 
- Tests: added/updated unit and contract tests for backend cancellation behavior and BFF contract tests verifying tenant-safe payloads and reason validation.

### Testing

- Ran `pnpm prisma generate` successfully to refresh Prisma client. 
- Typechecks and build completed: `pnpm -r typecheck` and `pnpm -s build` succeeded. 
- Backend tests: `pnpm --filter ./apps/api test` passed (added `FinanceService cancelCharge` tests cover idempotency, paid-block, reason validation, timeline and audit logging). 
- BFF/frontend tests: `pnpm --filter ./apps/web test` passed (contract tests updated to call `finance.charges.cancel` and validate payload/no `orgId`). 
- Lint: `pnpm -r lint` completed without blocking errors.

author: alexandercloch-netizen
body:
## Why (Roadmap Phase 1 · item 4 of 5)

From the audit: *"Tactics need numbers, not just a pretty map."* The live race screen showed speed/position but none of the instruments a tactician actually steers by. This adds them.

## What changed

- **`polarTargetSpeed`** (engine): the boat's polar speed for the current angle & wind — what a perfectly sailed boat would do. The new **% Polar** readout is the gap between that and your live speed, i.e. the cost of crew/hull condition and a conservative effort dial.
- **`laylines`** (engine): the close-hauled (upwind) or running (downwind) approach lines to the next mark, returned when the mark can't be fetched directly (null on a reach, where they'd be meaningless).
- **`RouteMap`**: a new `laylines` prop draws the two approach lines (thin dashed) into the mark — the headline tactician visual.
- **Race HUD**: a **VMG / Target / % Polar** instrument row, the laylines on the chart, and an **"Ahead: veering/backing · building/easing"** wind-trend line read from the field.

Together: you can now see how close you're sailing to polars, where the laylines are, and what the breeze is about to do — and act on it with the effort/side dials.

## Verification
`npm run tsc` clean · `npm test` **226 passed** (new: `polarTargetSpeed`, `laylines` upwind vs reach) · `npm run build:web` clean. e2e is now a required check and gates this merge.

Next: **item 5 — the post-race tactician's debrief** (your track vs the optimal, miles gained/lost, corrected-time delta).

author: askwigconsulting
body:
## Cohort improvement proposal — close the Codex/Cursor golden-lock

> The first trip through Cohort's own self-improvement loop. Recorded as a **draft PR** — the loop
> suggests and never decides; a human reviews and merges.

**Loop provenance**
- `cohort feedback --rating down --command recompile` — "Codex/Cursor renderer output is not
  byte-locked; recompile is unguarded for those two IDEs (golden-lock sub-gate open)."
- `cohort propose-improvement` surfaced the signal (command friction: `recompile`).
- The Steward (in-IDE enrichment) drafted the concrete change below.

**Evidence**
- Phase 7 shipped the Codex/Cursor adapters with an intentional two-step gate: structure + coverage +
  byte-stability locked then; concrete bytes deferred to a golden-lock sub-gate.
- That left Codex/Cursor rendering regression-unguarded — a renderer change wouldn't be caught the way
  Claude's goldens catch it.

**Change**
- Lock 16 staged files per IDE (15 agents + the hooks merge payload) under
  `tests/golden/roster/{codex,cursor}/`.
- Add `tests/test_golden_lock.py`: `compile_ide` output must be byte-identical to the goldens.
- Full suite: **355 passed, 1 skipped**.

**Honest caveat (for your review)**
- These bytes are **doc-cited** (verified against Codex/Cursor docs in Phase 7), **not** validated
  against a live Codex/Cursor install. The field-level items — exact hook-event names, Cursor
  frontmatter/skills dir — remain doc-cited. This lock is a **regression guard on current renderer
  output**; when a real install confirms the mappings, the renderer and these goldens move together.
- So this *partially* closes the sub-gate (byte regression protection now); the live-install
  validation is the remaining follow-up. Your review is the gate that decides whether locking
  doc-cited bytes now is the right call, or whether to wait for a real install.

**Safety**: opened `--draft`; no auto-merge, no push to `master`. Merge is yours.

author: joogo01
body:
Implements AUZ-100 per ADR-0006: a re-import no longer toasts the wallet's entire history.

## What it does

At import the chain tip N is pinned and persisted (`Meta.scan_target_height`, read from `GetLightdInfo`). During the Initial scan the transactions found in the pinned range [birthday, N] are recorded silently. Crossing N emits one "Wallet ready" toast and the wallet goes live, after which each freshly seen txid notifies, deduped by txid across rounds and restarts. The phase is read from the heights, not a stored flag, so a process killed mid-scan resumes in the Initial scan.

The seen-set, the silent/notify decision, and the crossing edge moved into a `NotificationPolicy` module (`notify_policy.rs`) with unit tests.

## A transaction's silence is judged by its block height

pepper-sync scans tip-first, so `synced_height` passes N before the older blocks are walked. Gating the per-transaction toast on `synced_height` let a stale historical transaction found after that jump notify, which a re-import surfaced. So a transaction's silence rides on its own block height (below N silent, at or past N or in the mempool notifies), while the one-time "Wallet ready" still rides on `synced_height` reaching N. Clarified in ADR-0006.

## Verification

Verified on Kubuntu: a fresh re-import scans silently (no per-tx toasts for historical transactions), one "Wallet ready" at the crossing, and per-tx toasts for new activity. `cargo check` and the 22 lib tests (6 new in `notify_policy`) green.

Commits: `a9b5b68` (policy + module + N pinned), `ecb4695` (height-based gate + ADR note).

body:
# [S-18.14] Dispatcher resolver WASM path resolution fix (TOML-parent-relative) + log_dir observability **Epic:** E-18 — Context Durability **Mode:** brownfield / feature **Convergence:** CONVERGED after 24 adversarial passes (BC-5.39.001 STRICT 3-CLEAN: passes 22/23/24 all CLEAN) ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-5%2F5-brightgreen) ![Red Gates](https://img.shields.io/badge/red_gates-5%20GREEN-brightgreen) ![Spec Passes](https://img.shields.io/badge/spec_adversary-24_passes-brightgreen) ![Priority](https://img.shields.io/badge/priority-P0_HIGH-red) Fix a P0 production regression in `resolver_loader::load_registry`: relative WASM plugin paths were resolved against process CWD (`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, the user's project directory) instead of the TOML file's parent directory (`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`). This caused 8,560 `resolver.load_error` events for the `wave_context` resolver across recent dispatcher sessions, with **zero successful loads since rc.21**. The fix adds the proven `if let Some(base) = path.parent() { if entry.plugin.is_relative() { entry.plugin = base.join(&entry.plugin); } }` pattern (mirroring `registry.rs::resolve_plugin_paths`) before the single `get_or_compile` call site in `load_registry`. Additionally emits `log_dir` (absolutized at emission) in the `dispatcher.started` event for observability — operators can now locate the dispatcher's internal log directory without re-running the seven-level ADR-024 path resolution algorithm. > **RELEASE DEPENDENCY (prominent):** The operator-level cached dispatcher at > `~/.claude/plugins/cache/.../vsdd-factory//` picks up this fix ONLY after an rc > release is cut. Develop-branch edits do NOT affect the cached plugin. A release MUST > be cut after this story merges. This is an out-of-band delivery note — not a deferral. --- ## Architecture Changes ```mermaid graph TD A["resolver_loader::load_registry\n(MODIFIED — SS-01)"] -->|"if let Some(base) = path.parent()\nif entry.plugin.is_relative(){\n entry.plugin = base.join(entry.plugin)\n}"| B["get_or_compile\n(unchanged)"] C["main.rs DISPATCHER_STARTED\n(MODIFIED — SS-01)"] -->|".with_field('log_dir',\nstd::path::absolute(log_dir)\n.display().to_string())"| D["InternalLog::log_dir()\naccessor — UNCHANGED"] E["registry.rs::resolve_plugin_paths\n(REFERENCE — existing proven pattern)"] -.->|"mirrors"| A style A fill:#90EE90 style C fill:#90EE90 style B fill:#f0f0f0 style D fill:#f0f0f0 style E fill:#e8e8e8 ``` **Before (regression):** `load_registry` called `path.canonicalize()` on `&entry.plugin` (relative path) against process CWD. Claude Code invokes the dispatcher with CWD = user's project dir. WASM plugins live under `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`. CWD join → non-existent path → `Err(ENOENT)` → `resolver.load_error`. **After (fix):** Resolver relative paths joined against `path.parent()` (TOML file's parent dir = `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`) before the `get_or_compile` call. Mirrors `registry.rs::resolve_plugin_paths` (proven pattern since S-12.04).
Architecture Decision Record — ADR-024 §Decision 1 Addendum + §Decision 5 **ADR-024 §Decision 1 Addendum — CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR vs CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:** `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (process CWD when Claude Code invokes the dispatcher) and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` are distinct paths. Code in `resolver_loader.rs` MUST resolve relative `entry.plugin` paths using `path.parent()` (the TOML file's parent directory), NOT `std::env::current_dir()`. This mirrors `registry.rs::resolve_plugin_paths` which computes `let base = path.parent()` and has been correct since delivery. **ADR-024 §Decision 5 — log_dir observability:** The `dispatcher.started` event MUST include an absolute `log_dir` field computed via `std::path::absolute(internal_log.log_dir()).unwrap_or_else(|_| internal_log.log_dir().to_path_buf()).display().to_string()` at the emission site in `main.rs`. The `InternalLog::log_dir()` accessor stays verbatim (returns `&Path`). Absolutization is at emission, not at storage. **Consequences:** - `wave_context` resolver loads on every dispatch (fixes 8,560-error regression) - Both `fail_closed: true` and `fail_closed: false` arms benefit (single resolved path feeds both) - Operators can read `log_dir` from any `dispatcher.started` JSONL event without replaying path resolution - No new dependencies; no API surface changes
--- ## Story Dependencies ```mermaid graph LR S1814["S-18.14\n✅ this PR\nP0 HIGH fix"] NoDeps["(no depends_on)\nStandalone W10"] NoBlocks["(no blocks)\nNo downstream E-18 deps"] NoDeps --> S1814 S1814 --> NoBlocks style S1814 fill:#FFD700 style NoDeps fill:#e8e8e8 style NoBlocks fill:#e8e8e8 ``` S-18.14 has an empty `depends_on` and empty `blocks` arrays. Standalone W10 story. No dependency PRs need to be merged first. --- ## Spec Traceability ```mermaid flowchart LR BC["BC-1.13.001 v1.12\nDispatcher MUST load\nresolvers-registry.toml\nat startup"] --> INV8["INV-8\nTOML-parent-relative\npath resolution"] BC --> PC9["PC-9\nSuccessful resolver\nload"] BC --> PC10["PC-10\nlog_dir observability\nin dispatcher.started"] INV8 --> AC001["AC-001\nif-let-Some path.parent\nis_relative guard"] INV8 --> AC002["AC-002\nCWD vs TOML-parent\ndistinction proven"] PC9 --> AC003["AC-003\nZero load_error\nwhen artifact at TOML-parent"] PC9 --> AC004["AC-004\nBoth fail_closed\narms benefit"] PC10 --> AC005["AC-005\nlog_dir field\nabsolutized at emission"] PC10 --> AC006["AC-006\nlog_dir in every\ndispatcher.started JSONL"] INV8 --> AC007["AC-007\nwave_context loads\nproduction-like fixture"] AC001 --> RG001["RG-001\ntest_BC_1_13_001_load_registry\n_resolves_relative_plugin\n_against_toml_parent"] AC002 --> RG001 AC003 --> RG001 AC001 --> RG002["RG-002\ntest_BC_1_13_001_load_registry\n_absolute_plugin_path\n_passes_through"] AC004 --> RG003["RG-003\ntest_BC_1_13_001_load_registry\n_fail_closed_false\n_toml_parent_relative_resolves"] AC005 --> RG005["RG-005\ntest_BC_1_13_001_dispatcher\n_started_event_log_dir\n_absolutized_at_emission"] AC006 --> RG005 AC007 --> RG006["RG-006\ntest_BC_1_13_001_load_registry\n_wave_context_production_fixture"] RG001 --> SRC1["resolver_loader.rs\n(if-let-Some base pattern)"] RG002 --> SRC1 RG003 --> SRC1 RG005 --> SRC2["main.rs\n(DISPATCHER_STARTED\n+ log_dir field)"] RG006 --> SRC1 ``` --- ## ## Summary
- persist parsed-field work-in-progress state as extension-owned metadata per hostname/page/selected target
- restore active, failed, unchanged, successful, included/excluded, split-field, active template, and draft URL state after panel close or reload
- keep live navigation stable across 404s, unchanged-image results, successful projections, and async save ordering

## Root Cause
Parsed URL field state only lived in panel memory. Closing or reloading the panel rebuilt fields from the page's original selected image, and later fixes exposed a few live-state hazards: failed/unchanged navigations could drop included fields, stale drafts could be saved after successful projection, and older async saves could overwrite newer resume state.

## Notes
- Resume state is not Recents, not a pin/bookmark, and does not use host-page localStorage.
- Follow-up pass/fail URL tracking was split to #142.

Closes #129

## Validation
- npm run typecheck
- npm test
- npm run format:check
- npm run lint
- npm run build

## Manual Test Run
- Increment a parsed field from a working image to a 404/missing image; expected: field shows the failure marker while included state remains included.
- Continue to a working image, then to an unchanged/same-image result; expected: unchanged marker appears without clearing included state.
- Stop on the latest visible working value, wait, close/reopen the panel; expected: the field value and selected image restore to the last visible state, not one behind.
- Select a different target image; expected: stale parsed-field markers do not apply to the new target.

author: fgfg12138
body:
## Summary

**This is a large product-milestone PR, not a small patch.** It combines two related bodies of work on `feature/p2-real-close-execution` (13 commits, 69 files, +4061 / -1742):

1. **P1.1 — Legacy surface cleanup** (7 commits)
2. **P2 — Complete trading closed loop** (6 commits)

Together they take the product from \"only opens positions\" to a full arbitrage tool: **open → position → close-plan → close-execution → post-close verification → review**.

---

## P1.1 — Legacy surface cleanup

- Remove `/risk-center` page and dead V1.0 nav component cluster
- Remove V1.0 simulation/funding/basis/opportunities/summary API routes
- Re-delete risk-center/nav cluster accidentally restored by a git checkout
- Gate E/F-area V121 engineering APIs behind `V121_ENABLE_DEV_TOOLS`
- Replace broken V1.0 `original*` tests with product-surface acceptance tests
- Fix pre-existing broken phase3/4/5 boundary tests to reach full green
- Docs: P1.1 legacy cleanup assessment

## P2 — Complete close execution cycle

Real Binance same-exchange spot-perp arbitrage close, with strict safety boundaries.

### New modules
- `closeExecutionTypes.ts` — types + Chinese label maps (`CLOSE_STATUS_LABEL`, `POSITION_STATE_LABEL`)
- `closePlanLedger.ts` — independent `close_plan_ledger` table
- `closeExecutionLedger.ts` — independent `close_execution_ledger` table (separate from plan, per design requirement)
- `closePrecheckGate.ts` — close-side pre-execution gate (mirrors open-side `preOrderExecutionGate`)
- `closePlanBuilder.ts` — builds close plan; **closeable qty = min(system record, exchange actual)** (exchange snapshot as ground truth)
- `guardedCloseExecutor.ts` — ledger-before-submission, perp-first leg order, post-close verification, protected state on any failure/unknown/partial
- Binance adapter close legs: `getPositionMode` (Hedge/One-way detection + cache), `submitPerpBuyCloseMarket`, `submitSpotSellMarket`

### New API routes (under existing MAINNET_TINY namespace)
- `POST/GET /api/v121/mainnet-tiny/close-plan`
- `POST /api/v121/mainnet-tiny/close-plan/test`
- `POST/GET /api/v121/mainnet-tiny/close-execution`
- `GET  /api/v121/mainnet-tiny/close-execution/[id]`
- `GET  /api/v121/mainnet-tiny/close-gate`

### Rewritten/updated product surfaces
- `/trade/close` — 5-step flow mirroring `/trade/open` (select position → generate plan → exchange param check → pre-execution gate → confirm close)
- `/positions` — `?include=closed` query param; default hides CLOSED; \"显示已平仓\" toggle
- `/review` — integrates `close_plan_ledger` + `close_execution_ledger`; new \"平仓执行明细\" table (status, net PnL, post-close verification, frozen reason, timestamp)

---

## Design note: why close APIs live under `mainnet-tiny/`

The close API paths use the existing `mainnet-tiny` namespace rather than `/positions/[id]/close-*`. **P2 reuses the existing MAINNET_TINY controlled-execution namespace** — the open chain already lives there (`order-plan`, `order-execution`, `preflight`, `gate`), so close keeps a symmetric, co-located safety surface.

**The frontend product pages do NOT expose this internal namespace.** `/trade/close` calls these routes internally but renders only product words (用户确认串 `CONFIRM_CLOSE_POSITION` → 后端 `EXECUTE_REAL_CLOSE_POSITION`). The `mainnet-tiny` name is an internal engineering label for the controlled-execution tier, never shown to users. This is consistent with the open side and the existing safety-audit exemption list.

---

## Safety boundaries preserved

- **Binance only.** OKX/HTX/cross-exchange close → `not_supported`.
- **No unattended auto-close.** Close is always user-initiated with a typed confirm string.
- **No auto leg-repair, no auto-retry.** Any failure/unknown/partial → `protected` state (position FROZEN).
- **Two independent env gates:** open requires `V121_ENABLE_REAL_ORDER_EXECUTION=1` + `EXECUTE_REAL_TWO_LEG_ORDER`; close requires `V121_ENABLE_REAL_CLOSE_EXECUTION=1` + `EXECUTE_REAL_CLOSE_POSITION`.
- **Kill switch + freeze respected:** EXIT allowed under `PAUSE_NEW_ENTRIES`; `freezeState` level2 blocks all close, level1 blocks `normal_tp`.
- **Perp-first leg order:** perp BUY close-short FIRST, spot SELL second — so a second-leg failure leaves the book hedged (spot long, no short) rather than exposed (unhedged short).
- **Post-close verification** re-fetches exchange snapshot (perp SHORT cleared, spot balance reduced, executed qty matched) rather than trusting order status.
- **Ledger-before-submission:** initial row written with `ok:false` before any order submission, updated after each leg.
- **Hedge Mode** (dualSidePosition=true): `positionSide=SHORT`, no `reduceOnly`. **One-way Mode**: `reduceOnly=true`, no `positionSide`.
- **No engineering terms in UI** (dry-run/ClosePlan/OrderPlan/Intent/Ledger/Preflight/SHADOW/PAPER/mainnet-tiny) — enforced by `lint:i18n` + safety-audit exemption list.

## Verification (all green)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `lint:i18n` | ✅ no forbidden UI terms in `app/(app)/**` |
| `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.ci.json` | ✅ 0 errors |
| `vitest run` (full) | ✅ 4380 passed, 279 skipped |
| `v121:verify` (lib/strategy-v121) | ✅ 410 passed, exit 0 |
| `build` | ✅ 59 pages generated |
| `v121:product-smoke` | ✅ 12 passed (Review + Positions included) |

Note: `npx tsc --noEmit` (non-CI config) reports 118 errors, all in pre-existing test files (`lib/apiKeys/crypto.test.ts`, `lib/arbitrage/arbitragePositionEngine.test.ts`) unrelated to this PR — identical count before and after these changes.

## Pre-merge review checklist (6 points)

1. `/trade/close` shows no engineering terms (dry-run/ClosePlan/Ledger/Preflight)
2. Real close button disabled by default; requires `close-gate` open
3. `V121_ENABLE_REAL_CLOSE_EXECUTION` unset → backend rejects real close
4. Hedge Mode → Binance close-short does NOT send `reduceOnly`
5. Perp close failure/unknown/partial → spot leg NOT submitted
6. After successful close → both `/positions` and `/review` show the closed-loop result

author: jmmaloney4
body:
## Summary
Garden `detect` keeps failing **flakily** with *"the self-hosted runner lost communication with the server"* — and crucially, **often without a clean `OOMKilled` event**. The disconnect and the occasional OOM are the same root cause: the GitHub **runner agent** (`Runner.Listener`, which must heartbeat to GitHub) shares the runner pod's cgroup with the heavy `nix-eval-jobs` eval. When the eval pegs CPU + disk (garden: 143-node flake), the agent loses the scheduler/IO race and **misses heartbeats before the kernel OOM-killer even acts** → GitHub marks it "lost communication" instead of a real build failure.

## Change
Wrap the eval in `nice -n 19` + `ionice -c2 -n7` so the **normal-priority agent always preempts** the eval for CPU and disk IO — its heartbeats keep flowing even while the eval saturates the pod.

```sh
lowprio=()
command -v nice   >/dev/null 2>&1 && lowprio+=(nice -n 19)
command -v ionice >/dev/null 2>&1 && lowprio+=(ionice -c2 -n7)
"${lowprio[@]}" nix run …nix-eval-jobs…
```
Graceful-degrade prefix array (skips either tool if absent), so non-Linux / minimal consumers are unaffected. The eval is **deprioritised, not capped** — it still runs to completion, just yielding to the agent. (Left `--meta` and the eval-splitting for a follow-up.)

## Test plan
- [x] `bash -n` clean; verified the empty-array and missing-tool `&&` paths are safe under `set -euo pipefail`.
- [ ] Post-merge (live `@main`): a garden `detect` run completes without "lost communication"; if the eval is still too big it should now fail with a *real* error rather than a flaky disconnect.

## Risk
Low. Worst case the eval is slower under contention (intended). `@main`, so live to all consumers on merge — but the change is a no-op on uncontended runners.

## Links
- garden#1046 (runner OOM/disconnect) · ergodicsystems/hq#173

## R14 — US-3c 선도입 warn 3종 opt-in fail 승격

### 무엇을
정부양식 수용검사에서 **괄호선택란(paren_choices)·라벨변형(empty_label_fields_ext)·빈그림칸(empty_image_slots)** warn 3종을, 공고가 해당 항목을 필수로 요구할 때 **fail 로 승격해 제출불가(_DRAFT) 게이트에 편입**하는 opt-in 기능.

### 왜 opt-in 인가 (설계 판단)
이 세 검사는 `usage_acceptance.py` 주석에 **"오탐 표면적 큼 — 음성 코퍼스 검증 후 차기 fail 승격"** 으로 일부러 warn 도입됐다. 음성 코퍼스(멀쩡한 실제 양식 표본) 없이 무조건 fail 로 바꾸면 정상 문서가 거짓 '제출불가'가 되는 회귀가 난다. 따라서 `AcceptanceConfig.strict_acceptance`(**기본 False, 오탐 0 불변**) + CLI `--strict-acceptance` 로 opt-in 구현. 기본값 fail 승격은 코퍼스 확보 후 차기 과제.

### 구현
- `run_acceptance` 가 결과 생성 후 `_PROMOTABLE_WARN_IDS` 에 한해 severity 를 `SEV_FAIL` 로 승격. `submittable`/`fail_defects` 는 severity 기반 property 라 자동 정합.
- 3 게이트 배선(기존 blind_review/max_pages 패턴 동일): `self_diagnose.py`(직접 config) · `auto_write_autopilot.py`→`run_autopilot` · `submit.py`→`SubmissionPipeline.run`.

### 검증
- `py -3.11 -m pytest` **332 passed**(기준 326 + 신규 6, 회귀 0).
  - 엔진 5: 기본 warn 유지(None·기본 config)·승격 시 fail+제출불가·정확히 3종만·다른 warn 불변·결함0이면 제출가능.
  - autopilot 통합 1: 기본 exit/제출가능 유지 → strict 시 `_DRAFT` 강제.
- CLI E2E: paren 결함 문서 `self_diagnose` 기본 **exit 0(제출가능)** · `--strict-acceptance` **exit 2(제출불가)**.
- 적대적 코드리뷰 **SHIP**(무회귀·승격 범위한정·severity 변이안전·파이프라인 스레딩·테스트 적정성 5축 PASS, 치명/개선 0).

### 범위 밖(의도된 비대상)
- `bizplan_autopilot`: run_autopilot 내부 호출, 기본 False 로 무회귀(정부양식 제출 게이트가 아닌 AI 작성 래퍼).
- `strip_notebooklm.py` 독립 CLI: blind_review/max_pages 도 원래 미배선인 선재 격차 — 차기 일괄 처리.
- 기본값 fail 승격: 음성 코퍼스 확보 후.

author: duguankui
body:
Closes #407.

## Problem
A digitally-born PDF with generous line spacing (the reported JP services agreement — ~2.8× glyph height per line) emitted **one Markdown paragraph per visual line**: a single sentence was shredded into multiple paragraphs by a blank line at every wrap.

Two compounding causes (measured on the reported file):
- The paragraph-split threshold was anchored to the **glyph-box height** (`1.6 × ~9pt ≈ 14.8pt`), far below the document's real line pitch (~26pt), so **92–100%** of line gaps were mis-read as paragraph breaks.
- The over-split is realized at the **block level**: `RecursiveXYCut` cuts each loosely-leaded line into its own block (pitch ≫ glyph height) and `RenderPage` joins blocks with `\n\n`.

The document also has **three** spacing levels — wrap (~20pt) / paragraph (~26pt) / section heading (~32pt) — so a median-pitch threshold over-merges whole sections; the data showed the distinguishing signal is **justification** (a wrapped line reaches the right margin; a paragraph's last line is short).

## Fix
A per-page, justification-aware paragraph model (`PdfReadingOrder`):
- **`ContentRight`** = the typical full-line edge (robust median of the wider half of line right edges, *not* the max — one anomalously wide line must not push every normal full line below the bar); **wrap pitch** = median gap below a margin-reaching line.
- A line **continues** the paragraph only when the previous line reached the margin (it wrapped) *and* the gap is within the wrap pitch; a short (paragraph-ending) line or a blank-line/section gap **splits**. Falls back to the legacy glyph-height threshold when no model can be measured (non-prose / sparse page) — so direct `Render` callers and existing fixtures are unchanged.
- **Block re-fold**: consecutive same-column (horizontally overlapping) non-table blocks merge into one `Render` call, so a paragraph the segmenter cut into per-line blocks re-folds. A table cluster or a horizontally-disjoint block (a different column) flushes the run first — columns are never interleaved.
- **CJK wrap join**: a wrap between two CJK glyphs closes with **no** separator (the `ウ`/`ェブサイト` stray-space artifact); Latin boundaries keep their space.

## Out of scope / unchanged
Table reconstruction (#310 Phase B), multi-column band ordering (#310 Phase A), heading/emphasis detection (#403), and figure/caption binding (#301) are untouched. `TextExtractionResult` / the egress contract / Markdown-first invariant are unchanged. Ragged-right (non-justified) loose documents are best-effort (non-regressive) — noted in #407.

## Verification
- Validated end-to-end against the reported file (all three text pages): the quoted body sentence now renders as **one** paragraph with no stray CJK space; `第N条` headings, list items, and the 料金表 / key-value tables stay intact; multi-paragraph clauses split correctly.
- **85/85** `Dignite.Extract.Parse.Pdf.Tests` pass (79 existing + 6 new: full-width fold, short-last-line, blank-line split, CJK join, legacy fallback, end-to-end re-fold). Full solution builds with 0 errors.

> Diagnostics used to confirm the cause were temporary and are not part of the diff.

## Respond-and-record pass for gale #428 (the per-function cycle gap)

gale #428 (2026-06-23): with loom v1.1.16's inline+DCE merging the `gust_mix` export wrapper (loom#228), the gap dropped **2.81× → 2.63× LLVM** (fn-only 1.125 → 1.05 ticks/call, frame 24 B → 8 B) — **"synth is now the sole remaining factor."** The merged `gust_mix` lowered by **synth 0.12.0** still shows every issue: the materialized-bool clamps (`cmp; ite lt; movlt #1; movge #0; cmp #0; it ne; movne` ×2), register shifts that should be `lsl #8`, `movw+and` that should be `uxth`, and the 6-reg leaf prologue.

gale re-ranks the levers: **(4) cmp→select → IT-block predication = the highest single win** (VCR-SEL-004), then (3) immediate folding, then (1) wiring the now-CI-gated allocator (#441) to shrink the prologue.

## What this records (docs-only, zero codegen change)
- **VCR-SEL-004** gets the v0.12.0 re-confirmation: the 2.63× / synth-sole-factor measurement, the fresh disassembly, the re-ranked priority, and gale's `benches/gust/src/bin/gust_codegen_bench.rs` (≤1.3× fn-only) as the **agreed on-silicon kill-criterion** (it lives on gale's side).

The actual lowering fixes are **byte-changing codegen** — the next *dedicated gated release* (implement → re-freeze `0x00210A55`/`0x07FDF307`/divseam result-identical → differential → gale silicon via `gust_codegen_bench`), not an idle-tick cram. body:
## Summary

- Moves site away from using custom hex, and non-DRY component application. Doesn't make any significant change to design, but aligns it all to a common system for easier management in the future.
- migrate the landing page to shared design-system components and semantic Tailwind tokens
- add reusable CTA, empty-state, and page-header components while removing the old welcome component
- make custom Tailwind token colors opacity-aware so slash-opacity utilities compile correctly

## Root Cause Fixed

Tailwind custom colors were registered as raw `var(...)` values. That prevented utilities like `bg-accent-alt/10`, `border-accent-alt/30`, and `bg-danger/10` from being emitted in the production CSS.

This PR keeps full CSS variables such as `--accent-alt` for handwritten CSS, adds channel-only OKLCH variables such as `--accent-alt-oklch`, and points Tailwind at `oklch(var(--*-oklch) / <alpha-value>)`.

## Validation

author: mudcube
body:
## Summary

Updates every workspace dependency to its latest version, fixes the resulting compile/lint breakage, repairs the test suite, and fixes the (previously 100%-broken) CI workflows.

### Dependencies
- `cargo update` (transitive) + `cargo upgrade --incompatible` (direct, incl. majors). Notable: sysinfo 0.30→0.39, sha1/sha2 0.10→0.11, rand 0.9→0.10, reqwest 0.12→0.13, askama 0.12→0.16, git2 0.19→0.21, nix 0.29→0.31, duct 0.13→1.1, colored 2→3, dialoguer 0.11→0.12, tower-http 0.6→0.7, pbkdf2 0.12→0.13, axum-test 18→20.
- sysinfo 0.39 requires Rust ≥1.95 (CI uses `@stable`).

### Code changes from the updates
- sysinfo: `refresh_cpu()`→`refresh_cpu_all()`; `physical_core_count()` is now an associated fn.
- sha1/sha2: `finalize()` no longer impls `LowerHex` → explicit hex encoding.
- reqwest: `rustls-tls` feature renamed to `rustls`.
- axum-test: `TestServer::new()` is now infallible.
- Clippy 1.96: `collapsible_match`, `unnecessary_sort_by`, `manual_option_zip`.

### Bug fixes surfaced by the tests
- `vm registry status/add/remove/list` panicked ("Cannot drop a runtime in a context where blocking is not allowed") — the async handlers called the `reqwest::blocking`-based package-server client directly on the async runtime. Now routed through `spawn_blocking`.
- `vm create` only validated service ports, not `ports.mappings`; host-port conflicts now fail fast with a clear config error before any Docker work.

### Test & CI hardening
- Repointed stale `vm auth` tests to the renamed `vm secrets` command.
- Made the shared `TEST_MUTEX` poison-tolerant so one panic no longer cascades into unrelated tests.
- PyPI lifecycle test now skips gracefully when the local wheel toolchain can't build (e.g. Debian distutils `install_layout`).
- **CI/coverage workflows ran cargo from the repo root, not `rust/`, so every job failed with "could not find Cargo.toml" — CI had never actually run the tests.** Added `working-directory: rust`.

### Verification
`cargo check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, and `cargo test --workspace --features integration --no-fail-fast` all green (Docker-dependent integration tests skip when Docker is unavailable; they run on Docker-capable runners).

author: w0h1v
body:
Three independent polish items (separate commits), all off `main` and independent of the Pips rebuild (PR #4).

### 1. Derive the game count from the registry (`3b7d130`)
The hub still said "**Fifteen** ready to play" / "**/15**" after the suite grew to 20 — and the hardcoded `15` also fed real logic (the progress-bar denominator and the **Clean Sweep** trigger + its ✅ share grid), so those were wrong too. Added `GAME_COUNT` / `GAME_COUNT_WORD` to `lib/games` as the single source of truth and used them across hub, archive, Clean Sweep, onboarding, settings, how-to-play and layout metadata. Now reads "**Twenty** ready to play" / "1 / 20" and tracks the registry automatically. (Edge OG routes keep a literal to avoid bundling the registry.)

### 2. Accent-colour wash on the six monochrome game boards (`5c9195e`)
Sudoku, Tile Slide, Schulte, Mental Math Sprint, Mini Crossword and Focus Forge had near-black boards with accent tints so faint they read as grayscale. Each game's **ambient** surfaces (board wrapper, empty cells, faint keypad controls) now carry a restrained wash of **that game's own accent** plus light cell structure — while every **functional feedback** colour (solved-green, conflict-red, per-value palettes, the strong "selected" state) is untouched. Also removed the throbbing infinite `animate-pulse2` on Sudoku conflict cells (the static red ring is enough) and fixed Sudoku's same-value/peer highlights that were hardcoded cyan despite its violet accent. The 11 already-colourful games were left alone.

### 3. Completion-modal: portal + scroll, and a review control (`7b1094f`)
- The completion card overlapped the page footer — the `Modal` rendered inline (not portaled) with no max-height, so a tall card spilled onto the page behind it. It now **portals to `<body>`** and is its own scroll container, so it floats above page chrome and scrolls when taller than the viewport. (Every modal benefits.)
- After a win there was no obvious way to dismiss the card and review the solved board. Added an opt-in **✕ "Close — review the board"** button.

### Verification
`tsc` · `eslint` · web build (37 pages) green; 105 affected-game tests pass. Browser-verified: hub/onboarding show the correct 20-count, onboarding modal portals + closes cleanly.

author: cgoodfred
body:
## Summary

Adds `spark.sql.catalog.nhl.rest.metrics-reporter-impl: LoggingMetricsReporter` to all three silver SparkApplication manifests (`silver-games.yaml`, `silver-plays.yaml`, `silver-players.yaml`).

## Why

Iceberg's default `RESTMetricsReporter` POSTs table metrics back to the catalog after each operation. The OAuth2 token isn't reliably refreshed for those calls — observed on `silver-players` last night: snapshot committed cleanly, then the metrics POST failed with `NotAuthorizedException`, that exception propagated from Java through py4j into Python, killing the script before it could print the success line. Net effect: **data wrote and committed successfully, but the SparkApplication was marked FAILED**.

`LoggingMetricsReporter` writes the same metrics to driver stdout instead of POSTing them. Same observability, no flaky auth dependency, no surprise FAILED status when the data is actually fine.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: silver-tests passes (this PR changes only yaml so pytest is unaffected, but workflow should still run)
- [ ] Merge triggers no image rebuild (yaml-only change) — `Build silver image` should not fire
- [ ] Re-apply `silver-players` after merge: SparkApplication reaches `COMPLETED`, driver log shows the `silver-players: complete (rows=N)` line, and includes the per-table metrics output from `LoggingMetricsReporter`

## Follow-up

The underlying OAuth2 + RESTMetricsReporter interaction is worth understanding eventually (likely an Iceberg 1.10 bug or interaction with Lakekeeper's token validation). For a portfolio project this workaround is fine; in a production setting we'd want to root-cause it.

author: mtcmarkfranco
body:
When ``--rewrite`` is requested but the LLM editor cannot apply rewrites, the warning was printed mid-flow and scrolled past the final Review Summary panel — the user would see the report + comments and have no end-state signal that the rewrite path was skipped.

This change makes the final summary the source of truth for rewrite status.

**What you''ll see now**

When rewrite is unavailable:

```
┌──────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Pass             │ 8                                       │
│ Fail             │ 3                                       │
│ Rewrite (LLM)    │ unavailable (0/3 emitted)               │
└──────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┘

╭─ ⚠ Rewrite unavailable ─────────────────────────────────╮
│ LLM rewrite was not applied.                             │
│                                                          │
│ No LLM editor agent is configured. Set                   │
│ LAMBDA_RAG_FOUNDRY_EDIT_ENDPOINT,                        │
│ LAMBDA_RAG_FOUNDRY_EDIT_DEPLOYMENT, and                  │
│ LAMBDA_RAG_FOUNDRY_EDIT_API_KEY (or LambdaRag:Foundry:   │
│ Edit:* config keys) to enable the ComplianceEditor.      │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

**Reason surfaced for every failure mode**

| Cause | Reason in callout |
|-------|------------------|
| No Foundry Edit endpoint / key (NoopClauseRewriter) | `No LLM editor agent is configured…` + env-var hint |
| ``--rewrite`` with non-.docx source | `--rewrite skipped: markup requires a .docx source (got ''.pdf'').` |
| ``--rewrite`` with ``--mode report`` | `--rewrite has no effect with --mode report (markup not emitted)…` |
| Every per-rule LLM call threw | `LLM editor returned no rewrites — every attempt failed with HttpRequestException (3 of 3)…` |

When rewrite *succeeds*, the summary shows ``Rewrite (LLM) │ 3 / 3 clause rewrite(s) emitted`` and the panel is omitted.

**Also**

- ``ex.Message`` is now captured in the existing per-rule skip table (was just ``LLM error: TypeName``).

Build: clean. No existing CLI tests covered the rewrite branch; behaviour-only change to console output.

author: bradflaugher
body:
## Summary
`cmd/cutlass` was an empty `func main() {}` stub. This implements it as fleet's **local one-shot harness**: it runs a single task YAML to completion in an **isolated workspace** through the **same governed scheduled runtime** the production scheduler uses — no orchestrator round-trip, no HTTP server, no scheduler ticker, no database. Closes #45.

## One core, not a fork
To avoid a second, weaker execution path (AGENTS.md: *"governance is one core"*), the scheduled driver is **extracted** into a shared package both callers drive, rather than duplicated:

- **`internal/scheduledrun`** (new) — the `Runner` (model resolve → shared sandbox warm pool → `agent.NewAgent` → `agentcore.Run`, `Mode=Scheduled`) plus per-task MCP credential-account isolation (`bindTaskMCP`), prompt assembly, and log conversion. Moved **verbatim** from cmd/fleet's package-`main` `scheduledRunner` (its dead `storage` field dropped — `runner.TaskRunner` only needs `Run`). `BuildMCPSpecs` moves here too so cmd/fleet and cutlass resolve identical MCP specs. The `bindTaskMCP` credential-isolation tests move with it.
- **cmd/fleet** — `newScheduledRunner(...)` → `scheduledrun.New(Options{...})`; the two `buildMCPSpecs` sites (`main.go`, `acp.go`) → `scheduledrun.BuildMCPSpecs`. Pure code-movement; the scheduled + cmd/fleet suites stay green. (Also dropped one now-unused `//nolint` the move made dead.)
- **cmd/cutlass** — parses a task YAML (a thin mirror of the scheduled-task create shape), mints a **fresh per-run workspace** (isolated from the server's shared `workspace/`), builds the Manager exactly as the Mega Box does, runs the task via `scheduledrun`, and writes the redacted session log as JSON.

## Testing (always-on, provider-free, DB-free)
`cmd/cutlass/main_test.go` drives the real harness against the **fake-LLM seam** (`OPENROUTER_BASE_URL`) with `FLEET_MOCK_MODE=1` (host sandbox — no podman):
- a full task **runs to completion** (satisfying the scheduled self-audit finish enforcement via a scripted `confirm_audit`) and writes a parseable `models.LogSession`;
- two runs get **distinct isolated workspaces**;
- a YAML-schema unit test.

The bindTaskMCP credential-isolation tests (per-account `<VAR>_<ACCOUNT>` overlay, refusal without creds, per-run client reaping) ride along in `internal/scheduledrun`. `make build`, `golangci-lint`, and the `cmd/cutlass` + `internal/scheduledrun` + `cmd/fleet` + `internal/runner` + `internal/agent` suites are green.

## Operator tooling + honest docs
- `scripts/run_workflow_live.sh` — builds the sandbox image, isolates a workspace, tails the log, runs cutlass.
- `docs/examples/cutlass-task.yaml` — the documented task schema.
- README gains a "Running one task locally (cutlass)" note; `.gitignore` gains `.fleet-runs/` + the cutlass binary.

## Invariants
Sandbox mandatory (the harness takes from the SAME warm pool interactive turns use); credentials host-side (per-task MCP binding unchanged, moved verbatim); **one governed core** (`agentcore.Run` via `agent.Execute` — the extraction makes this literal); honest docs.

author: notatallshaw
body:
Closes #207.

nab's configuration was ad-hoc: a single source (`[tool.nab]` in `pyproject.toml`), no `nab.toml`, no `NAB_*` scheme, and one global CLI flag. As the option count grows this drifts, and for a resolver a disagreement over where an option comes from is a correctness bug, not a cosmetic one. This gives every option one definition and one precedence policy.

Every option is one row in a registry (`nab_python.config_sources`) naming its scope, type, default, env var, and CLI flag. The loader, env reader, merge, category gate, and `nab config` are all derived from that registry, and the existing `[tool.nab]` parser now sources its values from it, so each option has a single parse path.

Scope splits options into two categories:

- PROJECT options change the resolved set, so they come only from `pyproject.toml` `[tool.nab]` or a project-directory `nab.toml`, plus an optional `--project-<key>` CLI override.
- USER options (`offline`, `cache-dir`, `http-backend`, `max-concurrency`) describe how a run executes on this machine, so they come from a system, user, or project `nab.toml`, a `NAB_*` env var, or a plain CLI flag. They are rejected in `[tool.nab]`.

Layers merge low to high: defaults, system `nab.toml`, user `nab.toml`, the two project files (same rank), `NAB_*`, then the CLI. Conflicting values for one key across the two project files are an error, identical values are fine, and a source that sets an option outside its scope is a named error rather than a silent drop. Each effective value carries its source.

### Included

- The registry and the discover/merge/provenance engine, with every `[tool.nab]` option sourced through it, so a project-directory `nab.toml` configures the resolve the same way `pyproject.toml` does.
- `NAB_*` reading for the USER options; an unknown or project-scope `NAB_*` name is rejected.
- `--project-<key>` overrides for the scalar and array PROJECT options (`resolution`, `mode`, `requires-python`, `uploaded-prior-to`, `dist-policy`, `build-policy`, and the repeatable `--project-constraint` / `--project-default-group`). A CLI project override prints a reproducibility notice and is recorded in the lockfile, since the lock no longer derives from the committed files alone. `--resolution` is renamed `--project-resolution`.
- A read-only `nab config` subcommand: `list`, `get <key>`, and `explain <key>` (with `--include-rejected`).
- `nab lock --locked` re-resolves and verifies the committed `pylock.toml` is current, writing nothing and failing if it would change.
- `--upgrade` now prints a notice naming the cutoff it drops when it re-anchors the resolve window.

### Deferred to a follow-up

Writing config (`nab config set` / `unset` / `edit`). The registry already exposes what a writer needs (value validation, the category gate, scope-to-file resolution), so it layers on cleanly later.

author: bmarshall511
body:
## The recurring problem (finally root-caused)

Every release needed **2 extra PRs** (advance \`bootstrap-sha\` + close a spurious \"release X.Y.(Z+1)\" PR). The spurious PRs always re-proposed the **latest release's** commit (never 0.1.0), so it was **not** the ancient \`Release-As\` footer.

**Real cause:** the config had \`draft: true\`, and **a draft GitHub release has no git tag until it's published**. So when release-please re-ran on the release-PR merge, the new tag didn't exist yet → it saw the prior tag as latest → re-proposed the just-released commit. Advancing \`bootstrap-sha\` only masked it.

## Permanent fix
- **\`draft: false\`** — release-please publishes immediately, so the tag exists when it re-checks → no phantom PR.
- **Remove \`bootstrap-sha\`** — with tag-detection working, release-please never scans back past the latest tag, so the \`36c3dff\` \`Release-As: 0.1.0\` footer (the only reason the floor existed) is unreachable.
- **electron-builder \`publish.releaseType: release\`** — upload the \`.dmg\` to the already-published release.

**Trade-off:** a release is visible for the ~3 min the macOS build runs before its \`.dmg\` attaches (draft-until-asset is gone — worth it to end the loop).

Synced spec 19 (amendment) + \`release.yml\` comments. No app code.

body:
> **Stacked on #1060** — base branch is `tho/activity-ingress-ownership`, **not** `main`. Review #1060 first.

## What this does

Makes each agent's **live `kind:0` NIP-OA `auth` tag the single source of truth** for agent-activity ownership, end-to-end — so the relay's observer-frame delivery and desktop's visibility gate agree on the same proof. This replaces the custom relay ownership endpoint #1060 introduces.

This is the direction Max & Eva converged on in the agent-observability room: the relay was gating *delivery* on the DB column `agent_owner_pubkey` (written from the NIP-42 AUTH event), while a UI gating on `kind:0` could disagree with what the relay actually ships. This PR closes that gap.

## The four moves

1. **Shared strict extraction** — `buzz-sdk::nip_oa` gets exactly-one-`auth`-tag extraction (mirrors the relay's existing `extract_single_auth_tag_json`), so relay + desktop share one helper. +5 unit tests.
2. **`resolveAgentOwnership` → thin wrapper** over the existing `resolveOaOwner` (live `kind:0` path). Adapter shape unchanged — `useCanViewAgentActivity` and `useChannelAgentSessions` both keep working.
3. **Delete the custom ownership endpoint** — `GET /api/agents/:pubkey/ownership`, its Tauri command + registration, and the e2e mock.
4. **Align the relay's observer-frame delivery gate** to verify the same live `kind:0` proof. Authority order: session NIP-OA fast-path → live `kind:0` proof → DB cache fallback. A **`kind:0` owner mismatch DENIES** (no DB fallthrough), so the DB can never contradict `kind:0`. `agent_owner_pubkey` stays as a cache/backfill fallback so **BYO/CLI agents that AUTH without publishing a profile keep observer delivery**. +3 DB-backed tests.

## Policy note (open for tho)

Shipped with the **BYO fallback kept** — AUTH-only/CLI agents retain observer delivery without publishing a `kind:0`. If we'd rather *require* every owned agent publish a `kind:0` (dropping the fallback for tidier authority), that's a one-line tightening of step 4.

- Relay: `cargo build` clean + 332 tests pass (the 3 new DB-backed tests ran against live Postgres).
- SDK: 179 tests pass.
- Desktop: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; no dangling refs to the deleted endpoint/command.

Desktop tauri `cargo build` could not run locally (`cmake` missing for the `audiopus` native dep — environment limitation, unrelated to these changes). **Please confirm the tauri crate builds in CI.**

author: ajsutton
body:
## Why

Follow-on to #1173 (instrument pricing unification, Sub-project A). `StockPriceService` and `CryptoPriceService` independently implemented the **same** daily-price-series orchestration — cap-to-yesterday → in-memory check → hydrate-from-SQL → bounded windowed network fetch → carry-forward → write-back — duplicated almost line-for-line (~85% identical), already sharing `SortedDateSeries` / `ContiguousFetchPlanner` / `cappedToYesterday`. This extracts that duplication into one shared engine.

## What

- **`PriceSeriesOrchestrating`** — an `Actor`-constrained protocol whose **default methods** hold the shared orchestration, conformed by both service actors. The defaults mutate `self.caches[key]` **per key** (never a whole-dict snapshot), preserving each actor's existing re-entrant cache semantics exactly — a concurrent two-instrument regression test guards the race the rejected snapshot design would have caused.
- The three genuine differences stay behind plugs and per-service: the provider fetch (single Yahoo client vs. the 4-provider CoinGecko→CryptoCompare→Binance→DefiLlama fallback chain + coalescing), the denomination (stock listing currency vs. crypto USD), and the optional first-trade floor (crypto only, defaulted no-op for stock).
- **Both cache tables kept** (`stock_price`/`crypto_price` + meta) — no schema migration. `ExchangeRateService` untouched (it's a pairwise multi-quote bridge, not a per-instrument series). Public APIs unchanged, so Sub-project A's `PriceSource` resolvers keep working with no edits.
- Net **−231 lines** of production code (352 deleted, 121 added) once the duplicated orchestration is removed; `StockPriceService+FetchRange.swift` deleted entirely.

## Incidental fix

The shared `generateDateSeries` standardises on `Calendar.utc`. `StockPriceService` previously stepped its date series with a **host-local** `Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)` — a latent timezoneless-date bug (`guides/DATE_TIME_GUIDE.md`); the engine fixes it. Result-neutral (the stock harness already pins UTC); a new multi-zone invariance test pins the day-token producer.

## Behaviour-neutral

The comprehensive existing stock/crypto price-service suites (coalescing, fallback, boundary, cap, persistence, attribution, warming, stablecoin, prelisting, metadata, price-lookup) pass with **unchanged expectations** — they are the proof. Full suite green on iOS + macOS.

## Review

Whole-branch review (ready-to-merge) + `datetime-review` + `concurrency-review` + `code-review` — 0 Critical, 0 Important after fixes. All in-scope findings applied (dropped a dead plug + an unmotivated `Equatable`, DRY'd the warming config, defaulted the first-trade plugs, hardened the tests). Three pre-existing findings in untouched files (`PriceCacheCap`/`ContiguousFetchPlanner` UTC-seam, a coalescing-cancel doc) are tracked for a separate follow-up PR.

author: aneeshv12
body:
## Issue Link / Problem Description
- Fixes #2783

`LangchainEmbeddingsWrapper` logs an `EmbeddingUsageEvent` for usage telemetry whose `model` field is typed `Optional[str]`, via `getattr(self.embeddings, "model", None)`. When the wrapped embeddings store a non-string object on `.model` (e.g. `langchain_community`'s `FastEmbedEmbeddings`, which keeps the loaded `TextEmbedding` object there), constructing the event raises a Pydantic `ValidationError`. Although `track()` is decorated `@silent` so telemetry can never break user code, the event is built as the *argument* to `track()`, so the error is raised before `@silent` can catch it. `RAGAS_DO_NOT_TRACK=true` does not help either, since the opt-out check runs inside `track()` after the argument is already constructed.

Net effect: in a full `evaluate()`, `answer_relevancy` (which needs embeddings) silently returns `NaN` while LLM-only metrics score normally.

## Changes Made
- Add `_extract_string_model_name()` in `src/ragas/embeddings/base.py`: returns a real `str` model name, falling back `.model` -> `.model_name` -> `None`, so the usage event is always valid.
- Use it at the four telemetry call sites in `LangchainEmbeddingsWrapper` (`embed_query`, `embed_documents`, `aembed_query`, `aembed_documents`) in place of `getattr(self.embeddings, "model", None)`.
- This restores the best-effort behavior that the `@silent` decorator on `track()` already intends: telemetry can no longer break an embedding call.

## Testing
### How to Test
- [x] Automated tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing steps:
  1. `from langchain_community.embeddings.fastembed import FastEmbedEmbeddings`
  2. `from ragas.embeddings import LangchainEmbeddingsWrapper`
  3. `LangchainEmbeddingsWrapper(FastEmbedEmbeddings()).embed_query("hello")` — raises `ValidationError` before this change, returns a vector after.

Added `test_embedding_usage_telemetry_tolerates_nonstring_model` in `tests/unit/test_analytics.py`: it wraps an embeddings stub whose `.model` is a non-string object and asserts `embed_query` / `embed_documents` succeed. The test fails on `main` (ValidationError) and passes with this fix.

Verification:
- `ruff format` / `ruff check`: clean
- `pyright src/ragas/embeddings/base.py`: 0 errors
- `pytest tests/unit/test_analytics.py tests/unit/test_embeddings.py`: passing

## References
- Related issues: #2783 (this bug). Unrelated but worth noting: a fresh install currently fails `import ragas` on the removed `langchain_community...vertexai` path under langchain 1.x (#2741 / #2745 / #2753), so upstream CI may be red until that lands. This change is independent of it.
- Documentation: n/a
- External references: n/a

## Screenshots/Examples (if applicable)
Before (any embeddings whose `.model` is a non-string object, e.g. fastembed):
```
ValidationError: 1 validation error for EmbeddingUsageEvent
model
  Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=<...TextEmbedding object...>, input_type=TextEmbedding]
```
After: the embed call returns its vector and `answer_relevancy` scores normally.

body:
## Summary

Adds two tap-to-view "show the working" popovers for the portfolio chart's
**Actual** and **Dividends** values (issue #426, part of milestone #420),
mirroring the existing "Portfolio Target working" popover. A small figures line
under the "Performance Over Time" chart now shows `Actual: X% · Dividends: Y%`,
and each value is a clickable popover that lists the per-stock working and the
equal-weighted total — so every number is visible and verifiable.

Both popovers are built from the **shared** return helpers in
`docs/projection.js`, so a popover can never disagree with the plotted /
summarised value. Closes #426.

- **Dividends popover** — per included stock: buy price, 90-day dividends ($)
  and yield % (dividends ÷ buy price), then the equal-weighted portfolio
  dividend total. This makes the ABC/XYZ ratio legible (a $1 stock paying 1c =
  1.0% yield is 4× a $20 stock paying 5c = 0.25%).
- **Actual popover** — per included stock: price return %, dividend return %,
  total return %, then the equal-weighted average = the Actual %.

### New shared helpers (single source of truth)

- `calculateReturnBreakdown(buyPrice, currentPrice, totalDividends)` — splits a
  stock's actual total return into its price and dividend components;
  `totalReturn` equals `calculatePerformanceReturn()` exactly.
- `calculateIncludedPortfolioDividendReturn(stocks)` — equal-weighted mean of
  included stocks' dividend yields, mirroring
  `calculateIncludedPortfolioPerformance()`.

The Actual figure is the equal-weighted mean of each included stock's total
return (`calculateIncludedPortfolioPerformance`), the same canonical figure the
totals-row Gain/Loss reports — so the popover total, the displayed figure and
the totals row all agree exactly.

> **Note on the chart's latest dot:** the canonical Actual figure is averaged
> over *all* included stocks. The chart's final plotted dot is averaged over
> only the stocks that have a market point on the single most-recent trading
> date, so when a stock's data is a day stale the raw final dot can differ from
> the canonical figure by a fraction of a percent (visually indistinguishable on
> the chart). The figure is anchored to the robust all-included-stocks average
> rather than the thin final sample; the underlying chart-sampling behaviour is
> pre-existing and out of scope for this issue.

### Data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    SD[scoreData + marketData] --> R[getPortfolioReturnRows]
    R --> RB[calculateReturnBreakdown per stock]
    R --> AP[calculateIncludedPortfolioPerformance]
    R --> DP[calculateIncludedPortfolioDividendReturn]
    AP --> FIG[Actual / Dividends figures under chart]
    DP --> FIG
    RB --> POP[getWorking popover content]
    AP --> POP
    DP --> POP
    FIG --> POP
```

## Evidence

Actual popover — per-stock price/dividend/total returns, equal-weighted Actual:

![Actual working popover](https://github.com/stSoftwareAU/GRQ-validation/raw/55d1dfc7a6228410ea01c1dd6a25514ac86ab7cb/docs/evidence/issue-426-actual-popover.png)

Dividends popover — per-stock buy price/dividends/yield, equal-weighted total:

![Dividends working popover](https://github.com/stSoftwareAU/GRQ-validation/raw/55d1dfc7a6228410ea01c1dd6a25514ac86ab7cb/docs/evidence/issue-426-dividends-popover.png)

Figures line beneath the chart (`Actual: 4.0% · Dividends: 0.23%`):

![Chart figures line](https://github.com/stSoftwareAU/GRQ-validation/raw/55d1dfc7a6228410ea01c1dd6a25514ac86ab7cb/docs/evidence/issue-426-chart-figures.png)

Screenshots captured against the live dashboard (default score 2026-03-25). The
Actual popover total (`4.0%`) reconciles with the displayed Actual figure and
the totals-row Gain/Loss; the Dividends popover total (`0.23%`) reconciles with
the displayed Dividends figure.

## Test Plan

- Added `tests/show_working_dividends_actual_test.ts` — exercises the new shared
  helpers via the real `docs/projection.js`:
  - `calculateReturnBreakdown` splits price vs dividend return; `totalReturn`
    equals `calculatePerformanceReturn`; ABC/XYZ dividend yields differ 4×;
    missing dividends default to 0; non-positive buy price → null.
  - `calculateIncludedPortfolioDividendReturn` equal-weights included yields,
    drops excluded stocks, and returns null for empty/all-excluded/invalid input.
  - Reconciliation: equal-weighted price return + equal-weighted dividend return
    equals the equal-weighted Actual figure.
- `deno test --allow-read tests/*.ts` — 668 passed, 0 failed.

- `cargo check --all-targets` — clean (Rust untouched; frontend-only change).

author: kevinkreiser
body:
## Summary

**What is the goal of this PR?**

Add touchscreen support for the **KONKR Pocket FIT** (Qualcomm SM8650). The device ships a **ChipOne ICNL9922C** TDDI touch controller that has no support under ROCKNIX today — display and inputs work, but the touchscreen does nothing. This PR makes it functional.

It adds three things:
* **`projects/ROCKNIX/packages/linux-drivers/chipone_tddi/package.mk`** — a new `linux-drivers` package that fetches and builds the ICNL9922C driver as an out-of-tree module (same pattern as `rocknix-joypad`).
* **`projects/ROCKNIX/devices/SM8650/options`** — enables it via `ADDITIONAL_DRIVERS="chipone_tddi"`.
* **`sm8650-konkr-pf.dts`** — the touchscreen node: controller on `&i2c4` (`i2c@a90000`) @ `0x48`, IRQ on TLMM gpio162, reset on TLMM gpio161, 1080×1920, reusing the existing `ts_irq_default` / `ts_reset_default` pin states.

The driver itself lives in its own repo (pinned by commit, like `rocknix-joypad`): 
**https://github.com/kevinkreiser/chipone_tddi**. It is a port of ChipOne's `cts_*` vendor driver from `MotorolaMobilityLLC/motorola-kernel-modules` (`drivers/input/touchscreen/chipone_tddi_mmi_v2`), which targets a downstream Android kernel; the fork makes it build/load as an out-of-tree module on the mainline 7.0.x kernel (API-drift fixes, I²C/ICNL9922C build config, charger/earjack disabled). Original copyright and `SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0` headers are retained.

## Testing

**How was this tested?**

Verified on real **KONKR Pocket FIT** hardware (nightly `20260618`, kernel 7.0.11):
* The driver was cross-compiled against the SM8650 7.0.11 kernel/config (all imported symbols confirmed exported by the kernel).
* Loaded on-device with the DT node applied via a runtime devicetree overlay (so no image reflash was needed for iteration).
* Confirmed the touchscreen works in EmulationStation and in NDS emulators, with correct axis orientation.

> Note: this was validated by loading the module + overlay at runtime, **not** yet via a full `make docker-SM8650` image build.
The `package.mk` follows the existing `rocknix-joypad` pattern, so a CI/full-image build should confirm it cleanly.

**Test results:**

CTS-Core Probe device
CTS-Core Firmware id: 0x9965
CTS-Sysfs Create device for ICNL9922C
CTS-Plat Request IRQ
input: chipone-tddi as .../a90000.i2c/i2c-2/2-0048/input/input12
Touches report on `ABS_MT_POSITION_X/Y` and drive the UI correctly.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdc7d049-3a9f-4587-b2cb-515a2bd962b7

## Additional Context

* The panel is mounted rotated 90°, so the X axis is inverted to match the display. This is currently a **driver build flag** (`CFG_CTS_WRAP_X` in the driver repo's Kbuild). Happy to instead express it via a DT `touchscreen-inverted-x` property if that's preferred.
* The upstream vendor driver carries debug/factory interfaces (`cts_sysfs` / `cts_oem` / `cts_test` / `cts_tool`) and SPI-flash code that aren't strictly needed here. I left them intact because they're entangled with the core comms path (`cts_tcs` calls into `cts_test`); they can be trimmed in a follow-up if desired.
* **Provenance/licensing:** out-of-tree GPL-2.0 module derived from Motorola/ChipOne GPL-2.0 source, fetched from a pinned commit — consistent with how `rocknix-joypad` and the RTL Wi-Fi drivers are handled.

---

### AI Usage

**Did you use AI tools to help write this code?**

YES, I've marked my commits as co-authored by claude opus 4.8. While I am a very experienced c++ (and a decent c) dev, I've never worked with the kernel modules directly before so it was super helpful in getting this up and working!

## What

`gog youtube videos list` now supports explicit control over the YouTube
`videos.list` parts:

- omitted `--parts` preserves the historical
  `snippet,contentDetails,statistics` request and output shape;
- `--parts all` requests every part documented as readable for arbitrary
  videos;
- an explicit comma-separated list is passed through unchanged, including
  owner-only parts for authenticated requests against the caller's own uploads;
- `all` cannot be mixed with explicit part names.

## Why

Metadata archiving and analysis sometimes need the full provider response, but
changing the default would broaden existing script output. The opt-in selector
adds the capability without a compatibility break.

The `all` set follows the current
[official `videos.list` contract](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/videos/list):
`contentDetails,id,liveStreamingDetails,localizations,paidProductPlacementDetails,player,recordingDetails,snippet,statistics,status,topicDetails`.
It excludes the owner-only `fileDetails`, `processingDetails`, and `suggestions`
parts. The API documents a fixed one-unit quota cost for the method.

## Proof

Exact candidate: `ee1a3e92400167f17fab748c3670b2c9824e61cb`.

- `go test ./internal/cmd -run 'TestYouTubeVideosList' -count=1`

author: martsokha
body:
Keyword-boost **context enhancement now works for image and audio**, not just text and tabular.

## The problem

The bare pattern recognizer already ran on image/audio (they're `TextRecognizable`, reading OCR `Layout` / STT `Transcription` text). But context enhancement was a *post-lift* `Recognizer` wrapper (`ContextEnhanced`) that recovered each entity's stream byte range via `M::span` — impossible for image/audio:
- their native location is a bbox / time span (no byte range), and
- the stream→location projection is **lossy and non-invertible** (`Layout::resolve` unions word boxes; no reverse map exists).

So the stream range, destroyed at lift, couldn't be recovered after the fact without storing an engine-specific OCR/STT offset on the serialized entity (rejected) or re-running the whole match scan (redundant).

## The fix: enhance *before* lift

- **`StreamRecognizer<M>`** (new, narrow trait): `find(text, ctx) -> Vec<EntityDraft>`. A recognizer that works over the recognized-text stream. Opt-in, **not** a replacement for `Recognizer<M>` — LLM (a native VLM recognizer via `LlmModality::lift`, no stream) is untouched.
- **`EntityDraft`** (new, non-generic): a stream-positioned finding with an **ephemeral** `stream_range` that never reaches the serialized `Entity`.
- **`Enhanced<R>`** (new adapter): wraps a `StreamRecognizer` as a `Recognizer<M>`, runs the optional `Enhancer` over the drafts, then `lift`s each to a located entity via `M::locate`. The composable enhancement seam (replaces the wrapper).
- **`Enhancer`** reworked to operate on `&mut [EntityDraft]` (no `M::span`) — now modality-free.

## Cleanups this enabled

- Delete **`TextSpanned`** (its sole purpose was the `M::span` range-recovery hack) and the `ContextEnhanced` wrapper.
- Narrow **`TextRecognizable::as_text`/`locate`** from `&RecognizerContext<M>` to `&Artifacts` — every impl only used the artifacts.
- Rename `text_backed.rs` → `text_recognizable.rs` (now holds only that trait); move `impl TextRecognizable for Text` into `text/mod.rs`, matching the other modalities.
- Move the `tracing` dep from `elide-pattern` (now unused there) to `elide-context`, where `lift` warns on an unplaceable match.

**Net −225 lines.**

## Proof

New `context_multimodal` test: `Enhanced<PatternRecognizer>` finds an SSN in OCR/STT text, the nearby "ssn" keyword boosts it above baseline, and the entity carries the **native location** (image bbox at x=45, audio time span at 400ms) — not a byte offset.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace --all-features` — 599 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="--cfg docsrs -D warnings" cargo +nightly doc` — clean
- `cargo machete` — `tracing` correctly relocated; only pre-existing false positives remain

author: lost-conn
body:
## Problem

The rsx `for`-loop capture scanner (`collect_capture_idents` in `crates/rinch-macros/src/dom_codegen/control_flow.rs`) walks a `for` iterator expression and emits `let name = name.clone();` shadow bindings for every identifier that *looks* like an outer local (lowercase, single-segment path). To avoid cloning names that aren't outer locals, the #32 fix taught it to skip identifiers bound by **closure params** and **`let` statements** — but it never learned about names bound by **`if let`**, **`while let`**, or **`match` arm** patterns.

So this real-world rsx (a `for` iterating a `.filter(...)` whose closure uses `if let`):

```rust
for fb in feedback.into_iter().filter(|f| {
    if let Pane::Editor(ref cid) = active.get() {
        f.id == *cid
    } else {
        false
    }
}) { ... }
```

made the scanner treat `cid` (bound by `if let`, used only in the then-branch) as an outer capture and emit `let cid = cid.clone();` for a binding that doesn't exist:

```
error[E0425]: cannot find value `cid` in this scope
```

Only `for` iterators hit this — rsx `if` blocks render via a separate re-destructure path (`generate_if_block`), so the identical `if let` inside an rsx `if` compiled fine. That asymmetry is what made it surprising.

## Fix

Give `if let` / `while let` / `match` the same scope-frame treatment that closures and `let` already get:

- **`visit_expr_if`** / **`visit_expr_while`** push a `locals` frame, then call a new **`scan_cond`** helper on the condition. `scan_cond` visits each scrutinee expression in the *outer* scope (so the scrutinee's own identifiers are still captured) and adds the names bound by each pattern to the frame, so the branch body skips them. The `else` branch is visited *outside* the frame (it can't see the bindings).
- **`scan_cond`** also recurses through `&&` let-chains, so a later link correctly sees an earlier binding — `if let Some(x) = a && x > 0` treats `x` as bound, `a` as a capture.
- **`visit_arm`** scopes each `match` arm's pattern to that arm's guard and body; the scrutinee is still visited by the default `visit_expr_match` in the outer scope.

This mirrors the existing `visit_expr_closure` / `visit_local` handling — it's the `if let` analogue of the #32 fix.

## Tests

Added unit tests in the existing `mod tests`:
- `if_let_binding_is_not_a_capture` (the repro)
- `if_let_else_branch_does_not_see_binding`
- `match_arm_binding_is_not_a_capture`
- `while_let_binding_is_not_a_capture`
- `let_chain_later_link_sees_earlier_binding`

> Note: I couldn't run `cargo test -p rinch-macros` locally — its dev-dependency on the full `rinch` crate pulls in desktop GPU/windowing deps that need system `fontconfig`, which isn't available in my headless environment (the crate's Cargo.toml already documents this caveat). `cargo build -p rinch-macros` passes. I validated the fix **end-to-end** instead: a downstream app with the exact repro above fails to compile before this change and compiles cleanly after (via the local path dependency). Please confirm the new unit tests pass in CI.

author: lxfind
body:
## Description

Adds a generic framework for **waitable system objects** — system objects (beyond a transaction's declared inputs) that execution may read at a specific version and must wait for if the local node hasn't caught up.

- `AssignedVersions` now carries a generic `system_object_versions: BTreeMap<ObjectID, SequenceNumber>` (replacing the dedicated `accumulator_version` field, read via an `accumulator_version()` accessor), threaded from consensus through the execution layer into `TemporaryStore`.
- `RuntimeObjectResolver::is_system_object_available` checks whether a required system object has reached its version. On `TemporaryStore` it errors if the object has no assigned version, and when the object hasn't caught up it records `ExecutionRetryError::SystemObjectUnavailable { object_id }` (out-of-band, since the signal must cross the Move VM boundary) and returns `false`.
- The authority propagates that retry: on `SystemObjectUnavailable` it produces no effects, waits via the new `ObjectCacheRead::notify_read_system_object_at_version` cache primitive for the object to reach the required version, then re-enqueues the transaction.

Inert until a consumer calls the availability check (object funds, 5/5).

## Stack

1/5 #27003 — `ExecutionRetryError` plumbing from execution to authority
2/5 #27019 — rename `ChildObjectResolver` → `RuntimeObjectResolver`
3/5 #27036 — waitable system object framework
4/5 #27037 — record read system objects in effects
5/5 #27038 — check object funds withdraw sufficiency in the Move VM

## Test plan

Framework infrastructure with no consumer in this PR, so no behavior change: validated by the existing `shared_object_version_manager` assignment tests (version map round-trips) and, end to end, by the object-balance stress test in 5/5, which exercises the availability check, the `SystemObjectUnavailable` retry, the cache-notify wait, and re-enqueue.

author: joshrotenberg
body:
Closes #48.

## Problem

`option/2` and `argument/2` ran `Macro.escape/1` over the opts keyword list before stashing it in a module attribute. For a literal value the escaped AST equals the value, so it round-trips. For a non-literal such as the common `choices: ~w(low medium high)`, `Macro.escape` preserves the `{:sigil_w, ...}` call node verbatim, so at runtime the opt held that AST tuple rather than `["low", "medium", "high"]`.

`mycli --help` then crashed:

```
** (Protocol.UndefinedError) protocol Enumerable not implemented for Tuple
    {:sigil_w, [...], [...]}
    lib/cheer/help.ex:251: Cheer.Help.format_option/2
```

## Fix

Emit `unquote(clean_opts)` instead of `unquote(Macro.escape(clean_opts))` so each opt value is evaluated at compile time in the module body. This is exactly what the `group/3` macro already does with its opts. `trailing_var_arg/2` had the same pattern and gets the same fix.

`~w(...)`, module constants, and any other constant expression now resolve to their value instead of being frozen as AST.

## Tests

Added a `non-literal opt values` describe block:
- `~w(...)` opt values evaluate (asserted against `__cheer_meta__`) for both an option and an argument
- `~w(...)` choices render in `--help` without crashing
- `~w(...)` choices are enforced at validation time

Full suite: 203 passing (was 200).

author: eugeneepshteyn
body:
The logical abbreviations .T. and .F. (for .TRUE. and .FALSE.) are a nonstandard extension that flang accepts only under -flogical-abbreviations, which is disabled by default because these spellings -- and the operator forms .N./.A./.O./.X. -- are also valid defined-operator names.

Of these, only the literals .T. and .F. cause a parse failure, since the operator forms parse as defined operators and instead fail later in semantics ("No operator .A. defined").

Consider the following code: `logical :: flag = .F.`

When -flogical-abbreviations is off, such code may cause a confusing cascade of errors that dosn't give the user a clue about the option that would accept it. The new implementation keeps the existing diagnostics and additionally emits a note pointing at the abbreviation:

  This nonstandard logical abbreviation requires the '-flogical-abbreviations' option

Assisted-by: AI

author: adhithyan15
body:
## W-20 — Advanced pattern constructs (MA04 §22)

Wolfram's advanced pattern constructs, built on W-18's matcher, W-19's `replace_all_once`, and the existing `cas-pattern-matching` crate. Entirely contained in `wolfram-runtime`. Version bumped to **0.16.0**.

### What shipped

- **`Alternatives[a, b, …]`** (surface `a | b | c`) — matches the subject against each alternative in order; first match wins, with its bindings. Empty `Alternatives[]` matches nothing; branches nest (`_Integer | _String`). Bounded: each branch tried once, left to right — no cross-branch combinatorial expansion.
- **`Condition[patt, test]`** (surface `patt /; test`) — matches `patt`, substitutes the captured named bindings into `test` (bare-symbol substitution), and accepts only if `test` evaluates to `True`. The test runs through a fresh, stateless `WolframBackend`-backed VM so it can neither see nor mutate session state.
- **`PatternTest[patt, fn]`** (surface `patt ? fn`) — matches `patt`, then accepts only if `fn[subject]` evaluates to `True` (the subject, not a binding). e.g. `MatchQ[4, PatternTest[Blank[], EvenQ]]` → `True`.
- **`ReplaceRepeated[expr, rules]`** (surface `expr //. rules`) — applies `ReplaceAll` repeatedly to a fixed point, evaluating between passes, until convergence or the iteration cap `REPLACE_REPEATED_MAX_ITERATIONS` (`2^16`).

### Grammar change?

**None.** All four constructs ship as ordinary head applications (`Alternatives[…]`, `Condition[…]`, …), which the parser already accepts as `NAME[args]`. The surface operator sugar (`|`, `/;`, `?`, `//.`) requires new lexer tokens + parser precedence + a regenerated grammar, so it is deferred to W-21.

### Security hardening

A dedicated `fix(security)` commit bounds two unbounded-growth vectors, with tests asserting each:

- **ReplaceRepeated tree-growth + iteration bound.** A self-recursive rule (`x -> f[x]`) never converges, so the equality check never fires; the iteration counter is what terminates the loop — at the cap it returns the last form with no hang, no panic, and no unbounded memory. A branching rule is additionally bounded by a tree-growth cap to prevent OOM. Each pass is still depth-guarded by `REPLACE_MAX_DEPTH`, so both inner (tree depth) and outer (pass count) loops are bounded.
- **Condition test-size bound.** The substituted test expression is size-bounded before evaluation; an oversized substituted test fails the match rather than aborting.

Malformed nodes never panic: the `pattern_tree_well_formed` guard rejects malformed `Pattern[…]` before indexing; wrong-arity `Alternatives`/`Condition`/`PatternTest` simply fail to match, and wrong-arity `ReplaceRepeated` stays unevaluated.

### Verification

`cargo test -p coding-adventures-wolfram-runtime -p coding-adventures-wolfram-repl` — W-20 unit tests (alternatives, condition, pattern_test, replace_repeated, match_q) and the `w20_advanced_pattern_constructs_evaluate_end_to_end` repl integration test all pass, including the security-cap stress tests.

### Deferred to W-21

- Operator **sugar** for all four constructs (`|`, `/;`, `?`, `//.` — needs a grammar change).
- **Sequence patterns** `__` (`BlankSequence`) / `___` (`BlankNullSequence`) — variable-arity matching is not yet in the shared `cas-pattern-matching` matcher (so W-20's `ReplaceRepeated` tests use non-sequence rules).
- **`Repeated`** (`patt..`), **`Except`**, **`Longest`/`Shortest`**, and **`Replace` level specifications** (the third argument).
