author: balianwang
body:
Moves the macOS updater from silent launch-time auto-apply to a user-controlled model and adds a manual version-downgrade escape hatch. Also bundles a small titlebar layout fix (the branch's original change).

## What changes

**Updater rework (primary):**
- **Detect-only launch + periodic polling.** `updaterClient` is split into `checkForUpdate()` (detect-only, 20s timeout) and `applyUpdate()` (download + install + relaunch, 120s timeout, progress forwarding, maps a rejected `relaunch()` → `needs-manual-restart`). A new `UpdaterProvider` (mounted in `App.tsx`, main window only) owns the state machine, the live Tauri `Update` handle (held in a `useRef`, closed before swap + on unmount), and polling: mount check + 12h interval + focus re-check (>1h) + manual-check interval reset.
- **Titlebar badge button.** `UpdateBadgeButton` (hidden until an update is available) one-click installs; shows download percent; falls back to a manual-restart message if relaunch fails. Clustered with the per-page toolbar in a new right-aligned `.desktop-titlebar__actions` group (single `margin-left:auto`).
- **Settings rewire.** The Updates section reflects the shared status (available → "Update now", downloading → percent, relaunch-failure → manual restart, error → retry). A Windows "auto-update not supported" note is gated on the existing `isMacPlatform()` (no new dependency).
- **Manual downgrade (R1-verified).** A new Rust command `install_version(manifest_url)` drives the plugin's public `UpdaterBuilder` with an overridden endpoint (the chosen tag's `latest.json`) + a `true` version comparator to install an older version via the same proven macOS pipeline, then `app.request_restart()`. A `versions.json` index (CI-generated, hermetic `generate_versions_manifest.sh`, reusing already-uploaded per-tag `latest.json` assets) feeds a Settings "Version history" panel with a Reinstall action.

**Titlebar (bundled):** removes the vestigial left traffic-light gutter (`a388c39`) — the main window uses native decorations.

Telemetry uses `reportFrontendEventSafely` throughout (`gui.update.detected/applied/check_failed/download_failed/relaunch_failed/downgrade_requested`); Rust uses `tracing`.

## Verification
- Full GUI suite **760/760**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, Rust `updater_tests` 4/4, `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean.
- New logic files ≥90% coverage (most 100%); pre-existing files not regressed.
- TDD across 12 tasks; each task passed spec+quality review; final whole-branch review (merge-ready).
- ⚠️ The end-to-end downgrade (real per-tag `latest.json` → reinstall older build) + the badge-apply-on-a-build path are the manual/verify gate (spec §7), not unit-tested.

## Notes / follow-ups (pre-existing, not from this work)
- `tests/workflows/release_workflow_test.sh` greps `pnpm/action-setup@v4` but `release.yml` uses `@v6` → that workflow test exits 1 overall (this branch's own assertions pass). Trivial stale-assertion fix.
- Global `functions` coverage ~89.75% (pre-existing; enforced gate is lines-90, which passes).

Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-23-updater-improvements-design.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-23-updater-improvements.md` (both versioned on this branch).

author: juliayakovlev
body:
In splitted-networks configurations (`scylla_addresses_on_different_interfaces`), `broadcast_rpc_address` is on a different NIC (`eth1`) than `broadcast_address `(`eth0`). The client-facing TLS certificate SANs were only populated with eth0 identities, causing the Java driver to fail hostname verification when connecting to the eth1 endpoint advertised by broadcast_rpc_address.

Failed test: https://argus.scylladb.com/tests/scylla-cluster-tests/0679cc5b-68c3-41fe-a2ec-ad1d25f152bf

**Why it happened.**

[PR #7450](https://github.com/scylladb/scylla-cluster-tests/pull/7450) (splitted-networks test) merged on `2024-06-03`, but [PR #7436](https://github.com/scylladb/scylla-cluster-tests/pull/7436) (per-node TLS certificate generation with SAN hostname verification) merged on `2024-06-17` — two weeks later.
When PR #7450 was tested and merged, SCT was still using the old shared static certificates created in 2016 that did not use SAN-based hostname verification at all. The Java driver didn't verify SANs, so it didn't matter which IP was in the cert.

PR #7436 introduced per-node certificates with proper SAN extensions (IP + DNS names tied to each specific node) and enabled hostname verification in stress tools. But it only considered the ip_address (= broadcast_address, NIC 0) and private_dns_name (also NIC 0) when building SANs — it didn't account for the split-network case where the client-facing endpoint (broadcast_rpc_address) is on a different NIC.

The two PRs were developed in parallel and merged close together without accounting for their interaction. The splitted-networks test passed originally because hostname verification wasn't enforced. Once per-node certs with SAN verification landed, the combination broke — but likely wasn't caught immediately because this specific test may not have run frequently or the failure wasn't triaged until now.

**The fix**

Add the `broadcast_rpc_address` IP and its DNS hostname to the client-facing certificate SANs when they differ from the broadcast_address identities.

Fixes: https://scylladb.atlassian.net/browse/SCT-529

author: craus81
body:
## What & why

Adds an admin **"Delete from FleetSuite"** button on each part in the Parts Catalog (`/parts`), for cleaning up duplicate rows and rows that are wrong locally but correct in NetSuite.

**Deletion is local-only — NetSuite is never touched.** This is the inverse of the edit feature: it removes the bad/duplicate row from the local `netsuite_parts` mirror without changing the source of truth.

## Changes

- **`src/app/api/parts/[id]/route.ts`** — new `DELETE` handler (admin-only):
  1. Removes attached files from storage (`graphics-proofs`) — the `part_files` rows cascade, but the stored objects would otherwise linger.
  2. Detaches FK references that have **no `ON DELETE` rule** (`po_line_items`, `schedule_assignments`) by nulling `part_id`, so the delete can't fail with a FK violation. `estimate_line_items` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`) and `part_files` (`CASCADE`) handle themselves. The `part_number` string stays on those rows so they remain identifiable and can re-match later.
  3. Deletes the `netsuite_parts` row.
- **`src/app/(main)/parts/page.tsx`** — red delete button in a part's expanded detail with a `confirm()` that spells out it's app-only and that a later sync may re-add a part still present in NetSuite.

## Important behavior

- **Re-sync resurrection:** a deleted row that has a *live NetSuite twin* (real internal id still active in NetSuite) will come back on the next "Sync Now" — that's correct, since NetSuite is the source of truth. Duplicate / stale / manual (`source='manual'`) rows with no live twin **stay gone**. The confirm dialog states this.
- Runs with the service role, so RLS doesn't block the cross-table cleanup.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` (109 tests) all pass.

author: sinity
body:
## Summary

Exact `find ... then read` refs now resolve to the selected session payload instead of falling back into the search renderer. This covers `session:<id>` and `id:<id>` when they are used as exact refs with no accompanying FTS or similarity term.

## Problem

Live dogfooding showed that `polylogue find session:<id> then read --view summary --format json` could return a search envelope rather than the concrete session payload. The verb layer had enough information to identify the selected session, but the standard read-view handler kept the original query terms and re-entered normal query rendering.

## Solution

The read verb resolver now treats exact session refs as concrete targets without a summary-list round trip when there is no text/similarity search leg. The standard summary/transcript read handler then rewrites that selected target to a direct `conv_id` request while preserving mixed `session:<id> needle` behavior as search-within-session.

Ref #2317

Remaining #2317 scope: broader root onboarding/facet/action grammar polish is still separate from this exact-ref read path.

## Verification

- `devtools test tests/unit/cli/test_query_verbs_runtime.py -k read_verb_summary` -> 3 passed.

author: goodjunseon
body:
## 작업 내용

평면 enum(`InterestCategoryType`) 기반 관심사를 **카테고리 + 사전 태그 + 태그 간 관계(유사/보완/충돌)** 구조로 재설계하고, 온보딩 키워드 선택·저장을 신규 구조로 전환합니다. 탐색 알고리즘 키워드 점수(K, 45%)의 데이터 기반을 마련합니다. (설계: `docs/keyword/KEYWORD_DOMAIN.md`)

### 1. 키워드 도메인 신설 (`keyword` 패키지)

- **`KeywordCategory`** — 카테고리 마스터(8종). `code`/`name` 유니크, `sort_order`, `is_required`(핵심 카테고리만 필수)
- **`KeywordTag`** — 카테고리별 사전 태그. `category_id` FK, `code` 유니크, `(category_id, name)` 유니크, `is_active`
- **`MemberKeyword`** — 회원의 태그 선택(N). `(member_id, tag_id)` 유니크로 중복 차단, `tag_id` 인덱스 (기존 `interest_category` 대체)
- **`KeywordRelation`** — 태그 간 관계. `RelationType`(SIMILAR/COMPLEMENT/CONFLICT)
  - `KeywordRelation.of`가 항상 `tag_a_id < tag_b_id`로 정규화 + `UNIQUE(tag_a_id, tag_b_id)` + `@Check` → **한 쌍은 한 행·한 유형** (검토 개선안 #2 중복 행 / #3 보완↔충돌 양립 차단)
- **`RelationType`** — 유형별 점수 상수(유사+5/보완+3/충돌−4). 동일(+10)은 행이 아니라 회원 간 `tag_id` 일치로 판정

### 2. 카탈로그·관계 시드 (`keyword/seed`)

- **`KeywordSeedData`** — 8개 카테고리·태그·관계 정의(기획 v1.1 §7.3·§7.4)
- **`KeywordSeeder`** (`ApplicationRunner`) — 비어 있을 때만 삽입하는 **멱등** 시더(Flyway 미사용 구성). `blursome.keyword.seed.enabled=false`로 비활성화 가능
- 관계는 한 쌍 한 유형으로 정규화(예: `운동↔산책`=유사, `즉흥형↔계획형`=보완). **충돌(CONFLICT) 쌍은 기획 §7.4.4 충돌 기준 정규화 후 보강** — 유형 enum은 포함, 시드만 후속

### 3. 키워드 카탈로그 API

- **`GET /api/keywords`** (공개) — 카테고리(정렬·필수 여부) + 활성 태그 목록. 온보딩 선택 화면이 태그 id를 알 수 있게 함
- `KeywordCatalogService`, `KeywordController`, `KeywordCategoryResponse`/`KeywordTagResponse`

### 4. 온보딩 전환

- `OnboardingRequest.interests`(List<InterestCategoryType>) → **`keywordTagIds`(List<Long>)**
- `MemberOnboardingService.completeOnboarding` — ① 태그 존재·활성 검증 ② 필수 카테고리(각 최소 1개) 검증 ③ `member_keyword` 저장
- `MemberProfileResponse.interests` → **`keywords`**(선택 키워드: 카테고리·태그)

### 5. 에러 코드 (`KeywordErrorCode`)

| 코드 | 상황 | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| `KEYWORD_400_TAG_NOT_FOUND` | 존재하지 않거나 비활성 태그 포함 | 400 |
| `KEYWORD_400_REQUIRED_CATEGORY_MISSING` | 필수 카테고리 미선택 | 400 |

### 6. 레거시 제거

- `InterestCategory`, `InterestCategoryType`, `InterestCategoryRepository`, `InterestResponse` 삭제

---

## 커밋 구성

리뷰 동선을 위해 **문서 → 도메인 → 리포지토리 → 시드 → API → 온보딩 전환 → 제거** 순 7개 커밋으로 분할했습니다.

| 단계 | 커밋 |
|---|---|
| 문서 | 문서: 관심사 키워드 도메인 설계 문서 추가 |
| 도메인 | 기능: 관심사 키워드 도메인 엔티티·enum 추가 |
| 리포지토리 | 기능: 관심사 키워드 리포지토리 추가 |
| 시드 | 기능: 관심사 키워드 카탈로그·관계 시드 추가 |
| API | 기능: 키워드 카탈로그 조회 API 추가 |
| 온보딩 | 기능: 온보딩을 키워드 태그 선택 기반으로 전환 |
| 제거 | 제거: 레거시 관심사(InterestCategory) 제거 |

---

## 변경 이유

- **DB 마스터 테이블 채택**: 관계(`keyword_relation`)가 태그를 FK로 참조해야 무결성이 보장되고, 태그·관계는 베타 후 튜닝 대상이라 코드 재배포 없이 데이터로 조정해야 한다(enum 방식의 약점). 카테고리/태그는 참조 데이터라 "enum=STRING" 컨벤션과 충돌하지 않는다.
- **관계 점수는 코드 상수**: 검토 개선안 #6 고정 점수표(동일+10/유사+5/보완+3/충돌−4)와 1:1 일치, 데이터 일관성 확보(쌍별 컬럼 관리 부담 제거).
- **필수 카테고리만 강제**: 8개 전부 강제는 온보딩 부담이 커, 핵심(취미/여가·성격/대화·연락/관계)만 `is_required`로 두었다(검토 개선안 #7).
- **외형 태그 분리**: 매칭 비대상이라 본 도메인에서 제외(별도 도메인 후속).

> ⚠️ **운영 배포 주의**: 신규 테이블(`keyword_category`/`keyword_tag`/`member_keyword`/`keyword_relation`)이 추가됩니다. prod는 `ddl-auto: validate`이므로 배포 전 DDL을 적용해야 합니다.
> ⚠️ **API 호환성**: 온보딩 요청/응답 필드가 변경됩니다(`interests` → `keywordTagIds` / `keywords`). 프론트 연동 동기화 필요.

author: benzsevern
body:
## What

The metrics harness's first **real** ER-benchmark probe — **Febrl3** (5000-record person dedup with published ground truth) via `recordlinkage`'s bundled data, so it's still offline (no download) and deterministic. This is the real-data counterpart to the synthetic accuracy probe: the regression net for changes that move accuracy on real corruption a hand-built generator can't model.

Follow-up to #1225 (harness) / #1232 (semantic) / #1234 (trained embedder). Implements the "real-dataset tier" rung.

## Result

Explicit deterministic config (`exact soc_sec_id` ∪ `fuzzy given_name+surname+date_of_birth`):

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| F1 | **0.9017** |
| precision | 0.8691 |
| recall | 0.937 |

(For reference, CLAUDE.md notes auto-config gets Febrl3 ~0.944 and multi-pass FS ~0.991; 0.90 from a fixed explicit config is a solid, stable operating point for a regression net.)

## Opt-in by design

The probe **skips cleanly** — contributing *no* metrics, never an error — unless `METRICS_REAL_DATASETS=1` **and** `recordlinkage` is installed. So the default offline run and the committed baseline stay dependency-free. This adds a `skipped` status to the probe protocol (distinct from `error`) — the seam for further download/key-gated sets (DBLP-ACM, NCVR) to plug in behind the same pattern.

- **Default run** (no flag): `accuracy_febrl3 — skipped`; its committed gated metrics show `MISSING`, which is **non-failing**. `--check` exit 0.
- **Opt-in run** (`METRICS_REAL_DATASETS=1` + recordlinkage): runs, diffs against the committed baseline. `--check` exit 0.

Both modes verified green.

## Gating

F1/precision/recall are **gated** (±0.02 — absorbs the handful of boundary pairs cross-env fuzzy scoring can flip out of 6538). The raw `tp`/`fp`/`fn` counts ride as **informational** diagnostics, since real-data scoring is likelier to wobble by a pair or two across environments than the synthetic path the strict-count gate was validated on. The committed baseline records the real numbers so opt-in runs diff against a known reference (and the benchmark result is documented in-repo).

## Wiring

- `bench-metrics` workflow runs the probe on schedule + dispatch (installs `recordlinkage`, sets the flag); a `real_datasets` dispatch input (default true) toggles it.
- The opt-in env var carries **no** `GOLDENMATCH_` prefix on purpose — it's a dev-harness toggle, not a runtime tuning flag, so it stays out of the user tuning-doc reference (and the docs-staleness flag gate). Verified clean.

4 new tests (skip-without-flag, skip-contributes-nothing-and-never-regresses, real-run-when-enabled [dep-gated via `importorskip`], baseline-records-real-numbers); `ruff` clean; 21 harness tests pass.

body:
## Description

Fixes multiple safety and correctness bugs in the Unix PTY/shell-spawn code path in `app/src/terminal/local_tty/unix.rs`. See linked issue for full details.

Changes:
- **UB fix**: Move `assume_init_read()` after `status` and `res` null checks in `get_pw_entry` — previously `assume_init()` was called unconditionally, reading uninitialized memory on failure
- **Correct error check**: Replace `status < 0` with `status != 0` — `getpwuid_r` returns positive errno values on failure, never -1
- **Error propagation**: Replace `panic!("getpwuid_r failed")` / `panic!("pw not found")` / `assert_eq!` with `Result` returns throughout `get_pw_entry`, `get_pw_shell`, `build_host_shell_command`, `build_docker_sandbox_command`, `spawn`, and `spawn_docker_sandbox`
- **ERANGE retry**: Replace fixed 1024-byte buffer with a doubling retry loop (1024 → 65536 bytes) to handle large passwd entries (long home paths, LDAP/NIS/SSSD)
- **Type-correct buffer**: Use `Vec<libc::c_char>` instead of `Vec<i8>` to avoid type mismatch on platforms where `c_char = u8`
- **Owned strings**: Change `Passwd` fields from borrowed `&'a str` to owned `String`, removing the buffer lifetime dependency
- **UTF-8 handling**: Use `to_string_lossy()` for `name`/`dir`, strict `to_str()?` for `shell` (shell path must be valid UTF-8 to exec)
- **`fcntl` return values**: Check both `fcntl(FD_CLOEXEC)` calls in `make_pty` and propagate errors
- **`res` pointer check**: Verify `res == entry.as_mut_ptr()` after `getpwuid_r`
- **Dead code**: Add `#[allow(dead_code)]` to `get_pw_shell` (no external callers)
- **Stale doc comment**: Remove outdated "pointers into buf" safety note from `get_pw_entry`
- **Tests**: Update all call sites in `unix_tests.rs` and `test_get_pw_entry` with `.expect(...)`

author: dgreco-debug
body:
Follow-up to [#86](https://github.com/narbiscorp/edge-earclip/pull/86) — the ▲/▼ nudge still looked dead on Mode C.

**Root cause:** while `modeB == null` the engine is "settling", and the breath cue is **frozen during settling** (added in #81). Without a Polar H10, Mode C stays in settling indefinitely → the cue never moves, so the nudge appears to do nothing. (Mode A is never settling; its nudge already works when the engine is running — verified by a new no-device test.)

**Fix:** `isSettling()` now **yields while a manual nudge HOLD is active** — the cue un-freezes and paces at the nudged rate (which also seeds where the Mode C search begins). After the hold expires, settling resumes and the seed override persists to handoff.

**Tests added:** Mode A nudge changes the pace with **no beats/devices connected**; a **Mode C nudge during settling** flips `settling` off and moves `pacerBpm` to the nudged rate. **49/49 pass**, `tsc` clean, `vite build` OK.

> Note: if Mode A's nudge looked dead for you too, it was likely a stale cached bundle — hard-refresh (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R). The new test proves the Mode A path works with nothing connected.

# S05-temp-workspace-diff: Temp Workspace Diff Extraction

## Goal
Run configured local agents in a temporary repository copy and convert safe before/after file changes into structured proposals.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Temporary workspaces are created outside the tracked repository and removed after execution.
- Repo copy excludes `.git` and avoids heavy generated/cache directories such as `node_modules` and obvious Quartz cache/output paths where practical.
- Created or modified allowed Markdown files become proposal records with normalized repository-relative paths and UTF-8 content.
- Deletions, symlinks, binary files, non-Markdown files, `.git/**`, `.llm-wiki/**`, `raw/**`, `quartz/**`, absolute paths, traversal paths, and backslash paths are rejected before real-repo writes.
- Agent execution failures report whether any temp workspace changes were observed.

## PRD Summary
Users who initialize llm-wiki for Codex get a safe, predictable path from queued raw source to validated curated wiki updates without manually copying prompts. The feature keeps the existing prompt-only and HTTP provider workflows intact while adding local Codex execution that is inspectable, validation-gated, rollback-friendly, and visible in status, help, and docs.

author: 0xnowater
body:
Closes #69

## What
The list poll's critical reads (`v2Project.list` / `v2Workspace.list`) decoded their arrays strictly. A tRPC **error envelope returned with HTTP 200**, or a single row whose required field drifted, threw `DecodingError` and failed the **whole** poll — blanking the browser, the outcome the code already avoids for `host.list`.

## How
- **Detect tRPC error-on-200 explicitly** — `TRPCEnvelope` makes both `result` and `error` optional, so `error.json.message` surfaces as `AuthError.trpcError` instead of being mis-decoded as a successful (empty) payload. The store's cache-first `refresh()` then keeps the last good list rather than blanking.
- **Per-row tolerant list decode** — `FailableDecodable` decodes each row independently; an un-decodable row is skipped (and logged) while its decodable siblings still render. `v2Project.list`, `v2Workspace.list`, and `host.list` all use the new `fetchList`.

## Verification
`xcodebuild test` green on the visionOS Simulator (32 unit tests + UITest). Two new tests in `CloudWorkspaceClientDecodeTests`:
- a drifted Workspace row (missing `id`) is skipped, its sibling survives;
- a tRPC error-envelope-on-200 throws `AuthError.trpcError` rather than decoding to an empty list.

💡 What: Replaced `fmt.Sprintf` with string concatenation and `strconv.FormatInt` for generating `cacheKey` and `byteRange` strings in the `CellsFuse.Read` method.
🎯 Why: `fmt.Sprintf` uses reflection and has high allocation overhead. In high-frequency hot paths like the chunk reading loop in a FUSE filesystem, this overhead becomes a measurable bottleneck, generating unnecessary garbage and consuming extra CPU cycles.

author: vitbokisch
body:
## Compiler trust — item 1, structural sub-step (the gate layer)

PR #1735 fixed the silent `[Any]` degradation at the **emit** layer. This PR closes the **gate** layer: the Swift validator was `swiftc -parse` (syntax-only) and could not catch *any* type error — `[Any]` is valid Swift, so type-erased emit sailed through green. Kotlin already did full semantic analysis via `kotlinc`; Swift was parse-only. **This closes that asymmetry.**

### What it adds

`validateSwiftTypecheck(source)` — runs `swiftc -typecheck` against the **real SwiftUI SDK**: full name + type resolution, **no stubs**. Unlike the kotlinc gate (which compiles against a *superset* Compose stub file that can mask mismatches — a documented hazard), this typechecks against the genuine framework, so there is no masking surface. Prepends `import SwiftUI` / `import Foundation` when absent.

### macOS-only, skips cleanly elsewhere

SwiftUI is an Apple framework — absent on the Linux PR runner even with `swiftc` installed. `isSwiftUIAvailable()` probes it (cached) and the validator **skips, never fails**, when it's unavailable. So the gate runs on local macOS dev + macOS CI; the cheap ubuntu PR job skips it. It's **additive** — not a new blocker.

### Verification (rungs named)

- **Gate discriminating power (negative control)** — a hand-built `let xs: [Int] = ["a", "b"]` SwiftUI View: `validateSwift` (`-parse`) **passes** it; `validateSwiftTypecheck` **rejects** it (`cannot convert value of type 'String' to expected element type 'Int'`). Proves the gate catches what the old one waved through, without depending on a live bug.
- **Real emit** — the #1735 typed `.map` projections (`[Int]`/`[String]`/`[Bool]`) + a counter/computed component **typecheck clean** against the real SDK (exit 0, zero stubs).
- **Idempotent preamble** + **off-macOS skip contract** covered.
- **Full native suite: 1243 pass** (1238 + 5 new gate tests).

### Scope / explicit follow-up

Validates emit referencing SwiftUI + stdlib + Foundation (the dominant component shape). Emit that references the `PyreonRuntime` package (storage / fetch / store / router components) needs that module on the search path via `-I` — the next sub-step (build the runtime module once, pass it to `-typecheck`, then run the gate across **all** emit fixtures). This PR establishes the faithful gate and proves it discriminates; broadening coverage is tracked.

`@pyreon/native-compiler` is private → no changeset.

author: ianhundere
body:
## what

Make `--cert-identity-list` a real signer allowlist that accepts **multiple** signer identities in a single `verify attestation` run, on both the online and offline paths.

- the list alone now enforces (was silently ignored without `--cert-identity`) — **closes #257**
- an image plus its `rw-verify` VSA (two distinct signers) verify in one run — **addresses #258** (CLI side; see note below)
- effective allowlist = `--cert-identity` (accepted as-typed) ∪ the revocation-checked valid list SANs; each attestation must match at least one (OR semantics via repeatable `verify.WithCertificateIdentity`)
- `--cert-identity` alone still behaves exactly as before

## fail-closed / safety

- a malformed/unreachable list, or a configured list that resolves to **zero** acceptable identities (all revoked/expired), now returns an error instead of degrading to accept-any
- when **neither** `--cert-identity` nor `--cert-identity-list` is set, behavior is unchanged (accept any valid signature) but a single warning is emitted to stderr, ungated by `--quiet`
- `IsValidIdentity` checks revocation across all entries before accepting any match, so cross-entry revocation is order-independent

## #258 note

The CLI change enables multi-signer verification, but the `rw-verify` signer must also be present in `cert-identities.json`. That list is generated in `autogov-workflows` by `scripts/update-cert-identities.sh`, whose glob currently excludes `rw-verify*`. A companion change there + a release is required to fully close #258 in production; it is sequenced after this PR.

## tests

New/extended coverage in `certid`, `attestations`, `orchestrate`, `offline`, and `cmd/verify`: allowlist resolution + union, list-only enforcement, all-revoked/empty-list fail-closed, cross-entry revocation (by SAN and by sha, order-independent), offline list plumbing, and the unsafe-mode warning. `go build`/`vet`/`test ./...` and lint all green.

Closes #257

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

## Release Notes

* **New Features**
  * Added support for an allowlist of acceptable signer identities, with OR-style enforcement across identities during attestation verification.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Offline attestation verification now enforces the signer identity allowlist consistently with online verification.
  * Verification now fails safely (fail-closed) when the configured certificate identity list is malformed or resolves to no valid identities.
  * Unsafe-mode messaging is now emitted exactly once, even when quiet mode is enabled.

* **Reliability**
  * Improved revocation validation so results are no longer sensitive to identity ordering.

## Summary

The main timeline page exposed three sub-tabs — **Home / No Announces / Mention** — each backed by its own materialized projection in the `timelines` table. Now that the **lists** feature covers custom feeds, the extra tabs are redundant. The timeline page now renders a **single Home feed with no tab strip**.

## What changed

- **UI:** Removed the tab strip from `MainPageTimeline`; it renders the Home (`MAIN`) feed only (load-more / refresh / scroll-to-top all retained).
- **Timeline enum & query:** Dropped `NOANNOUNCE` and `MENTION` from the `Timeline` enum, removed their `getTimeline` switch branches, and deleted the no-announce timeline rule. `/api/v1/timelines/noannounce` and `/api/v1/timelines/mention` now return **404** (invalid timeline), like any other unknown timeline.
- **Notifications preserved (important):** the old `mentionTimelineRule` did double duty — it materialized the mention timeline **and** created reply/mention notifications for **remote** statuses. That has been refactored into `notifyRemoteReplyAndMention`, a **notification-only** side effect invoked from `addStatusToTimelines`. The Alerts feature reads the separate `notifications` table and is unaffected; local-actor notifications still flow through `createNote.ts`. All the reply/mention dedup, email-channel, block, and policy-filter behaviors are kept (and still covered by the renamed test).
- **Migration:** `20260624000000_remove_noannounce_mention_timelines.js` deletes existing `noannounce`/`mention` rows from the `timelines` table. It is **data-only** (a `DELETE`, no DDL), so the reference schema dumps (`migrations/schema.sql`, `migrations/schema.sqlite.sql`) are unchanged and need no regeneration. `down` is a no-op (the rows are a rebuildable projection of `statuses`).
- **Mock + tests:** mock seeding only writes the `MAIN` timeline now; tests updated/renamed accordingly.

Добавлена контейнеризация `Docker` с кэшированием и настройкой для локального продакшена.

## Добавлено
### `Docker`
- `Dockerfile` - сборка `Django` приложения.
- `.dockerignore` - исключение кэшей, виртуальных окружений, логи и секреты.
- `docker-compose.yml` - управление всеми контейнерами:
  - `db` - база данных `posgres`.
  - `redis` - хранилище `redis` для кэширования ответов представлений.
  - `web` - приложение и веб-сервер(`django`, `gunicorn`).
  - `nginx` - обратный прокси сервер для раздачи статики и маршутизации запросов.
    - `nginx.conf` - конфигурация `nginx`.

Добавлены пакеты `gunicorn`(+ зависимости), `redis`, `django-debug-toolbar`(для локальной разработки), `psycopg` в `requirements.txt`.

### Кэширование
- Кэшируются эндпоинты:
  - Получение статических путей эндпоинтов `api_root`.
  - Редирект на оригинальную ссылку по токену `RedirectToOriginalUrlAPIView`.
    - Ручное кэширование.
  - Получение статистики `StatsAPIViewSet`.
    - Реализован декоратор `cache_retrieve`(добавлен файл `decorators.py`) для кэширования неуспешных запросов.
    - Реализован сигнал `clear_link_cache_on_save`(добавлен файл `signals.py`) для очистки кэша при создании/редактировании объекта `Link`.

## Изменения
### Разделения настроек для разработки и для продакшена.
- Создана директория `settings` в которой:
  - Перенесен файл `settings.py` и переименован в `base.py`.
  - Добавлен файл `local.py`, настройки для разработки.
  - Добавлен файл `prod.py`, настройки для продакшена.

По дефолту `django` использует настройки для разработки, `docker-compose` переопределяет настройки для продакшена.

Удалено поддержка суффиксов форматов url, так как бэкэнд отдает только `json`.

## Тесты
Добавлено
- Класс `TestRedirectToOriginalUrlAPIViewCache` тестирующий кэширование редиректа с методами:
  - `test_redirect_to_original_url_cache` проверяет работоспособность кэша при успешном редиректе.
  - `test_redirect_with_not_exist_token_cache` проверяет работоспособность кэша при неуспешном редиректе.
- Класс `TestStatsAPIViewSetCache` тестирующий кэширование статистики с методами:
  - `test_stats_detail_cache` проверяет работоспособность кэша при запросе детальной статистики с существующем токеном.
  - `test_stats_detail_with_not_exist_token_cache` проверяет работоспособность кэша при запросе детальной статистики с несуществующем токеном.
  - Для кэширования детальной статистики используется декоратор `cache_retrieve`.
- Класс `TestSignalClearLinkCacheOnSave` тестирует сигнал с методом:
  - `test_clear_cache_after_create_link` проверяет удаление кэша объекта, после создания/редактирования этого объекта.
- Кэширование при тестировании использует заглушку(не кэширует), при тестировании кэширования используется кэширование в оперативную память.

Изменения
- Рефакторинг тестовых значений ссылок и токенов, ссылки теперь используют зарезервированные адреса для тестирования, токены стали менее реалистичными, более читаемыми, обновлены файлы:
  - `test_models.py`, `test_serializers.py`, `test_views.py`.
 
## Как запустить и протестировать
Тестировать имеет смысл только приложение, так как тесты используют `SQLite` и `LocMemCache`.

Для тестирование только приложения:
1. Собрать образ `docker build -t <name-image> <путь к папке с Dockerfile>`.
2. Запустить образ `docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 <name-image> python manage.py test`.

Для запуска:
1. Собрать все контейнеры и запустить `docker compose up --build`.
2. Пройти по url `http://localhost/api/` или использовать `curl` и команду `-X GET http://localhost/api/` должно вернуться `json` со статичными url.

author: kafaat
body:
## ملخّص

يربط **محرّك المياه FAO-56** بمؤشّر الأقمار: بدل اشتقاق `Kcb` من **عمر** المحصول (منحنى جدوليّ ثابت)، يُشتقّ من **غطاء نباتيّ مرصود** عبر NDVI — فحقل متأخّر أو مُجهَد يُظهِر NDVI أدنى ⇒ `Kcb` أدنى ⇒ احتياج مائيّ **أصدق للواقع**. الفكرة «⭐» المتبقّية من `water-intelligence-direction.md`.

## الطريقة (FAO-56 §9.4 «Kc من كسر الغطاء»، Eq. 76-77)
دوالّ نقيّة في `core/engines/fao56.py`:
- `fractional_cover_from_ndvi(ndvi)` → كسر الغطاء `fc` ∈ [0,1] (علاقة fc–NDVI الخطّيّة، مقصوصة).
- `density_coefficient_kd(fc, h)` → معامل الكثافة `Kd = min(1, ML·fc, fc^(1/(1+h)))` (Eq. 76).
- `kcb_from_ndvi(ndvi, kcb_full, h)` → `Kcb = Kcb_full · Kd` (Kcb_full = ذروة الموسم).
- `compute_etc_dual(..., ndvi=None)` — عند تمرير `ndvi` يُشتقّ Kcb وfc **رصداً** بدل العمر.

## الصدق
- **حفظ السلوك تماماً:** `ndvi=None` (الافتراضيّ) ⇒ المسار القائم بلا تغيير (**١٧ اختبار dual-Kc أخضر**؛ المسار المفرد سليم).
- **تقدير لا قياس:** الحدود `NDVI_bare/full` (0.15/0.85) و`ML` افتراضيّة **تحتاج معايرة محلّيّة** لكلّ محصول/تربة — تُعلَن صراحةً في `DualKcResult.assumptions` وقت التشغيل (لا تلفيق دقّة).
- **engine-level** (كنمط dual-Kc نفسه): **الربط الاستهلاكيّ** (تمرير NDVI الحيّ من raster-service إلى المحرّك عبر نقطة/مهمّة) + LAI/غطاء التاج — **مرحلة تالية موثَّقة**، غير مُدّعاة هنا.

## التحقّق
- **٦ اختبارات جديدة** (`tests_v9/test_kc_ndvi.py`): حدود fc · رتابة Kd · Kcb=Kcb_full·Kd · التكامل (NDVI منخفض ⇒ Kcb أدنى) · **حفظ السلوك** عند غياب NDVI.
- `pytest -m unit`: **1713 ناجح** (+٦) · ١٧ انحدار dual-Kc أخضر · ruff/format نظيف.
- (فشل MFA الـ5 في `services/auth` سابقٌ لا صلة له.)

author: edtheguy00
body:
## Summary

Two zellimctl TUI improvements:

### 1. Dashboard loads live data on launch (bug)
The dashboard showed stale placeholders (`daemon: stopped`, `cert: 0`, `network: not yet loaded`) until you Tab away and back. Root cause: `runner::run` started its event loop with an empty channel, so `on_enter_screen(Dashboard)` (which dispatches the four loads) never fired at startup — it's only reached via navigation. Fix: seed one `Message::NavTo(Dashboard)` before the loop, and add a ~1s `RefreshStatus` poll on the Dashboard so daemon status/clients stay live.

### 2. Single-token pairing via a fullscreen QR overlay (feature)
Removed the **Pair** tab entirely. Its `start_pairing_task` minted a *second* throwaway token on every generate — separate from anything in the Tokens screen. Now pairing is driven from a token you just created:

**Tokens → `c` create → `Enter` → fullscreen QR overlay** encoding *that* token → scan → "✓ a client connected". One token per device, no second mint, no throwaway-token revoke machinery.

A QR can only be shown for a *just-created* token because tokens are stored hash-only (plaintext exists once, at creation). New app-level `qr_overlay` state + `ShowTokenQr` action that builds the URI from the existing plaintext (no mint, no regen); `screens/pairing.rs` → `screens/qr_overlay.rs`.

### Overlay rendering fixes (follow-ups)
- Center the QR in the window (was pinned to a fixed left column).
- `Clear` the overlay area before painting so the dashboard's text glyphs underneath don't bleed through (a `Block` background fill only recolors cells; it leaves the glyphs — which read as a "transparent" QR background). The QR matrix itself was always opaque (verified via a buffer probe).
- Coalesce the overlay + screen status polls onto a shared single-flight guard (was double-dispatching `status()`).

## Unchanged / out of scope
The auth-token ↔ session-key model (`Login` RPC, 28-day TTL), the pairing URI format, the Flutter app, and the gRPC bearer + TLS-fingerprint-pinning boundary are all untouched.

## Verification
`cargo build`, `cargo test` (113 pass), `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` all clean. Multi-dimension review (logic/architecture/quality/security): APPROVED_WITH_CONCERNS — security PASS, one Major (poll double-dispatch) fixed and verified. Deferred minors are documented in the review.

body:
## Two fixes for the duplicate-delivery risk you flagged

### 1. Multi-product modal clarity
On a multi-product invoice the form correctly stays open after saving one product (to record the next), but at the **save button** there was no signal — so it looked like pressing again would duplicate. Now:
- A progress banner above the button: *"✓ 1 of 2 products saved · Now recording product 2 of 2: petrol · 4000L — this is the last product."*
- Dynamic button label: **"✓ Record this product → N more to go"** vs **"✓ Record last product & finish"**.
- Single-product / last-product still **closes** the modal on save.

### 2. Server-side duplicate guard (the real safety net)
Even with the UX fix, a double-press / two browsers shouldn't be able to create a dupe. Added:
- **App pre-check**: same `(station_id, dc_number, fuel_type, gross_volume_ltrs)` → friendly **409**: *"Already recorded — DC 20274440B026517, petrol, 4000L (on 23-Jun). Not saved again."*
- **23505 catch** backstops the race once the unique index exists.
- Different products of one invoice (different fuel) are still allowed.

## ⚠️ One-time DDL to run (race-proof backstop)
Prod has only 3 deliveries, all distinct — installs cleanly:
```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_fuel_deliveries_dedup
ON fuel_deliveries (station_id, dc_number, fuel_type, gross_volume_ltrs)
WHERE dc_number IS NOT NULL;
```
The app-level check works immediately even before you run this; the index just closes the simultaneous-race gap.

**Edge case:** two compartments of the *same fuel at the exact same litres* on one invoice would be blocked. Rare — tell me if your tankers do that and I'll add `compartment_no` to the key.

Frontend `npm run build` + backend syntax both pass.

author: frankely29
body:
## What this fixes

A driver reported (IMG_4138): *"there is a nearby area that is much better and it is recommending I should stay... it's not smarter than a human."*

The map showed a **green** zone (much busier) a couple minutes away, but the assistant said *"Sit tight in Bay Ridge a few minutes — you've moved a lot without a trip, so let dispatch work."*

### Root cause
Anti-churn was too aggressive. After 2 fruitless moves, the engine blocked **all** nearby moves — even to a zone that is ~2 demand buckets stronger and an easy hop away. A human always takes an obvious upgrade; the engine didn't.

### The change
Add an **"obvious upgrade"** escape in `build_driver_guidance`:

- `LARGE_UPGRADE_GAP = 15.0` (~2 demand buckets).
- `obvious_upgrade` = the **closest** nearby candidate that is `>= current + 15`, blue+ (`>= 60`), and within `2.5 mi`.
- It overrides the move-attempt gate (`recent_move_attempts < 2`) **but not** the 11-minute rapid-rebounce cooldown — so we still never oscillate.
- Below-blue current zones reach it via the existing `clear_close_upgrade` escape; blue+ current zones get a new base-chain branch (`"Move to X — much busier and close."`).
- **Marginal** gains (< 15 pts) still respect anti-churn — small-gain churning stays blocked.

### Verified behavior
| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| sky 55 + green 83 @1.8mi, churned | hold | **move** ✅ |
| blue 62 + green 83 @1.5mi, churned | hold | **move** ✅ |
| sky 55 + blue 65 (+10) @1.5mi, churned | hold | hold ✅ (marginal) |
| sky 55 + green 83 @3.2mi, churned | hold | hold ✅ (too far) |

All 28 engine/benchmark tests pass. The benchmark `test_after_two_fruitless_moves_it_holds_instead_of_bouncing` was updated to use a genuinely marginal gap (+8) so it still asserts anti-churn holds for small gains.

author: aizu-m
body:
Tracing how driver-reported counts flow into the device-group sort.

    out-of-bounds write, linux_sort_physical_device_groups (loader_linux.c:363):
        internal_device_info[gpu] = ...      gpu < group_props.physicalDeviceCount
        internal_device_info is [VK_MAX_DEVICE_GROUP_SIZE]   (32 entries)

`VkPhysicalDeviceGroupProperties::physicalDevices` is a fixed `[VK_MAX_DEVICE_GROUP_SIZE]` array, and `loader_physical_device_group_term` embeds a matching `internal_device_info[VK_MAX_DEVICE_GROUP_SIZE]`. terminator_EnumeratePhysicalDeviceGroups copies each group straight from the ICD into `local_phys_dev_groups[...].group_props` and trusts `physicalDeviceCount` unmodified.

An ICD that reports `physicalDeviceCount` greater than 32 then drives the consumers off the end of those fixed arrays: the Linux sort writes past `internal_device_info`, while the Windows sort and `setup_loader_tramp_phys_dev_groups` read past `physicalDevices`. The count from the first (group-count) query is already clamped, but the per-group device count never was.

Clamp it to `VK_MAX_DEVICE_GROUP_SIZE` at the two points where the group is copied in, so every downstream consumer sees a count that fits its array. The plain-device path already sets the count to 1.

author: youtalk
body:
## Summary

Stacked on the M2 D-cache work (`perf/freertos-s32z2-mpc-150ms`). Fixes the cold-boot RX death that appeared right after the L1 D-cache was enabled (`4511075`).

The NETC RX/TX buffer-descriptor rings and the NTMP command BD ring use the driver's `ETH_43_NETC_*_NO_CACHEABLE` MemMap section, which is a Green Hills `#pragma ghs section`. Our **GCC** (`arm-none-eabi`) build ignores it, so the descriptors landed in **cacheable** `.sram_data` (`int_sram_dram`, ~`0x3178d000`) instead of the non-cacheable `int_sram_no_cacheable` region (`0x31800000`) the MPU marks non-cacheable. The D-cache-enable commit assumed they were already non-cacheable; they were not.

With the D-cache on, the CPU read **stale descriptors**: the NETC DMA advanced the ring producer index (`RBPIR`) as frames arrived, but the poll thread's `Eth_Receive` saw stale "not ready" BDs, so the consumer index (`RBCIR`) never advanced and RX stalled once the ring filled.

## Evidence (hardware, SI ring counters over UART)

| D-cache | RX ring |
|---|---|
| **ON** (before fix) | `RBPIR=15 RBCIR=0` stuck -> RX dead |
| **OFF** (control) | `RBPIR==RBCIR` cycling -> RX works |
| **ON + this fix** | `RBPIR==RBCIR` cycling -> RX works (D-cache kept ON) |

## Fix

A linker `INSERT BEFORE .sram_data` fragment (`netc_bd_no_cacheable.ld`) claims the `Netc_Eth_Ip_Buffers` and `Netc_Eth_Ip_*_PBcfg` objects' `.data`/`.bss` into `int_sram_no_cacheable` before the default script's greedy `.sram_data` grabs them. ~1.5 KB of descriptors move; the driver's `*_DataBuffer` arrays are unused (`eth_port.c`'s `ethif_DataBuffer`, already non-cacheable, is the RX buffer). **D-cache stays ON**, preserving the MPC speed-up.

## Verification

- **Static:** `arm-none-eabi-nm` with `S32Z2_DCACHE=ON` confirms `Netc_Eth_0_TxRing_0/1_DescBuffer`, `Netc_Eth_0_RxRing_0_DescBuffer`, `Netc_Eth_CommandBDR` and `ethif_DataBuffer` all reside at `0x3180xxxx` (non-cacheable).
- **Hardware (confirmed 2026-06-17, board power-cycled):** with this fix and `S32Z2_DCACHE=ON`, `SCTLR=0x70c5183d` (I-cache + D-cache ON) and the SI RX ring cycles `RBPIR==RBCIR` in lockstep — the previously stuck `15/0` ring now drains. The board boots to `Actuation Safety Island is Live`, receives host DDS inputs, and runs the MPC/PID control loop with no faults. The multi-week cold-boot RX death is resolved with the D-cache kept enabled.
- **Hardware round-trip (confirmed 2026-06-17):** a full end-to-end DDS round-trip succeeds with the D-cache on — the host subscriber received **17 `control_cmd` samples** from the board, all `steering_tire_angle = -0.236017 rad` (identical to the pre-cache baseline). A CycloneDDS trace confirms the board's `control_cmd` writer matched the host reader and unicast DATA was delivered, so the fix is correct for both the RX **and** TX descriptor rings.

## Notes

- Depends on the D-cache commit in the base branch.
- The board->host round-trip is intermittent on this bench (a discovery race seen across earlier sessions): a prior run showed `0` control_cmd before a clean run delivered all 17. This is a discovery-robustness/bench concern, independent of this fix (the fix's data path is confirmed working in the successful run).
- **Out of scope (separate follow-up):** with the D-cache on, the MPC cycle measured ~2.67 s (vs ~3.04 s uncached) — far short of the assumed 10-50x, so the M2 perf hypothesis needs re-instrumentation. Unrelated to this change.

author: laqieer
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1376 / PR #1384 (the Patch Manager `HARDCODING_*`/`!` token-handling fix). **GUI validation of the merged fix revealed it still showed `(filtered: 0)`** — because the patches were never loaded.

`PatchMetadataCore.EnumeratePatches` only scanned the **immediate** subdirectories of `config/patch2/{ver}` and took `patchFiles[0]` of each (one patch per top-level dir → ~506 of 1933). Hardcoding/installed patches live in **subdirectories** (e.g. `FE8U/SYSTEM/PATCH_Eirika's Tale.txt`), so they were never in `_allPatches` and the `[HardCoding]` token filter could never match anything in the GUI. The token fix in #1384 was necessary but not sufficient.

This makes `EnumeratePatches` enumerate **every** `PATCH_*.txt` recursively (`SearchOption.AllDirectories`), matching WinForms `PatchForm.ScanPatchs`. Each patch is named by its `NAME` param (fallback = filename minus `PATCH_`); `DirectoryName` is set to the patch's real containing folder so the CLI `--patch-name` folder filter keeps working. `ParsePatchFile` is unchanged (no blast radius on its other caller / existing tests).

Ref #1376

## Changes
- **`FEBuilderGBA.Core/PatchMetadataCore.cs`** — `EnumeratePatches` recurses over all `PATCH_*.txt`; per-file display name; `DirectoryName` = real containing folder.
- **`FEBuilderGBA.Core.Tests/PatchMetadataCoreTests.cs`** — new `EnumeratePatches_RecursesAndFindsAllPatchFiles` (subdir + multi-file-per-dir + top-level; asserts all found + re-loadable `PatchFilePath`).

## Proof — real running Avalonia GUI

Captured from the actual app (vanilla `roms/FE8U.gba`), Patch Manager filtered with the token the `[HardCoding]` link seeds:

![Patch Manager filtered to HARDCODING_UNIT=01](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/laqieer/FEBuilderGBA/master/pr-screenshots/pr1376-hardcoding-filter-gui.png)

`Total: 1933 patches | Installed: 0 (filtered: 2)` showing **"Main Character for Eirika's Tale"** + **"Eirika Campaign Supply"** — exactly the issue's *Expected (WinForms)* behavior. Before this fix the GUI showed `Total: 506 patches … (filtered: 0)`.

## Test plan
- [x] **Core `EnumeratePatches_RecursesAndFindsAllPatchFiles`** — two patches in a subdir + one top-level: all 3 found, named by `NAME`/filename, `PatchFilePath` re-loadable.
- [x] **Existing Core patch tests (119 pass)** — `PatchMetadataCoreTests` + `PatchFilterCoreTests` + `PatchHardCodeScannerTests` all green (`ParsePatchFile` unchanged → no regression).
- [x] **Avalonia `PatchManagerFilterTests` (6 pass)** — token + `!` + substring + empty filter.
- [x] **Real-GUI end-to-end** — launched the Avalonia app on FE8U, opened Patch Manager via UIAutomation, applied `HARDCODING_UNIT=01`: summary went from `Total: 506 … (filtered: 0)` (old) to `Total: 1933 … (filtered: 2)` (fixed), list shows the two Eirika hardcoders. Screenshot above.

## GUI Test Report

| Scenario | Token | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit `[HardCoding]` (FE8U, unit 0x01) | `HARDCODING_UNIT=01` | `Total: 506 … (filtered: 0)` | `Total: 1933 … (filtered: 2)` — Eirika's Tale + Eirika Campaign Supply |
| Patch list load | — | 506 patches (subdirs dropped) | 1933 patches (recursive) |
| Plain substring | `Skill` | worked | worked (69) |

author: axisrow
body:
Объединяет **три родственных sub-issue** группы 5 «CI-гигиена» (родитель #1023) в один PR — все трое правят `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, порознь параллельно дали бы merge-конфликт по одному файлу с одной точкой ревью.

## #1051 — триггеры + concurrency + timeout + paths-ignore
- **Триггеры (решение владельца — CI только перед PR):** `push: [main]` (post-merge проверка main) + `pull_request:` (open + push-в-PR через `synchronize`). Убран push-триггер для `fix/**`/`codex/**` — он давал двойной ран (ветка + PR) и жёг раннеры на черновых push без PR. Промежуточный push в feature-ветку **без открытого PR теперь НЕ триггерит CI**.
- **`concurrency`** по `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` + `cancel-in-progress: true` — при новом пуше старый ран той же группы отменяется (перестаём жечь раннеры впустую). main и каждый PR независимы.
- **`timeout-minutes`** на каждый job (`check-branch-name` 5, `static-checks` 10, `lint-and-test` 15) — hang-guard вместо 6-часового GitHub-дефолта.
- **`paths-ignore`** docs-only (`docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `mkdocs.yml`). ⚠️ all-or-nothing: ран скипается только если **ВСЕ** файлы попадают под фильтр → code+docs PR всё равно гоняет полный suite.

## #1052 — coverage-гейт (baseline для баг-ханта #1024)
- `--cov=src` на parallel + serial прогонах (`--cov-append` на serial), combined `coverage report` + `coverage.xml` артефакт. `[tool.coverage.run] parallel = true` уже держит датафайлы xdist-воркеров раздельно; pytest-cov их комбинирует.
- **Ratchet `fail_under = 88`** в `[tool.coverage.report]`. Измеренный baseline combined (parallel+serial, ~9319 тестов) — **~91%**; гейт на пару пунктов ниже от branch-coverage jitter. Эпик #1024 двигает число вверх (raise, never lower).

## #1053 — security-scan (pip-audit + bandit) + Dependabot
- **`pip-audit`** (CVE зависимостей) + **`bandit`** (статанализ `src/`) как **advisory** шаги (`continue-on-error`, по образцу jscpd-гарда) в `static-checks`. Локальный триаж: bandit даёт **183 находки** (121 Low / 61 Medium / 1 High — B704 false-positive, там `escape()` на всех значениях); pip-audit ловит транзитивные CVE. Blocking сразу свалил бы CI → стартово advisory, ratchet позже (skip-лист/`# nosec`).
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** (новый): экосистемы `pip` + `github-actions`, weekly, group minor/patch (major — отдельным PR для ревью, supply-chain note #918).
- `pip-audit>=2.7.3` / `bandit>=1.8.0` в `[dev]`; `[tool.bandit] exclude_dirs = ["tests"]`.

## Не-регресс соседних workflow
`real-provider.yml` (workflow_dispatch), `docs.yml` (push docs/** + dispatch), `release.yml` (tags v*) **не трогаются** и не конфликтуют по триггерам с новыми `on:`/`concurrency` ci.yml.

## Верификация (продукт-кода нет, только YAML+config)
- `ruff check src tests conftest.py` — pass; YAML ci.yml + dependabot.yml парсятся, структура dependabot валидна.
- Триггер-логика: push в feature-ветку без PR → нет рана; open PR → ран; push в PR → ран (synchronize); docs-only PR → suite скипнут; push в main → ран.
- Coverage: локально parallel 88% + serial `--cov-append` → combined **91%** ; `coverage report` с `fail_under=88` → exit 0; `coverage.xml` генерится.
- `bandit -c pyproject.toml -r src` — конфиг применился (tests исключены, 0 файлов в tests просканировано).
- smoke preflight (`pytest -m smoke`) — pass; pyproject-изменения не ломают сбор и `filterwarnings=["error"]`.

## ⚠️ Операционная заметка для ревьюера
Если `lint-and-test` настроен как **required status check** в branch protection, docs-only PR (где job скипается через `paths-ignore`) может «висеть» в ожидании чека, который не появится. Это известный нюанс GitHub `paths-ignore` + required checks — решается на уровне branch-protection (отдельно от файлов репо), не входит в scope этого PR.

После мержа — убедиться, что main по-прежнему гоняет **полный** CI (память проекта: проверять conclusion CI перед мержем).

Closes #1051, Closes #1052, Closes #1053

body: In the dashboards widget builder, the aggregate column dropdown displayed **"None"** whenever the saved column value was not present in its options. `CompactSelect` renders "None" as the trigger label when the `value` prop matches none of the available options. This happened when a saved field — including a function's column argument like `p90(my_field)` — was not returned by the `/trace-items/attributes/` call. The existing "old tags" fallback only re-injected top-level field columns, so aggregate column arguments missing from attributes still fell through to "None". Before After ## Changes - `selectRow.tsx`: Always include the currently selected `columnValue` in the column dropdown's options when it's not already present, so the dropdown reflects the saved state instead of showing "None". Scoped to the column dropdown only — the aggregate dropdown and other `sortSelectedFirst` callers are unaffected. DAIN-1726 fixes https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/issues/118150

author: jalehman
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refs #88838.

Memory dreaming, QMD export, and memory session sync need the session identity and ownership model from the 3.1b session accessor migration. This PR adds a transcript corpus helper that reads active session entries through the session accessor seam, then gives memory callers one entry shape with path, session id, session key, agent owner, artifact kind, and generated-session flags. The CI ratchet covers the migrated memory corpus surface so future memory changes use that helper.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #93187 changed transcript and session-file behavior in memory paths that sat outside the previous session-accessor guards. Active sessions already have canonical identity through `listSessionEntries`. Retained reset/delete transcripts are file-backed artifacts because core does not expose archive enumeration through the session accessor. The corpus helper combines those inputs at the SDK boundary and keeps ownership and classification decisions out of dreaming and QMD call sites.

## User Impact

There are no user-facing command changes. Memory dreaming, QMD session export, full session indexing, targeted session sync, and live transcript-update catchup keep active, reset, and deleted transcript coverage. The corpus respects configured `session.store` paths, shared-store agent ownership, legacy default-agent aliases, generated dreaming/cron classification, malformed metadata rejection, symlink rejection, and cross-agent transcript boundaries.

## Changes

- Add a dedicated memory transcript corpus module.
- Read active transcripts from session accessor entries.
- Represent retained reset/delete transcript files as corpus artifacts.
- Move dreaming, QMD export, and memory sync to corpus entries.
- Carry generated dreaming/cron classification through corpus entries.
- Keep `listSessionFilesForAgent` as a corpus wrapper.
- Ratchet migrated corpus entrypoints and helper calls.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-sync-yield.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-sync-ops.startup-catchup.test.ts packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts test/scripts/check-session-accessor-boundary.test.ts src/plugins/contracts/extension-package-project-boundaries.test.ts`

- `node scripts/check-deprecated-api-usage.mjs && node scripts/check-session-accessor-boundary.mjs && node scripts/check-session-transcript-reader-boundary.mjs && node --import tsx scripts/check-no-monolithic-plugin-sdk-entry-imports.ts`

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.packages.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-packages.tsbuildinfo`
  - Confirms the package test TypeScript gate accepts the split corpus module and exports.
- `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check`
  - Confirms the SDK surface budget matches this PR's public export change.
- `git diff --check`
  - Confirms the final patch has no whitespace errors.

body:
## Autonomy Level: AUDIT — please scan the diff before merge. Do NOT auto-merge; I did not deploy.

Q4 direction **B**. Surfaces IBKR's own realized P&L + commission on the dashboard, **additively**, without changing the existing estimate or the kill-switch.

### Why AUDIT / why I stopped short of deploy
- Touches the execution/reconciler P&L path and adds DB columns.
- **The commissionReport semantics are NOT yet live-verified on DUQ331660** — there were no fills to probe at authoring time (last trade 2026-06-18; restarts cleared the in-session fill cache). Per §0.5.98 the meaning of `realizedPNL` (round-trip vs per-leg, net vs gross of commission) should be confirmed against a **live round-trip** before these numbers are trusted. The dashboard column is labelled accordingly and falls back to the estimate until then.

### Design — additive, off the hot path, kill-switch-safe
- New **nullable** columns `commission_broker` / `realized_pnl_broker` (migration `20260623200000`, idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`). `pnl_gross`/`pnl_net`/`commission_total` stay the fixed-rate estimate and **remain the kill-switch drawdown input — unchanged** (kill_switch reads `pnl_net` only; confirmed).
- `commissionReport` arrives **async** (zero-filled inline at fill time), so capture is a best-effort **reconciler backfill** on the periodic `full_scan`: query recently-CLOSED lifecycles missing the columns → read `IB.fills()` → sum commission over entry+exit (round-trip) + realizedPNL over the exit leg → PATCH. Never raises into the loop; **does not touch `router.on_fill`**. Rows whose fills predate a reconnect stay NULL → dashboard shows the estimate.
- New `Lifecycle` fields are **not** in `_PNL_FIELDS`, so they gate no invariant in any state (synth-zero / force-close paths unaffected).
- Dashboard: trade log gains a **Broker P&L** column beside `P&L net (est.)`; `—` until captured.

### Operator checklist before merge

## Summary

Splits the single `professor-synapse/` skill into **two self-contained flavors**, plus a portable self-update mechanism.

The in-process transport (epic #192) deferred `POST /v1/stt/load` as a "Phase 2a follow-up", so a standalone in-process consumer's `preloadModel()` got `unsupportedOperation`. In Yooz Whisper's in-process build (issue #246) this meant the launch-time STT preload failed, `isModelLoaded` stayed false, and dictation gated off — surfaced while validating App Store packaging.

The same lazy `start()` already runs on first `batch`/stream, so this is a pre-warm, not a prerequisite.

author: randyap8-wq
body:
## The problem

On the Mixtral 8x7B run, hit rate tracked the cache fraction almost exactly — 128/256 slots (50%) → **57.7% hit rate** — so streaming from SSD bought nothing over the RAM we paid for. The predictors were inert (locality 0.00%, speculator 0.82% ≈ random `2/256`).

**Root cause (information-theoretic, not a bug):** the benchmark feeds `synth_hidden_state(t) = splitmix64(t, seed)` — every token is an **independent, uniform** random vector. Under a uniform‑i.i.d. access stream the optimal hit rate of *any* cache of capacity `c` over `N` experts is exactly `c/N`, and **no predictor can beat the diagonal**. Worse, chance-accuracy speculation floods a saturated NVMe queue and inflates foreground-miss latency (p50 read 120 ms → 405 ms). Real MoE traces are Zipf-skewed + Markov-correlated; these tiers exploit exactly those two properties.

Every tier is **opt-in**. With defaults unchanged the engine streams bit-for-bit as before (446 tests pass, 1 ignored).

## What's in this PR

| Tier | What | Knobs |
|---|---|---|
| **Harness** | `--workload synthetic\|skewed\|replay` so Tiers 1/3 are falsifiable (Zipf popularity + Markov correlation; or replay a `--trace-out` JSONL). Skewed @ 50% cache ≈ 90% hit vs ~50% wall. | `--workload`, `--zipf-s`, `--workload-correlation`, `--replay-trace` |
| **Tier 1** | Skew-aware **static residency** — pin the hottest fraction (online-derived after warmup, or from a profile) so popular experts are read at most once. | `--static-residency-fraction/-warmup-tokens/-profile`, `--profile-out` |
| **Tier 2** | **Packed expert storage** — one blob + JSON manifest; physically-adjacent experts coalesce into a single vectored `preadv(2)`. New `repack` subcommand. Falls back to per-file retry/breaker path on any short/failed read (byte-identical; integration-tested). | `repack`, `--packed-blob`, `--packed-manifest`, `[storage]` |
| **Tier 3** | Per-layer **pre-gate** — online layer‑L→L+1 conditional drives high-precision next-layer prefetch (multi-layer / replay path). | `--pregate` |
| **Tier 4** | Adaptive **prefetch governor** (throttles low-precision speculation under disk contention — the antidote to the self-inflicted latency above) + **cost-aware eviction** (decaying heat score vs strict LRU). | `--prefetch-governor`, `--prefetch-precision-floor`, `--prefetch-contention-weight`, `--cost-aware-eviction` |

New modules: `residency.rs`, `workload.rs`, `pregate.rs`, `packed_storage.rs`, `prefetch_governor.rs`. Telemetry: gated `governor:` and `pregate:` run-summary lines; legacy summary shape untouched when off.

## Validation
- `cargo build --offline` clean; `cargo test --offline --bin micro-expert-router` → **446 passed, 1 ignored**.
- Tier 2 verified end-to-end via the CLI (`repack` → 128 MiB blob; packed run byte-identical, ~90.7% hit on skewed workload).
- All new flag/config/summary-line names cross-checked against the code.

## Docs
README gains a **"Defeating the cache-fraction wall"** section (root-cause + all four tiers + harness), CLI reference entries (run flags + `repack`), serve-time `[predictive]`/`[storage]` blocks, `config.toml` knobs, TOC, and limitations (incl. the note that Tier 3 only contributes on the multi-layer/replay path).

## Caveats
- Skewed-workload hit-rate figures are cache-simulator results, not full-model inference.
- Tier 3 pre-gate is unit-tested; it needs a `--num-layers > 1` / real-model / replay run to exercise end-to-end (the flat single-namespace benchmark has no next layer to predict).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

author: sdubois777
body:
## Auction live-draft regressions (after the React-resolver release)

Three issues reported live; root-caused and fixed. Extension 77/1, frontend 205, backend 140 router/engine — all green.

### 1. Drafted players never left the available / suggested lists
The React DOM gives an **abbreviated** nominee name ("T. McMillan") + Yahoo's own player id (different id-space than the board's canonical UUID), so `recordPick`'s exact-name/id match found nothing. (Snake works because the backend enriches `snake_pick`; the auction `_record_pick` didn't.)
- **Backend** `_record_pick`: enrich the broadcast payload with the **full name + canonical id + position** (mirrors `_record_snake_pick`).
- **Frontend** `recordPick`: match by id **or `matchesPickName`** (abbreviated-name backstop), like snake.
- **Extension**: the sale now fires when the **nominee leaves the block** (every auction nominee sells at ≥ $1), winner from the team-budget delta or `'unknown'` — instead of only firing when a winner was resolvable (which silently dropped picks).

### 2. Two "you" teams (13 total: "Stephen(You)" + "You")
The poller labels your own card `"You"`, which leaked into `teamsState` and `draft_pick` winners as a phantom team beside `myTeamName`, and your wins weren't booked to you.
- **Extension**: `draft_pick` carries `is_yours` when `winner === "You"`.
- **Frontend**: `recordPick` books your wins to `myTeamName`; `updateTeams` folds the `"You"` budget entry into `myTeamName`. One entry for you again.

### 3. Clock froze after a couple updates — PARTIAL
`NominationPanel` now runs a **local 1s countdown** that resyncs to the extension's clock/bid ticks, so the timer ticks smoothly and never appears frozen between the coarse 5s updates.
**Caveat:** if the extension's clock *read* is itself stale (a frozen value, not just coarse cadence), this band-aid won't fix the source. I need a quick **timer-element capture** to confirm — see ask below.

### Capture I need for #3 (only if the clock still misbehaves after this)
On the live auction page, with a nomination active, paste at ~8s remaining **and** again after it "freezes":
```js
const t=[...document.querySelectorAll('span')].find(s=>/^\d{1,2}:\d{2}$/.test(s.textContent.trim()));
console.log(t && t.outerHTML, '| inDialog', t && !!t.closest('[role=dialog]'));
console.log(t && t.parentElement.outerHTML.slice(0,400));
```
That tells me whether the ticking value lives in a different element than `findLiveTimer` matches.

Extension requires a **rebuild + reload** to take effect.

author: zaingz
body:
## Summary

Levels up the template's production posture while keeping the default install **offline, key-free, and dependency-light**. Every guardrail runs on the `echo` path with no API key or network; all heavy integrations (Redis, real LLM SDKs, vector DBs, tracing) are **docs/recipes + optional extras**, never core deps.

### Core guardrails
- **Security headers** middleware: `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options` + CSP `frame-ancestors`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, conditional **HSTS** (`HSTS_ENABLED`).
- **TrustedHostMiddleware** via typed `ALLOWED_HOSTS` (empty = allow any in dev).
- **Request-size cap** middleware (`MAX_REQUEST_BYTES`) → uniform **413**.
- **Correlation IDs** bound into structlog contextvars **and** every error body (`request_id`), mirroring `X-Request-ID`.
- **One structured access log per request** (`method`, `path`, `status`, `duration_ms`, `request_id`).
- Tighter default CORS `allow_headers`.

### Downstream resilience
- **Lifespan-managed shared `httpx.AsyncClient`** with explicit connect/read/write/pool timeouts and connection limits, exposed via `HttpClientDep`.
- **Upstream error taxonomy** (`UpstreamError`/`UpstreamTimeoutError`/`UpstreamRateLimitError`) + **stdlib retry/backoff** that retries **only** classified transient failures (429/502/503/504, timeouts) with full jitter, honoring `Retry-After`. No blanket `except Exception` retry. (No mandatory `tenacity`/`stamina`; documented as optional upgrade.)

### Rate limiting & seams
- `RateLimiter` Protocol + in-process fixed-window limiter, **disabled by default**; `RateLimitError` → **429 + Retry-After**, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`.
- Recipes: Redis cache + rate limiter, OpenAI/Anthropic/Pydantic AI/LangGraph providers, pgvector/Qdrant `VectorStore` sketch, Prometheus/OTel metrics & tracing — all lazy-import, Protocol-conformant, opt-in extras.

### Observability / ops / CI
- `/health/ready` adds a **bounded** HTTP-client check (no blocking network call).
- CI **security job**: Ruff `S` (flake8-bandit) blocking on first-party code + **advisory `pip-audit`** over the locked deps; explicit `--cov-fail-under=80`.
- New `docs/production.md` (incl. **app-layer vs. edge/CDN DDoS** responsibilities) and updated README / `docs/architecture.md` / `docs/deployment.md` / `.env.example`.

### Anti-bloat / deletion-first notes
- Only one new runtime dep: `httpx` (already pulled in transitively by `fastapi[standard]`), now explicit since runtime code uses it. `redis` is the sole optional extra.
- Chose a stdlib retry helper over adding `tenacity` to keep the default path dependency-free.
- Request-size guard is a `Content-Length` check (not a `receive`-wrapping byte counter) — `ponytail:` note left naming the upgrade path.
- pip-audit is advisory because the locked transitive CVEs require a `fastapi`/`starlette` major bump; triage path documented.

## Test plan
- [x] `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .` clean
- [x] `mypy app/` (strict) clean
- [x] `pytest` — **51 passed**, coverage **93.7%** (floor 80%)
- [x] `ruff check --select S .` clean; `pip-audit` runs against exported lock
- [x] `uv sync --extra redis` resolves
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm advisory-vs-blocking stance on `pip-audit` matches project policy

author: qr-madness
body:
The smooth prose caret (JP-259) was mispositioned on collab docs — rendering ~a line below where it should be, and drifting when scrolling. Diagnosed with temporary instrumentation (since removed) across the prose mount, `healDoubledProse`, and the caret overlay; the real ProseMirror selection was always correct, so both were **overlay positioning** bugs.

## Root causes
1. **Line-offset (collab-only, even offline).** The overlay caret computed its position relative to its host (`.tiptap-editor` / `.ds-caret-host`), but it's absolutely positioned, so the browser resolves it against its nearest **positioned ancestor**. On a local doc that's the host; on a collab doc the host isn't a positioned box, so the true offset parent is an outer layout wrapper (`.document-area-wrapper`) — leaving the caret a constant ~44px (≈ one line) too low. (Offline too: it's the y-prosemirror `Collaboration` binding that differs, not the live cursor.)
2. **Scroll drift.** The caret re-rendered only on ProseMirror updates/resize/pref changes — never on scroll — and the smooth `transform` transition made it float/lag chasing the text.

## Fixes
- **Measure against the caret's actual `offsetParent`** (not the assumed host) — correct in both cases (local's offset parent *is* the host). Show the caret before reading `offsetParent`, since a hidden element reports none.
- **Scroll tracking:** a capture-phase, passive, rAF-throttled scroll listener repositions the caret **instantly** (transition suppressed for that frame). The smooth glide is fully preserved for caret *moves* while typing.
- **Caret color (requested):** a `caretColor` appearance preference + a `ColorField` in Settings → Appearance → Caret. Any CSS color; defaults to the theme text color; the block caret keeps a translucent blend. No store version bump — persist `merge` defaults the new field.
- **Scoped prefs subscription (perf):** the caret re-renders only on caret-relevant pref changes, not every appearance change.

## Verification
- `bun run typecheck` clean; full suite green (198 files / 2579 tests).
- **Live (yours):** on a collab doc (offline is fine) the caret sits exactly on the line; scrolling keeps it glued; the glide still feels right while typing; Settings → Appearance → Caret → Color changes it live.

author: danquirk
body:
## Summary

This PR makes the first Windows-focused cut of the headless gate workflow. The main goal is to make the system usable by a Windows-only developer team without requiring the team or generated agent instructions to know about AXI.

The existing daemon, SQLite state, local git gate, disposable worktree model, pipeline executor, and existing agent adapters are preserved. This PR also adds GitHub Copilot CLI as a native agent backend. AXI remains as a compatibility surface, but the first-class non-interactive workflow is now `no-mistakes gate`.

## What changed

### New `no-mistakes gate` headless surface

- Added a surface-parameterized headless command implementation shared by `gate` and `axi`.
- Added first-class commands:
  - `no-mistakes gate`
  - `no-mistakes gate run --intent ...`
  - `no-mistakes gate respond --action approve|fix|skip`
  - `no-mistakes gate status`
  - `no-mistakes gate logs --step ...`
  - `no-mistakes gate cancel`
- Kept `no-mistakes axi` compatibility, including the existing `axi abort` command and AXI telemetry paths.
- Removed dead AXI-only wrapper functions after the shared headless implementation made them unused.
- Made `gate cancel` report `cancelled` wording while preserving `aborted` wording for `axi abort` compatibility.

### GitHub Copilot CLI adapter

- Added `agent: copilot` as a native backend using the installed `copilot` CLI.
- Copilot runs in non-interactive prompt mode with managed flags for unattended pipeline work, including `--allow-all`, `--no-ask-user`, no remote export, no auto-update, silent output, and hidden Windows subprocess windows.
- The full no-mistakes prompt is written to a temporary prompt file and Copilot receives a short file-reference prompt, avoiding Windows command-line length limits for large review/test prompts.
- Added parser hardening for Copilot prompt-mode output, including stripping prompt bullets and repairing wrapped JSON strings before schema validation.
- Added fakeagent Copilot support so e2e scenarios can exercise the real prompt-file indirection path.

### Neutral control logic

- Added `internal/control` for pure headless gate decisions such as terminal status mapping, active-run matching, CI-ready detection, and auto-resolution of approval gates.
- Moved these decisions out of AXI-specific command ownership so future callers are not coupled to AXI naming.

### Skill and documentation updates

- Updated the generated `/no-mistakes` skill to drive `no-mistakes gate ...` instead of `no-mistakes axi ...`.
- Updated docs so `gate` is the primary headless interface.
- Updated docs/config references for `agent: copilot`.
- Kept AXI documented only as a compatibility alias for older automation.

### Windows subprocess behavior

- Added a small `internal/process.HideWindow` helper.
- Applied hidden-window behavior to high-volume Windows subprocess paths so normal gate usage and e2e validation do not flash command prompts or steal focus:
  - Git subprocesses
  - shell step commands and `taskkill`
  - managed agent servers
  - SCM auth checks
  - doctor checks
  - update background process
  - e2e harness subprocesses
- Added Windows-specific assertions for hidden shell/server subprocess configuration.

### Git for Windows bare-repo handling

- Added explicit bare-repo helpers using `git --git-dir`.
- Switched gate bare-repo config, hook isolation, remote setup, rerun head resolution, and worktree operations away from cwd-based bare-repo assumptions.
- This fixes Git for Windows cases where `git -C <bare>` or cwd-based bare repo commands fail with `safe.bareRepository=explicit` behavior.

### Windows e2e and test hardening

- Added a Windows-safe gate e2e slice for the new command surface.
- Added a `windows-latest` CI job that runs the `Gate` e2e slice.
- Hardened Windows test assumptions that were exposed during validation:
  - e2e fake-agent shims copy `name.exe` when symlink creation is denied.
  - tests no longer require Unix `cp` or `mkdir` commands.
  - symlink-specific tests skip when the host lacks symlink privilege.
  - shell-command tests use cross-platform pass commands instead of Unix `true`.
  - a Windows cancellation timing assertion was relaxed enough to avoid scheduler-noise failures while still catching hangs.

## Validation

Passed locally on Windows with a portable Go 1.25.0 toolchain:

```powershell
go test ./...
go test -tags=e2e -count=1 -timeout 300s ./internal/e2e/... -run Gate
go build -o .\bin\no-mistakes.exe .\cmd\no-mistakes
go run .\cmd\genskill --check
go vet ./...
```

I also dogfooded the change through `no-mistakes gate`. The gate review found and applied follow-up fixes for dead AXI wrappers, `gate cancel` wording, hook-test stubs, Copilot prompt transport, and fake Copilot prompt-file scenario matching. One Copilot follow-up review failed because Copilot returned incomplete/non-JSON output, so the final validation source of truth is the explicit command set above.

## Notes for reviewers

- AXI is intentionally not removed in this PR. It remains as a compatibility adapter over the shared headless implementation.
- The new `gate` surface still uses the existing TOON rendering in this first cut. The important decoupling here is command vocabulary and ownership of the control logic, not an output-format migration.
- `agent: auto` now checks `copilot` after `claude` and before `codex`. Users who want Copilot when Claude is also installed should set `agent: copilot` explicitly.
- The Windows e2e job is intentionally scoped to the `Gate` slice because the broader e2e suite still has known non-Windows assumptions and OpenCode runner flakiness.

author: dotts-h
body:
Closes #41 (issue #0022), under epic #38 (v1.1 — close the deferred remainders). Highest-severity remainder.

## Problem (SECURITY.md RESIDUAL)

`run_spec` executes **model-authored** spec code via `npx playwright test` (full Node), inheriting the full `process.env`. The standards linter blocks *flaky* patterns, not *host-capability* access — so a prompt-injected codifier could author a spec that reads the filesystem, spawns a process, or exfiltrates host secrets.

## Approach (ADR 0010) — defense in depth, portable, no infra

Two layers, pure Node (runs identically on the brain and in CI — no container/Docker dependency):

1. **Capability scan** (`scanSpecCapabilities`) — rejects source importing a dangerous Node core module (`fs`/`child_process`/`net`/`tls`/`http`/…) or using `eval`/`new Function`/`require`/`process.binding`/non-literal `import()`. Comment-aware. Enforced at `write_spec`/`write_pom` **and** re-scanned across every `tests/authored/*.ts` at `run_spec` (so a file placed out-of-band still can't run).
2. **Scrubbed env** (`safeSpecEnv`) — `run_spec` executes under a minimal allowlist (PATH, HOME, X/TMP/locale, `PW_CHANNEL`, `STORAGE_STATE`/`AUTH_STATE`…), forces `RUN_AUTHORED=1`, and drops everything else — closing the secret-exfil leg even if the scan is bypassed.

**Accepted residual:** static scan, not an OS sandbox — authored specs stay *untrusted-until-human-reviewed*; container isolation is the documented future hardening. The env scrub bounds the blast radius regardless.

## Changes

- **`src/spec-guard.mts`** (new) — `scanSpecCapabilities` + `safeSpecEnv`; exported on the public surface.
- **`src/codify-tools.mts`** — `write_spec`/`write_pom` reject capability-violating source; `run_spec` re-scans + runs under `safeSpecEnv`.
- **docs** — ADR 0010 (+ index), SECURITY.md RESIDUAL → HARDENED, #0022 closed.

## Tests

`tests/spec-guard.spec.ts` (14): every dangerous import/escape blocked; clean spec + auth-reuse fixture allowed; comment not tripped; secrets dropped from `safeSpecEnv`.
`tests/codify-depth.spec.ts` (+2): `write_spec` rejects a capability-violating spec (never writes it); `run_spec` blocks a planted file before executing.

Gates: `npm run lint` green; `PW_CHANNEL=chromium npm test` → **177 passed, 10 skipped**. Real-signal check: an existing authored spec passes under a fully scrubbed `env -i` (PATH/HOME/NODE_PATH/PW_CHANNEL/RUN_AUTHORED only).

## Acceptance (#0022)

- [x] Constrained execution: static capability check (write + run) + scrubbed env
- [x] ADR 0010 records the decision + trade-offs
- [x] Deterministic tests: host fs/network/eval rejected; legit spec still green
- [x] SECURITY.md updated; lint + test green

author: mrie04
body:
## What

When sales order candidates that belong to one external order (same external system + external header reference) carry **different delivery dates**, build **one** sales order whose **lines keep their own delivery date** (header = earliest), and make the "ship/pick after above date" flags hold **each line until its own date**. System-wide (no config gate).

## Changes

- **Aggregation** — drop `DatePromised` from the order-split key (`DefaultGroupingProvider`, `OLCandProcessingHelper`): candidates of one external order that differ only by delivery date no longer split into multiple orders (which also removes the `C_Order_ExternalHeader_ID` unique-index crash that the split caused).
- **Per-line date** — `OLCandOrderFactory`: each `C_OrderLine` keeps its source candidate's `DatePromised`; the `C_Order` header is set to the earliest of the lines. Sequenced so `MOrder.afterSave`'s header→lines broadcast does not clobber the per-line dates.
- **Ship flag** (`C_Order.IsFixedDatePromised`) — the two enforcement filters compare the per-line `M_Packageable_V.DeliveryDate` instead of the header `DatePromised` (`PackagingDAO`, `ShipmentService`). Java-only (the view column already exists).
- **Pick flag** (`C_Order.IsFixedPreparationDate`) — per-line preparation date: `OrderDeliveryDayBL` is refactored to expose a per-delivery-date preparation-date computation (the same tour / no-tour-fallback / offset / sysconfig logic that produces today's header value), called per-line by `ShipmentScheduleOrderReferenceProvider`. Single-date orders are byte-identical to before (no regression).
- **Migration** — `AD_Index_Table` record for the existing `C_Order_ExternalHeader_ID` unique index with a translated (DE/EN/FR) `ErrorMsg`, so a forced-split conflict (candidates sharing an external header reference but forced apart by another field) surfaces a clear, translatable message instead of the generic fallback. Gated automatically by the index's `WHERE ExternalId IS NOT NULL`.

## Tests

Cucumber coverage for: multi-date candidates → one order with per-line dates and earliest header; ship-after-date holding each line by its own delivery date; pick-after-date holding each line by its own preparation date; single-date no-regression. Behaviour verified RED→GREEN on CI.
