author: webeferen
body:
## What
A paired phone was permanently stuck on a full-screen **"Connecting to your Mac…"** spinner with no way to reach settings or re-pair. Root cause is architectural: `app/index.tsx` gated the **entire** UI behind the gateway transport, and the drawer — the only path to Account / re-pair / settings — was mounted *inside* `<Chat/>`, which only renders once connected. Since the desktop gateway is now on-demand and **off by default** (#316, never auto-resumes at boot), a paired phone routinely can't connect on launch → infinite spinner → zero reachable config.

PR #320's 6s `ReconnectScreen` just bolted onto the same gate. This removes the gate entirely.

## Rebuild
The app shell now **always renders once a gateway is paired**, connected or not:

- **Token-gated entry** (`app/index.tsx`): neutral backdrop only while storage is read (sub-second), `Onboarding` when nothing is stored, otherwise the full shell. No blocking gateway loader.
- **One derived `connectionState` model** drives an inline header status chip + a **non-blocking banner** (Reconnect + Settings) when the bridge is down. Ordinary chat-history loading still runs once the gateway is connected (kept by request).
- **Always-reachable config**: a `ConnectionSheet` (tap the header status, or the banner's Settings) and the always-available drawer → Account expose **Reconnect / Re-pair / Disconnect** plus guidance to enable the gateway on the Mac.
- **`usePairing.reconnect()`**: a non-destructive re-arm (keeps the stored pairing, unlike `disconnect()`), and the bridge re-arms automatically when the app returns to the foreground — so opening the app after enabling the Mac gateway just connects.
- **Deleted** the blocking loaders `SplashScreen`, `ReconnectScreen`, `ConnectingView`, `reconnectUi`, and the now-superseded `chatConnectionUi` (+ their tests).

## Scope (confirmed with maintainer)
- **Mobile-only** — the desktop gateway stays on-demand; the app handles "gateway off" gracefully with clear guidance rather than forcing a desktop change.
- Removed only the **gateway/data-tied blocking loaders**; ordinary chat-history loading (when connected) and in-chat streaming cues are kept.

## Verification
- `pnpm --filter @moxxy/workspaces-app typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm --filter @moxxy/workspaces-app test` — 212 passed (added `mobile-connection-state`; removed the dead reconnect/chat-connection tests; updated the layout guard)
- `eslint` on all changed files — clean
- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` (includes #320 + #319)

### Manual to run on device (paired, Mac gateway OFF)
1. Cold-launch → brief neutral backdrop, then the **full shell** (amber dot + status, transcript shows the gateway-off banner + Reconnect/Settings, composer present/read-only). No spinner trap.
2. Drawer opens; Account reachable → theme / Reconnect / Re-pair / Disconnect all work offline.
3. Tap header status → ConnectionSheet opens.
4. Enable the gateway on the Mac, foreground the app (or tap Reconnect) → dot turns green, transcript populates. No onboarding flash.

## Follow-ups (logged in TECH_DEBT)
- Manual paste-a-link pairing (Onboarding) still looks racy (`loadPairing` stores without connecting) — fix when next touching pairing.
- Connection recovery needs a real-device pass (StrictMode double-mount WS-handle close, the desktop #211 lesson).

author: benchaikin
body:
- JSON is a poor format for a file humans hand-edit (no comments, trailing-comma intolerance, noisy quoting); the config is opened in `$EDITOR`/Finder via the GUI and documented as hand-editable, so YAML makes it far more comfortable to read and annotate.
- Keeps everything else identical: the in-memory `PerchConfig` shape, `configSchema`, and the full RPC + hot-reload pipeline are unchanged — this is purely a serialization swap at the file boundary (`perch.json` → `perch.yaml`).
- Doesn't strand existing installs: `loadConfig` falls back to a legacy sibling `perch.json` when `perch.yaml` is absent, and a one-time migration rewrites it as YAML on first boot/write so repos, plugins, theme, and gitBin survive.
- Migration leaves the old `perch.json` in place (safest — it's simply ignored once `perch.yaml` exists).
- `perch config get` still prints JSON (a display choice for an already-parsed object, not the on-disk format).

## What

Two related upgrades to code blocks in the iOS chat:

1. **Expand** — code blocks can now open **full-screen** in a scrollable, pinch-zoomable viewer (syntax highlighting preserved, long lines scroll instead of wrapping). New `ZoomTarget.code` case + `ZoomableCodeView`, routed through the existing tap-to-enlarge zoom surface.
2. **Intuitive copy** — replaced the lone faint floating "Copy" pill with a clear **header bar** on every code block: a language label on the left, and **⤢ Expand** + **Copy** buttons on the right. Copy is also available (prominently) inside the expanded view.

Both are explicit buttons, so reading/scrolling code never triggers them by accident.

## How

- `apps/ios/markdown/entry.mjs` — code blocks render a `.code-toolbar` header (lang + Expand + Copy); new `.code-expand` handler lifts the highlighted `<pre>` + raw text to native via the `enlarge` message (`kind: "code"`). Fixed the copy handler to resolve `<code>` via the `.code-block` ancestor (the button moved into the toolbar).
- `apps/ios/markdown/markdown.css` — `.code-block` container owns the card frame; styled header bar + buttons.
- `Views/MarkdownWebView.swift` — routes `enlarge`/`kind:"code"` to `ContentZoom.code(html:text:)`.
- `Views/ContentZoom.swift` — `ZoomTarget.code`, a Copy button in the full-screen bar (native `UIPasteboard`, uses the raw text), and `ZoomableCodeView`.

`markdown.html` / generated `markdown.css` are gitignored build artifacts — the **renderer source** (`entry.mjs` + source `markdown.css`) and Swift are committed. Regenerate with `node scripts/build-ios-markdown.mjs`. iOS isn't built by CI.

- In-bubble: header bar renders with `SWIFT`/`BASH` language labels + Expand/Copy buttons, highlighting intact (screenshot in PR thread).
- Button payloads asserted via a headless harness: Expand posts `{kind:"code", html:<pre>, text}`; Copy posts the raw code text (this caught & fixed an empty-copy regression).

author: kelby0320
body:
## Summary

init's hand-rolled config front end (Part 4 of slice 4), lib-side and host-tested — per `userspace/init/CLAUDE.md`, init parses TOML itself rather than pulling an ecosystem crate. The mount-*processing* loop (spawn fs-server → Ready → `sys_ns_bind`) stays Part 5 / slice 7; this is the pure front half.

## What's here

- **`init::toml_lite`** — a minimal, line-oriented TOML parser for exactly the subset `docs/spec/init-toml-schema.md` uses:
  - table arrays `[[name]]`, one-level subtables `[name.sub]` (attached to the most recent `[[name]]` element, e.g. `[mount.options]`)
  - scalar values: basic strings (no escapes), decimal integers (`_` separators allowed), booleans
  - whole-line + trailing `#` comments (quote-aware), blank lines
  - returns a `Document` (`array(name) -> &[ArrayEntry]`, each a `Table` + named subtables) or a `ParseError` carrying the 1-based line number
  - unsupported forms (bare `[table]`, deeper nesting, arrays / inline tables / multiline strings) are rejected with a clear error — upgrade if the schema ever needs them
- **`init::manifest`** — validates `[[mount]]` entries into `Vec<MountSpec>` (`fs_server`/`device`/`mount_point`/`mode`/`required_for` required; `mode ∈ {ro, rw}`; `required_for == "boot"`; `mount_point` absolute; `[mount.options]` kept verbatim for the slice-7 Ready handshake) and **topologically sorts by mount-point depth** (shallowest first, stable so equal depths keep file order). Typed `ManifestError` variants for the eventual eshell diagnostics.

## Verification

- `cargo xtask build` (no warnings) / `check-arch` — clean
- `cargo xtask test` — kernel 462, libkern 8, **init 18** (+15: 7 `toml_lite` + 8 `manifest`), 0 failed
- `cargo xtask qemu` — on-target smoke test: init parses an embedded out-of-order sample and prints `/ <- fs-server-ext4`, `/store <- fs-server-xfs` (correctly sorted shallowest-first, via `String`/`Vec` on the bump allocator); all prior demos pass, init reaped

No kernel/ABI change (userspace-only).

## Next

Part 5 — init becomes the real PID 1 (the kernel-boot swap), with the reaping loop and the bootstrap-flow skeleton reading the real `/initramfs/etc/init.toml`.

author: rampage270906
body:
Fixes alignment issue of #161 (Animation issue will be solved via another PR)
Previously, all animation modes rendered bitmap content starting at column 0, causing short text to appear left-aligned on the display regardless of the mode selected. This was especially noticeable in Fixed, Laser, Snowflake, and Scroll Up/Down modes where content visually sits in one place and should be centered.

Changes:
- still(): now computes content width and applies a horizontal offset to center content when it doesn't fill the full 44-column display width
- get_x_offset(): new helper that computes the centering offset for a given frame, returns 0 for full-width content so clipart is unaffected
- ani_shift_y(): updated to apply x_offset so scroll up/down center content horizontally during all phases (in, still, out)
- laser_in() / laser_out(): updated to accept and apply x_offset so the laser reveal/collapse animation operates around the centred position
- snowflake_in() / snowflake_out(): updated similarly so the vertical effect is centered horizontally
- ani_laser() / ani_snowflake(): updated to compute x_offset once per frame and pass it through to their sub-functions

Behaviour:
- Short text is now centered for: Fixed, Animation, Scroll Up, Scroll Down, Laser, Snowflake
- Full-width clipart is unaffected (x_offset is 0 when content_width == LED_COLS)
- Scroll Left/Right and Picture modes are unchanged as centering does not apply to their rendering logic

author: brianlane
body:
## Summary

- **Adds a Deno typecheck CI gate** for the Supabase edge functions. The repo-root `tsc --noEmit` excludes `supabase/functions` (it can't resolve the Deno `https://` URL imports), so the app typecheck has never caught missing exports or type breakage in the edge functions — the exact blind spot that boot-crashed `ai-flow-worker` in prod (a removed export compiled fine for the app but threw a `SyntaxError` at module boot in Deno). New `deno-check` job runs `deno check` on every function entrypoint (Deno v2.8.3), transitively type-checking each function + its `_shared` deps the way the Supabase CLI bundles at deploy.
- **Fixes all 133 pre-existing strict type errors** so the gate is green. All changes are types/guards — no runtime behavior change.

## Fixes by category

- **Structural client interfaces** (`telemetry` `RpcSupabase`, `chat_spend_cap` `SpendSupabase`, `ai_flows/compliance` `ComplianceRpcClient`, `telnyx_edge_guard` `RpcSupabase`): `rpc()`/`maybeSingle()` now return `PromiseLike` instead of `Promise`, so supabase-js's thenable `PostgrestFilterBuilder` satisfies them structurally — same approach already documented in `cap_alerts.ts`.
- **`SpendSupabase` builder shape**: split the flat `QueryBuilder` into a `from() -> {select, update}` stage plus a `FilterBuilder` stage so the real two-stage `PostgrestQueryBuilder` is assignable.
- **`ReturnType<typeof createClient>` mismatch**: that resolves to `SupabaseClient<unknown, never, GenericSchema>`, which the real `createClient()` value (`SupabaseClient<any, "public", any>`) is **not** assignable to. Helper params/aliases now use a permissive `SupabaseClient<any, any, any>`.
- **`sms-inbound-worker`**: fixed narrowing broken by `x as string | null` casts (`cfg`/`tset` possibly null) and widened a `GenericStringError` cast via `unknown`.
- **`ai-flow-worker` send_sms**: guards `cfg.from` before passing it where a non-optional `fromE164: string` is required.

## Test plan

- [x] `deno check supabase/functions/*/index.ts` — 0 errors (was 133)
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — passes
- [x] `npm run lint` — passes
- [x] `npm run test` — 4386 tests pass, 100% coverage
- [ ] CI `Edge Functions Typecheck (Deno)` job green
- [ ] Bugbot review clean

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes are mostly type-only and CI; the group MMS guard clarifies existing behavior (fail without MMS-enabled sender) rather than broad runtime refactors.
> 
> **Overview**
> **CI** adds an **Edge Functions Typecheck (Deno)** job that runs `deno check supabase/functions/*/index.ts` (Deno v2.8.3), closing the gap where root `tsc` never type-checks `supabase/functions` because of Deno `https://` imports.
> 
> **Shared `_shared` types** are adjusted so the real supabase-js client structurally satisfies them: `rpc()` / `maybeSingle()` return **`PromiseLike`** instead of **`Promise`** (aligned with `cap_alerts.ts`), and **`SpendSupabase`** models the two-stage **`from()` → select/update → filters** builder instead of a flat query interface.
> 
> **Edge function entrypoints** replace **`ReturnType<typeof createClient>`** with **`SupabaseClient<any, any, any>`** for helper params, because `ReturnType` resolves to generics that are not assignable from the actual client instance.
> 
> **`ai-flow-worker` group SMS** requires a configured **`from`** only for multi-recipient group MMS (uses trimmed **`own`** for the guard and **`telnyxSendGroupMms`**); 1:1 sends may still omit `from` and use the profile pool.
> 
> **`sms-inbound-worker`** gets small narrowing/cast fixes for optional config rows and memory row typing.
>

author: chickendude
body:
Closes the last gap in the offline story (follow-up #1): **reading offline now saves your place.** Before, progress writes went straight to the network — lost when offline — and progress couldn't be read back offline either, so a cached text reopened at the top.

## How it works
- **`pending_progress` table (DB v4)** — one queued position per text (latest wins).
- **`saveProgress`** — on an online success it clears any stale queued write for that text and flushes the rest; on failure (offline) it **queues** the latest position.
- **`progress`** — online prefers an **unsynced local** position (and flushes the queue so the server catches up); offline **resumes from the queued position**. Once flushed, the server is authoritative again.

Flushing is opportunistic — it happens on the next successful save or on opening a text while online — so there's no background worker.

## Tests
`ReaderRepositoryTest` adds: offline save is queued and read back while offline; the queue flushes to the server on reconnect; a later online save drops a stale queued write. **127 tests, 0 failures; lint clean.**

## Caveat
`pending_progress` lives in the same cache DB, which rebuilds destructively on a schema bump — so an *unsynced* position could be lost if the app updates the DB schema before you reconnect. Rare (offline + unsynced + app update before reconnect); flagging it rather than adding a real migration for the disposable DB.

author: wangxiaoyou1993
body:
## Problem

`MonitorStats.get_pipeline_run_count` can try to load pipelines that belong to other workspaces/repositories in project-platform deployments. That produces noisy "pipeline does not exist" errors when monitor stats include pipeline runs whose schedule repo does not match the active workspace.

The problematic path queried pipeline runs, then looked up pipeline metadata with all-project behavior enabled. That made monitor stats cross workspace boundaries even when the UI was scoped to a specific project.

Fixes #6036.

## Changes

- Make `MonitorStats.repo_path` resolve to the active project repo when project platform is enabled.
- Add a repo-path filter to the shared pipeline-run monitor stats query in project-platform mode.
- Use the scoped repo path for pipeline type lookups instead of searching all project repos.
- Apply the same repo-path scoping to pipeline runtime stats, since it uses the same shared pipeline-run filter.
- Add a regression test that verifies project-platform monitor stats use the active repo path and do not call `Pipeline.get(..., all_projects=True)`.

## Impact

Pipeline monitor stats should only consider runs for the active workspace, avoiding cross-workspace metadata lookups and reducing noisy monitor logs. Standard non-project-platform behavior is unchanged.

## Validation Notes

The new regression test is included for CI, but local execution was blocked by missing Python dependencies in the temp worktree.

## Tests

- `python3 -m py_compile mage_ai/orchestration/monitor/monitor_stats.py mage_ai/tests/orchestration/test_monitor_stats.py`
- unit test could not run locally because this worktree is missing installed dependencies (`python-dateutil`)
- pre-commit hooks run during commit and push

author: wangxiaoyou1993
body:
## Problem

`ensure_file_is_in_project` returned immediately whenever project platform was enabled. That meant API paths that rely on this helper skipped the existing project-directory validation entirely in project-platform mode.

This is the code path called by file and folder APIs before reading, writing, moving, or creating files. In project-platform deployments, the helper still needs to resolve the appropriate project repo for the incoming path, but it should not bypass the containment check.

Fixes #6063.

## Changes

- Remove the project-platform early return from `ensure_file_is_in_project`.
- Keep the existing `get_repo_path(file_path=...)` lookup so project-platform paths are still matched to the correct project repo.
- Continue using the existing absolute-path/commonpath validation to reject paths outside the resolved repo.
- Update the project-platform test coverage so:
  - a file inside the active project repo is accepted
  - a relative path escaping the project is rejected

## Impact

author: wangxiaoyou1993
body:
## Problem

Recent Docker images can resolve to a scipy/numpy combination that crashes during Mage startup on Python 3.10. The reported failure happens while importing scipy through the sklearn-related import chain before the server binds to a port.

The base dependency list currently pins neither scipy nor an upper numpy bound, so Docker/package installs can pick a scipy release that is incompatible with the numpy version installed in the image.

Fixes #6103.

## Changes

- Add `scipy==1.14.1` to the base `requirements.txt` dependency set.
- Keep the change in the base section so it is picked up by:
  - Docker image dependency installation
  - `setup.py` `install_requires`, since `setup.py` reads from `requirements.txt` until `# extras`

## Impact

This forces the image/package install to use the known-good scipy version suggested in the issue, avoiding the startup crash caused by resolving to the newer incompatible scipy version.

## Validation Notes

I did not run a full Docker build locally. The package metadata path was checked to make sure the edited requirements still parse through `setup.py`.

## Tests

- `python3 setup.py --name`
- pre-commit hooks run during commit and push

author: wangxiaoyou1993
body:
## Problem

Renaming callback blocks from the UI can appear to do nothing. The update modal saves through `savePipelineContent`, but that function builds its save payload from regular pipeline blocks by default.

Callback and conditional blocks are stored separately on the pipeline object (`callbacks` and `conditionals`), so an update override for a callback block may never be applied when the save pass only iterates over `blocks`.

Fixes #6110.

## Changes

- Expand `savePipelineContent` to include regular blocks, callback blocks, and conditional blocks when constructing the save payload.
- Deduplicate by block UUID while preserving the existing save ordering behavior.
- Apply block overrides against this combined list so callback block updates, including renames, are included in the outgoing pipeline update.
- Keep the final payload separated into `blocks`, `callbacks`, and `conditionals` as expected by the backend.

## Impact

Callback block rename/update flows now use the same save path as regular block updates while preserving the pipeline payload structure. Conditional blocks are included too because they use the same add-on block storage pattern and would otherwise be vulnerable to the same omission.

## Validation Notes

Frontend dependencies are not installed in the temp worktree, so I could not run the full Next build/type check locally.

author: vibecoderst
body:
## Summary

Adds a **mobile-only pop-out overlay for the performance chart** — the core
open/close lifecycle of milestone #446. On a viewport `< 768px` an expand
control appears on the chart card; tapping it pops the single live
`#performanceChart` canvas out into a full-viewport overlay (`#chartPopout`),
locks background scroll, and resizes the chart to fill the screen. ✕, Esc and
the device back-gesture all close it, restoring the canvas to `.chart-container`
exactly as before. Desktop (`≥ 768px`) never sees the control and is unchanged.

Because there is exactly one Chart.js instance, the overlay **re-parents the
existing canvas** rather than building a second chart, calling
`chart.resize()` / `chart.update()` after each move so the chart fits its new
box. No chart data, the 90/180-day window, or the colour-key/legend logic is
touched (those belong to siblings #452/#453).

Closes #451.

### Contract exposed for the sibling sub-issues
- Overlay container id: `#chartPopout` (with `#chartPopoutBody` hosting the canvas).
- Body state class while open: `body.chart-popout-open`.

### Changes
- **`docs/chart_popout.js`** (new) — dependency-injected open/close engine
  published on `globalThis.GRQChartPopout`. Pure `openPopout`/`closePopout`/
  `togglePopout` core plus `createChartPopout()` wiring (tap, ✕, Esc, and a
  pushed history entry so the back-gesture pops the overlay).
- **`docs/index.html`** — mobile expand button (`#chartPopoutExpand`,
  `aria-label`), the hidden `role="dialog"` overlay with a labelled ✕ close
  button, and the `chart_popout.js` script tag before the app bootstrap.
- **`docs/app.js`** — wires the engine to the live chart via
  `getChart: () => validator.chart`.
- **`docs/styles.css`** — mobile-only trigger (`display:none` at `≥768px`),
  full-viewport overlay, and `body.chart-popout-open { overflow: hidden }`.
- **PWA** — added `./chart_popout.js` to `STATIC_ASSETS` in `docs/sw.js` and
  bumped `APP_VERSION` 1.0.212 → 1.0.213 across `sw.js`, `sw-register.js`,
  `index.html` and `trend.html` so returning mobile users get the new shell.
- **`README.md`** — dashboard feature note + docs file-tree entry.

### Accessibility
- Expand and close controls have `aria-label`s.
- Focus moves to the close button on open and is restored to the trigger on close.
- The overlay is `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`; background scroll is locked
  via the body class.
- `pa11y-ci` stays green: **6/6 URLs, 0 errors**.

## Evidence

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Dashboard
    Dashboard --> Overlay: tap expand (mobile only)\nre-parent canvas → #chartPopout\nadd body.chart-popout-open\nfocus ✕ · chart.resize()
    Overlay --> Dashboard: ✕ / Esc / back-gesture\nrestore canvas → .chart-container\nremove body class\nrestore focus · chart.resize()
```

Mobile chart with the expand control (top-right of the chart):

![Mobile dashboard with the chart expand control](https://github.com/stSoftwareAU/GRQ-validation/raw/76e95671ea4f5501e7b686432ffe0bbd1805faa2/docs/evidence/issue-451-mobile-chart-collapsed.png)

Overlay open — full-viewport chart with the ✕ close control:

![Chart pop-out overlay open](https://github.com/stSoftwareAU/GRQ-validation/raw/76e95671ea4f5501e7b686432ffe0bbd1805faa2/docs/evidence/issue-451-mobile-chart-popout-open.png)

Headless CDP checks confirmed the runtime contract: at 390px the control is
visible (`display:flex`), opening sets `#chartPopout.hidden = false`,
`body.chart-popout-open` is added, and the canvas is re-parented into
`#chartPopoutBody`. At 1200px the control is `display:none` and the overlay
stays hidden.

## Test Plan

- Added **`tests/chart_popout_test.ts`** — 17 Deno tests over the real shipped
  engine using a minimal fake DOM:
  - open: overlay shown, `aria-hidden=false`, `body.chart-popout-open` added,
    canvas re-parented into the overlay, focus → close button, chart
    resized+updated;
  - close: canvas restored to the container, overlay hidden, body class removed,
    focus restored to the trigger, chart resized again;
  - `togglePopout`, no-op guards (open-when-open / close-when-closed), and
    tolerance of a missing chart instance;
  - `createChartPopout()` end-to-end open/close via an injected document;
  - production `docs/chart_popout.js` parses cleanly; `index.html` loads it
    before the bootstrap and exposes the `#chartPopout` / `#chartPopoutExpand`
    contract; `sw.js` precaches it.
- `./quality.sh` passes (cargo fmt/clippy/test/build + 760 Deno tests).
- `pa11y-ci` green (6/6, 0 errors).



## Milestone
This PR is part of the **#446 feat: expand chart to full-screen landscape pop-out on mobile** milestone and targets the `milestone/446-feat-expand-chart-to-full-screen-landscape-pop` feature branch.

body:
Closes #14 (Ollama+CLI scope — see note).

## What
Pass `agentLoopStrategy: maxIterations(8)` to the Ollama chat stream **when tools are present**, so a tool-using prompt runs multiple *bounded* tool round-trips in a single turn rather than one step. Tool-less turns stay single-shot. The existing `tool.call` / `tool.result` trace (name · done/error · `elapsedMs`, in the event-stream view) already surfaces each round, distinct from the answer.

## Scope note (the issue was over-specified)
#14's AC assumed tool support that **only exists on the Ollama+CLI path today**:
- **OpenRouter** drops tools (its custom SSE adapter never parsed tool calls) → split to **#23**.
- **Desktop** chat has no MCP/tools at all; wiring it needs a webview↔bun-side MCP execution bridge → split to **#24** (design-first).

So the net-new here is exactly what the issue called for — the **bounded loop** — on the only surface that has tools. The other two AC paths are now their own prerequisite issues.

## Verification
`bun run check` green: biome · typecheck (5/5) · 95 tests. Runtime multi-step behavior needs a live tool-using model (not AFK-testable), but the loop config is correct + bounded.

## What

The husky `pre-push` hook runs the full unit suite, and two CPU-bound tests intermittently blow Vitest's 5s per-test default when the suite saturates the worker pool, failing the push even though nothing is actually wrong:

- `tests/format/schema-drift.test.ts` regenerates the whole VFPF schema from the TypeScript types.
- `tests/architecture/layer-boundaries.test.ts` constructs a full ESLint flat config (twice, once per test) and lints sample modules.

- Give each slow test an explicit 30s timeout via a named constant.
- Build the layer-boundary suite's `ESLint` instance once for the file instead of once per test, so the expensive flat-config construction happens during collection and no longer counts against either test's clock.

No production code changes; behaviour and assertions are unchanged.

author: alexandrosk0
body:
## Intent

Slice **P1.3** of the Phase-1 Android mobile work (`docs/plans/active/mobile-app-fuller-integration.md`).
Make the grid cell editors usable by touch: a **long-press** opens/arms each editor (touch has no
double-click), and every editor commits on an **explicit Save/Apply** — never on focus-loss — so a
Cancel / Back / tap-away issues **no PUT**. The redesign must keep desktop input **byte-identical**
(Pillar-3 / Risk invariant, plan line 131).

This PR adds the **ImGui glue** that wires the already-unit-tested pure seams (the long-press gate
`52da1075`, the touch-popup commit policy `aeaff745`) into the live editors.

## What changed

New shared header `Source/Core/include/Ui/TouchCellEditGesture.h` exposing two seams:
- `ShouldOpenCellEditorOnGesture(cellClicked, openOnClick)` — the open gesture, consuming the pure
  `ShouldOpenCellEditorByLongPress`.
- `ArmThenPopupCellGate(...)` — the arm-then-popup state-machine + collapsed-preview `Selectable`,
  **extracted** so the four combo/popup editors share one scaffold (not copy-pasted per editor).

`kMobileTouchBuild` (`__ANDROID__`-gated `constexpr bool`) dead-eliminates the touch branch on desktop,
collapsing the gate to the exact pre-existing `clicked && (openOnClick || IsMouseDoubleClicked(0))`.

Wired three TUs:
- **`TicketFieldEditor.cpp`** — replaced the file-local open-helper; routed SingleSelect / MultiSelect /
  Cascading through `ArmThenPopupCellGate` (each keeps its divergent tail); kept `kMobileInlineEditBuild`
  for the inline-text commit policy.
- **`TrackerLabelsEditor.cpp`** — Labels arm site → `ArmThenPopupCellGate`.
- **`TrackerDateTimeFieldEditor.cpp`** — phone-centered modal on touch; Apply / Clear / Cancel / Back
  rewired through the pure `ShouldCommitTouchPopupEdit` / `ShouldCloseTouchPopupEdit`.

## DRY note

The first glue draft *flattened* the combo arm sites inline, which made MultiSelect / Cascading
byte-identical to Labels → the `duplication` gate FAILed (two NEW 103-token clones). Fixed by
**extraction, not exemption** (`ArmThenPopupCellGate`). `dup_audit.py --diff origin/develop` → exit 0.

## Verification

- **Build** — desktop dual-target (`SmatchetStandalone` + `SmatchetCore_DX12`, clean link) + Android
  x86_64 `assembleDebug` → `app-debug.apk` 54.6 MB.
- **Lint** — `test-lint-rules.sh --diff origin/develop` green, incl. the **strict zone**
  `Source/Core/src/Tracker/`.
- **Emulator (`-s emulator-5554` pinned; physical device never coordinate-injected)** — inline-text
  long-press → `EditLongText` modal → `Escape` → **zero** mutation tag; SingleSelect long-press → combo
  opens → tap-away → cell reverts, **zero** mutation tag.
- **Held for explicit user confirmation** — the live Save → PUT against a real ticket was **not**
  exercised (external-service mutation). It is the first item of the visual-validation pause.
- **Deferred** — full five-editor open/commit/discard matrix backlogged as bucket-E (ImGui Test Engine),
  CI-blocked on the Mesa-GL lane: `docs/self-improvement/categories/test/2026-06-23-mobile-touch-editors-bucket-e.md`.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes when tracker field PUTs fire on mobile (discard vs commit) across multiple editors; desktop paths are constexpr-gated to prior behavior, with policy covered by new unit tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **P1.3 mobile grid editing**: Android opens cell editors via **long-press** (not click/double-click) and popup editors commit only on explicit **Save/Apply**, with Cancel/Back/tap-away discarding without a PUT.
> 
> Introduces **`Ui/TouchCellEditGesture.h`** with `ShouldOpenCellEditorOnGesture` and shared **`ArmThenPopupCellGate`**, wired from **`TicketFieldEditor.cpp`** (inline text + Single/Multi/Cascading combos), **`TrackerLabelsEditor.cpp`**, and **`TrackerDateTimeFieldEditor.cpp`** (touch-centered picker modal + canonical date equality before queueing). **`TicketFieldEditorCommitPolicyPure.h`** gains unit-testable predicates for long-press, touch-popup commit, and close; **`TicketFieldEditorCommitPolicyPure.test.cpp`** expands coverage. author: oxyc
body:
A `group|`-purge Kinsta invalidator, mirroring the Fastly hard/soft pair (base + one override).

### Why
[`kinsta-mu-plugins`](https://github.com/generoi/kinsta-mu-plugins) resolves purge URLs two ways: `single|` (exact URL) and `group|` (string-prefix wildcard — clears the URL and everything beneath it, proven by its `sitemap`/`feed` group entries). A `group|` purge of `/shop/` therefore clears `/shop/`, `/shop/page/2/`, **and** `/shop/?orderby=…` in one request.

### What
- **`KinstaCacheInvalidator`** (base) — unchanged behavior (`single|`, exact), refactored to an overridable `purgeKey()` + a testable `purgeList()`.
- **`KinstaGroupCacheInvalidator`** (new, recommended) — purges by `group|`, and disables `cachetags/store-query-string` so the store keys bare paths. A path prefix-purge already clears every query-string/pagination variant, so per-query store rows aren't needed. The site root (`/`) is always purged `single|`, so a group purge never flushes the whole site (trailing slashes keep `/shop/` from matching `/shopping/`).

### Relationship to #30 / #32
This is the **cleaner fix for the Kinsta fleet**: path-only storage + prefix purge clears all variants, with none of the store-growth that full-URL storage (#32) brings on Kinsta. #32 (full URL + `single|`) remains the tool for exact-match caches that cache query strings (SiteGround, or Kinsta set to cache GET params).

3 dedicated tests; full suite 117 green.

body:
## Problem

Tenant pod `listings-ingest-tenant-pool-0-0` stuck in `Init:ImagePullBackOff`:

```
Pulling image "registry1.dso.mil/ironbank/opensource/minio/operator-sidecar:v7.0.1"
Unable to retrieve some image pull secrets (private-registry)
```

The MinIO Operator injects a sidecar init container into every tenant pod. The sidecar image defaults to the IronBank registry and was not covered by the existing image overrides.

## Fix

Adds `upstream.operator.sidecarImage` override in `values-minio-operator.yaml`:

```
registry1.dso.mil/ironbank/opensource/minio/operator-sidecar:v7.0.1
  -> quay.io/minio/operator:v7.0.1
```

## Outstanding (Vault secret — operator action required)

The `minio-root-credentials` ExternalSecret is also failing:

```
error processing spec.data[0] (key: platform/minio/root), err: Secret does not exist
```

The Vault path `platform/minio/root` needs to be populated with `accesskey` and `secretkey` before the Tenant can initialize. Run via Vault CLI or UI:

```
vault kv put secret/platform/minio/root accesskey=<value> secretkey=<value>
```

- gitops PR #319

author: anatissera
body:
## Summary

Three integrated phases bring the Claude CLI from ephemeral terminal-bound sessions to persistent, remote-controllable multi-model workflows:

1. **Guard hardening** (agent security)
   - Merged denylist covering credentials, destructive filesystem ops, fork bombs
   - Path confinement for Write/Edit/MultiEdit tools (reject writes outside project root)
   - Proxy TCP preflight (fail fast, not opaque SDK timeout)
   - Cost logging in result summary

2. **Persistent tmux + remote ttyd** (session survivability)
   - `./scripts/cc-up.sh <name>`: launch or reattach persistent tmux session
   - `./scripts/cc-remote.sh <name> [port]`: expose session over ttyd, bound to Tailscale only
   - Works from mobile browsers, survives disconnects

3. **Model switching with context handoff** (multi-LLM flexibility)
   - `./scripts/cc-switch.sh <session> <model>`: switch backends mid-workflow
   - Requests brief handoff summary from outgoing model (optional, fails gracefully)
   - Relaunches on new model with --continue (full transcript replay)

## Test plan

### Agent hardening (unit tests)
- Run: npm test in agent/ directory
- Expected: 29/29 tests pass (including 9 new path guard tests)

### Session management (manual)
1. Install tmux/ttyd: sudo apt install -y tmux ttyd
2. Ensure Tailscale is up: tailscale up && tailscale ip -4
3. Start a session: ./scripts/cc-up.sh demo glm
4. Expose it: ./scripts/cc-remote.sh demo

Every Dependabot PR fails `DCO Check`: the bot's commit author email is `49699333+dependabot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com` but its `Signed-off-by` trailer uses `support@github.com`. `dco-check` requires those to match, so it fails all bot PRs unconditionally — a rebase cannot fix it. author: jalehman
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Path 3 is moving session and transcript state toward SQLite-backed storage, but compaction checkpoint branch/restore still had storage mutation logic coupled directly to file-backed store helpers. This PR narrows that boundary so checkpoint branch/restore owns transcript fork/copy plus session-entry metadata mutation as one domain store operation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The future SQLite implementation needs to copy transcript rows and update `session_entries.entry_json` inside one write transaction. Routing the current file-backed implementation through `CompactionCheckpointStore` and session-accessor operations preserves today's behavior while making the intended transaction boundary explicit for the SQLite-backed store.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change is intended. Existing compaction checkpoint list/get/branch/restore behavior continues to fork from the stored checkpoint boundary and persist branch/restore session metadata; the change is internal migration preparation for openclaw/openclaw#88838.

## Evidence

- `pnpm lint:tmp:session-accessor-boundary` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts src/gateway/session-compaction-checkpoints.test.ts test/scripts/check-session-accessor-boundary.test.ts` passed: 28 unit-fast tests, 64 gateway tests, 49 runtime-config tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src` passed.
- Autoreview clean against `upstream/main`: no accepted/actionable findings.
- Real behavior proof completed on live local gateway from `/Users/phaedrus/Projects/clawdbot` using head `2f40aabd3e5` before the non-live rebase follow-up.
- Non-live mergeability follow-up completed after `upstream/main` advanced to `c70accc86f8`: branch rebased to `4c3d1f83ce0`, local `merge-base HEAD upstream/main` equals `c70accc86f8`, and local `git merge-tree` reports no conflicts.
- Rebase conflicts were limited to accessor ratchet/test overlap from landed Path 3 slices; resolution kept both current-main entries and this compaction checkpoint slice.
- Post-rebase proof passed: `pnpm lint:tmp:session-accessor-boundary`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts src/gateway/session-compaction-checkpoints.test.ts test/scripts/check-session-accessor-boundary.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, and autoreview against `upstream/main`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: compaction checkpoint branch/restore storage boundary, including transcript fork/copy from a stored checkpoint boundary and session-entry metadata persistence through the accessor-backed store operation.

Real environment tested: live local OpenClaw gateway in `/Users/phaedrus/Projects/clawdbot`, loopback gateway on port 18789, agent `main`, synthetic temporary proof session only.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Preflight and exact build
pnpm openclaw tasks list --status running --json
# -> { "count": 0, "tasks": [] }
git checkout --detach 2f40aabd3e5ab63763691adc2c4c54dbaed01d62
pnpm build
pnpm openclaw gateway restart
pnpm openclaw --version
# -> OpenClaw 2026.6.9 (2f40aab)
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:18789/readyz
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:18789/healthz

# Synthetic proof fixture, created through SessionManager, not raw JSONL message writes
# source key: agent:main:path3-checkpoint-proof-rebased-20260623164953-30482
# checkpoint: c9b07ac6-eece-4a07-9e9d-dc56193a6cfd
# pre-compaction leaf: 8a38d197
# post-compaction checkpoint leaf: 3d251843

pnpm openclaw gateway call sessions.compaction.list --json \
  --params '{"key":"agent:main:path3-checkpoint-proof-rebased-20260623164953-30482","agentId":"main"}' \
  --timeout 20000

pnpm openclaw gateway call sessions.compaction.branch --json \
  --params '{"key":"agent:main:path3-checkpoint-proof-rebased-20260623164953-30482","checkpointId":"c9b07ac6-eece-4a07-9e9d-dc56193a6cfd","agentId":"main"}' \
  --timeout 20000

pnpm openclaw gateway call sessions.compaction.restore --json \
  --params '{"key":"agent:main:path3-checkpoint-proof-rebased-20260623164953-30482","checkpointId":"c9b07ac6-eece-4a07-9e9d-dc56193a6cfd","agentId":"main"}' \
  --timeout 20000
```

Evidence after fix:

- `sessions.compaction.list` returned `ok: true` with the synthetic checkpoint.
- `sessions.compaction.branch` returned `ok: true`, branch key `agent:main:dashboard:a0d9bba0-926c-42ec-8114-f877bd608359`, branch session id `9ad7d9d2-1f06-4b36-b564-10731e7a7234`, parent session key `agent:main:path3-checkpoint-proof-rebased-20260623164953-30482`, and `totalTokens: 34` / `totalTokensFresh: true`.
- `sessions.compaction.restore` returned `ok: true`, restored session id `fe11b495-db40-4605-a2e6-fa81010475fb`, preserved one checkpoint in the restored entry, and persisted `totalTokens: 34` / `totalTokensFresh: true`.
- Verification script read `sessions.json` and both generated transcript files. The branch and restore transcripts contained `PATH3_CHECKPOINT_SOURCE path3-checkpoint-proof-rebased-20260623164953-30482`, did not contain `PATH3_CHECKPOINT_FUTURE path3-checkpoint-proof-rebased-20260623164953-30482`, and the store entry matched the restored session id/file.

What was not tested: SQLite-backed session/transcript storage is not enabled yet, so this proof covers the current file-backed store implementation and the intended transaction/accessor boundary only. 💡 What: Optimized the `apply_edge_shift` morphological operator (erode/dilate) in `prunr-core`.

body:
## Phase P10 PR1 — forecast-suite hardening (remediation gap #10)

Fixes the red forecast suite via five mechanical groups. **`pytest -k forecast`: 88 → 35 failing · 53 fixed · zero new regressions.** No schema, no hb_assistant product-code change.

### Groups
- **D (P4b regression, `55b992ae`):** the 4 bare-file generators ran a relative `from ..common.project_config import ...` reached under `__main__`, which fails when the script runs as a bare-file subprocess. Converted to absolute imports (matching each file's existing `sys.path` bootstrap). Unblocked the phase6–13 cascade. *(Corrects the earlier "CFR not importable" framing — the real cause was this relative import.)*
- **E (revealed by D):** 7 tests asserting the old `"unsupported project_key"` → `"not eligible"` (P4 eligibility message drift).
- **B:** 6 forecast tests track `LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` instead of hardcoded `== 61`; left the intentional v61 backward-compat fixture (`test_forecast_runtime_config.py:219`).
- **C:** the 2 `unconfigured→503` tests monkeypatch the source-module resolver to `None` (true unconfigured-runtime isolation).
- **A:** evidence script uses the repo venv interpreter (`VENV_PYTHON`) instead of bare `python3`; the 2 evidence-script tests pass `sys.executable`.

### Residual (documented, not bundled)
The remaining 35 failures are **pre-existing** (in the clean-`main` baseline) and **unmasked** — not caused — by the Group-D fix (those tests previously died at the relative import). They are 4 distinct, multi-subsystem root causes (`project_display_name` KeyError; `_run_comprehensive` missing `project_key`; proof perturb-callback `project_key`; launcher `HB_FORECAST_EVAL_ROOT`), documented in the evidence bundle for a focused follow-up. PR2 (forecast-correctness VALUE tests) can seed from these.

### Gates
Plan-gate review (REVISE→resolved: added the 4th generator), diff auditor PASS, ruff-clean on changed files, ADR 304 + evidence bundle. Ledger: P3→merged/#109, P10→in-review.

author: jeffdafoe
body:
## Problem
Josiah Thorne (NPC merchant) closed his shop for **4 hours mid-shift** after a *mild* "You feel tired." cue (tiredness ≈8 of 24). Traced live via the umbilical: the deliberation prompt rendered a bare adjective, the model called `take_break` with no `until_hour` → the fixed 4h default, and a competing "return to your post" steer walked him back to his stall — asleep at his post during working hours, for a barely-elevated need.

## Change
Four coupled changes so tiredness reads proportionately (cues over compulsion — render the situation, let the model choose):

1. **Awareness floor `needSilentFloor` 8 → 10** (all needs): 8–9 of 24 isn't worth a cue.
2. **Tiredness "weary" threshold 20 → 16**: the mild "a little tired" band no longer spans most of a working day. (Also lowers the warrant/red-backstop trigger to 16 — the same constant drives labeling and actionability; intended.)
3. **`take_break` default 4h → 2h** (omitted `until_hour`): a daytime top-up (~4.8 tiredness at the 2.4/h recovery rate), not a half-reset that shutters the shop a third of the day. `until_hour` still honored for a longer rest.
4. **Tiredness renders its own situated, descriptive line** (`renderTiredness`), pulled out of `renderFeltNeeds` (now hunger/thirst only), anchored to real hours awake:
   - 10–15: `You're starting to feel a little tired — you've been awake for X hours.`
   - 16–23: `You're weary — …`
   - 24: `You're exhausted — …`
   No "Address now" imperative at any tier — the actionable rest affordances live in the "## How you can rest" menu. This completes LLM-67, which suppressed that imperative only while resting.

`computeHoursAwake` derives X at build time from the snapshot clock − the actor's shift-start, **gated on on-shift** (where wakefulness-since-shift-start is guaranteed); off-shift / unscheduled / clock-less → tail dropped. Wrap-midnight shifts handled via modulo.

## Verification
- Full engine suite passes uncached; gofmt + vet clean.
- Prod has **no `tiredness_red_threshold` settings row**, so the default change is effective (not inert).
- Reviewed by code_review (GPT-5.4): flagged the off-shift hours-awake overstatement (fixed via the on-shift gate, commit `35d82f7`); confirmed the rest sound.

Closes LLM-85.

author: alexeiveselov92
body:
## Summary

Make the `dtk autotune --label` incident labeler genuinely usable on real series and persist labels properly, plus showcase it on the landing. Follow-up to #38. Version **0.21.0 → 0.22.0**; 734 unit tests pass; website builds.

## Labeler (`dtk autotune --label`)

- **Zoom + pan** so narrow incidents are markable even on a long span with a small step: **scroll to zoom** at the cursor, **double-click** to reset, and a **navigator strip** below the chart — drag the window to pan, drag its edges to **stretch/squeeze** (Ableton-style). No conflict with click-drag marking.
- **Min/max decimation** keeps a 100k-point series fast and spike-faithful at any zoom.
- **Per-incident description** field, exported as the canonical `label:`.
- **Versioned, never-overwriting export** `<metric>-<UTC>.yml` — a browser can't write into the project, so keep every labeling round under `incidents/<metric>/`.
- Restyled on the detectkit brand (palette/fonts/logo, axes + ticks + gridlines, hover tooltip, live summary, responsive).

## Directory-aware label resolution

- `--incidents` (and `autotune.labels_file`) may point at a **directory**; the newest versioned file is used. So `dtk autotune --select <m> --incidents incidents/<m>/` always tunes on the latest labels while the full history stays on disk. (`_newest_labels_file`, tests added.)

author: paulmanoni
body:
## Summary
Custom (dotted) decorators like `//@inertia.Page` previously **rejected** modifier annotations — adding `//@auth Required` produced `//@pkg.Func … does not accept modifier annotations`, which skipped the **entire package's** codegen (un-registering every annotated handler in it). That, in an Inertia app, surfaced downstream as the `@inertiajs/vue3` error modal (a `srcdoc` iframe) with CORS / "Module source URI is not allowed" noise — because the route silently stopped registering.

Now modifiers are **appended as trailing options** to the custom registrar call:

```go
//@auth Required
//@inertia.Page "GET" "/admin" "Admin/Index"
func NewAdmin(...) (AdminProps, error)
```
emits
```go
inertia.Page("GET", "/admin", "Admin/Index", NewAdmin, auth.Required())
```

`inertia.Page` takes `...nexus.RestOption`, which `auth.Required()` satisfies. If a registrar doesn't accept the option type, it's a compile error — the right, loud failure (vs. a silently dropped package).

## Changes
- `internal/handlergen/emit.go`: `optsAllowed` returns true for dotted keywords; `renderPrimary`'s custom-decorator branch appends `optTail`.
- `internal/handlergen/emit_test.go`: the reject test flipped to assert the appended option + auth import.
- Docs: `inertia` docs topic and `decorate/DESIGN.md` updated.

## Validation
- `internal/handlergen`, `cmd/nexus`, `decorate` suites green; `go build ./...` + `go vet` clean.
- End-to-end on a real Inertia app: `//@auth Required` above `//@inertia.Page` now produces **no** codegen skip and the page registers (with auth) — verified via the live `/__nexus` manifest.

Follow-up to #31/#32. The companion nexus-zed LSP `custom-no-modifier` diagnostic is updated separately.

author: ttupper92618
body:
## What

Closes #388. When the master recovers a node that could not pull its shard or whose download failed (#381), the *reason* was invisible: the node looked normal in the topology while placements quietly routed around it. This surfaces a derived per-node health summary so the recovery is legible, with the **fix** shown alongside each problem.

## Backend

`GET /state` now carries a `nodeHealth` map (per live node):

```json
"nodeHealth": {
  "<node-id>": {
    "level": "ok" | "warn" | "error",
    "reasons": [{ "code": "...", "message": "...", "remediation": "..." }]
  }
}
```

It is a pure, read-only derivation (`src/skulk/api/node_health.py`, `compute_node_health`) over state already in the `/state` response — **no new gossip type, command, or state field, and no new polling**:

- **download_failed** (error) — a terminal `DownloadFailed` in `State.downloads`; pairs with the #381 recovery so the operator sees *why* an instance was re-placed off this node.
- **disk_low** (warn) / **disk_full** (error) — models-volume free space from `TelemetryView.node_disk`; pre-emptive, warns before a download fails.
- **unreachable** (warn) — `State.last_seen` heartbeat staleness approaching the 30s prune.

`placement_refused` (#290) is intentionally **not** surfaced: refusals are ephemeral commands (the master deletes + re-places), not in replicated `State`, so it would need a new state field — out of this read-only scope.

## Dashboard

An amber (warn) / red (error) alert badge on the affected topology node; hover names the problem **and** its remediation. Also wraps Storybook in the Tolgee provider (existing i18n-using stories were silently broken without it) and adds two health story variants.

body:
## What & why

Two behavioral gaps in the handler-level test suite are closed:

1. **All five XML special characters in one `buildSuggestions` call.** Existing tests covered the five entities in pairs across two tests (`&`, `"`, `<` in one; `'`, `>` in another), but never exercised all five together in a single call. A single-pass regex bug that only misfired with multiple simultaneous special characters in one string could have gone undetected. The new test uses `"a & <b> 'c' \"d\""` to assert both that `content` stays raw and that `description` escapes all five correctly.

The handler was only tested with `""` and plain queries — whitespace-only was tested at the `buildSuggestions` level but not at the full handler→suggest-callback level. author: weningerii
body:
## Connector `set_preface` was auto-selecting borrowed materials

While verifying the Render-hosted MCP connector after the wood/strings + cascade work, I found a real connector bug.

The universal cross-instrument materials are `auto:false` — a human picks them; the inverse-configure optimizer must **never** reach for one on its own. The browser fix for this (#66) only touched `src/app.js`'s `inverseConfigureForPreface`. But the **connector and CLI** use the shared SSOT `scripts/_inverse_configure.js` (explicitly *"a port of"* the browser function, meant to be identical), which still offered **every** variant to the optimizer.

**Result:** `set_preface` on the deployed connector auto-picked a borrowed material in **~77% of (instrument, preface) cases** (3684/4800 in a local sweep) — e.g. a 12-string electric getting `pipa_steel_nylon` strings, or an electric guitar getting `adirondack` (an acoustic top wood) as its body wood. Recipes the app would never produce.

**Why CI missed it:** `check_app_parity` only compares **default seed + render** between app and connector — it never exercises `inverse-configure` / `set_preface`, so the drift between the two implementations slipped through.

### Fix
Port the exact app-side fix to the SSOT (`scripts/_inverse_configure.js`):
- Each part axis offers only its **curated** variants (keeping the current pick even if it's already a borrowed material, so a prior human choice is preserved, not dropped).
- Mirror `app.js`'s `opts.pin` so the two implementations stay aligned.

### Guard (so it can't regress)
New check in `mcp/test.mjs` (runs under `test:connector` → `npm test` → CI) drives the **real connector engine**: `set_preface` across afrobeat's material instruments × several prefaces, asserting it never lands on an expanded variant. **Verified it fails on the pre-fix code** (catches `body_wood=adirondack` on an electric guitar) and passes after.

### Scope / safety
Connector-only — `codex.html` and `src/app.js` untouched, recipes **1198/1198 byte-identical**, `api/` unchanged (the static API serves *default* recipes, not inverse-configured ones). Render auto-deploys from `main`.

### Also verified in this pass (no change needed)
All 9 live connector tools work (`start_recipe`, `edit_recipe`, `render_recipe`, `search_catalog`, `search_prefaces`, `get_instrument`, `get_tradition`, `list_traditions`, `list_options`), and Render is **caught up** — the live afrobeat recipe is byte-identical to the current-main engine, and catalog counts match (1119 traditions / 419 instruments / 649 prefaces).

author: vdorie
body:
## Summary

Redesign the home page so a single shared file drop serves both starting paths -- inviting a partner and accepting an invitation -- instead of burying the drop inside the invite panel. The inviter sees the chosen file's default exchange columns and an Advanced Options control beside Generate; the acceptor can drop a file up front and have it carried to the consent screen. This removes the odd "no file -> Advanced -> file -> Advanced" gate and the duplicate Advanced link, and stops an invite-side disclosure from popping up when the operator only means to accept.

## Changes

- HomePage: lift the file selection here and render one shared drop below both compose panels; clamp it to the exchange reading width (centered, fills a narrow window, gaps on a wide one); render the relocated default-columns disclosure under the drop; keep dropping the grid, accept form, and drop on the post-generate takeover.
- InvitePanel: take the file as a prop instead of owning the dropzone; add an "Advanced Options" secondary button to the left of "Generate invitation" on one row, both disabled until a file is chosen.
- DefaultExchangeColumns (new): the "Default exchange columns" awareness surface (relabeled from "What you will send"), shown under the shared drop; derived from the same predicate the wire transmits on, in a polite atomic live region, withdrawn when nothing would be sent.
- AcceptForm: disable "Review invitation" until the field holds a usable token; stash the chosen file (or clear a stale stash) for the accept screen on submit.
- acceptHandoff (new), AcceptInvitation / AcceptInvitationPanel / FileAcquire: carry the home-page file to `/accept` in memory (a File handle only, never parsed early) and pre-fill the consent dropzone, seeded once on first mount so a back edge does not resurrect it; the parse stays behind the existing consent gate.
- FileDropzone (new) / FileSelect: extract the bare dropzone so the home page can use it standalone, while FileSelect keeps composing it with an action button for the file-acquire and Advanced screens.
- docs/COMMUNICATION.md, CHANGELOG.md: reflect the shared drop, the accept-side carry-over, and the empty-disclosure wording.

## Test plan

Ran: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format`; `npm run test` (unit projects, 530 web plus cli); and the browser project for the touched components -- `npx vitest run --project browser test/browser/{invitePanel,homePage,defaultExchangeColumns,acceptForm,acceptConsentGate,appShell,fileSelect,fileAcquire}.test.ts`.
New tests cover: the AcceptForm hand-off stash/clear contract and the disabled-until-token gate; the default-columns disclosure (correct chips, withdrawn when nothing is sent); and on the accept side, the pre-fill staying behind the consent gate, the consume-once stash, and a back edge not re-seeding the stale file.

## Background

Because one drop feeds both paths, the inviter's column disclosure originally rendered in the invite panel even for an acceptor; moving it under the file (as "Default exchange columns") makes it a neutral property of the chosen file, with the invite-only Advanced Options control kept in the invite panel. A multi-reviewer pass also corrected a consent-surface overclaim: "everything else stays on your device" became "your partner never receives the values in your non-matching rows", since PSI exchanges blinded key material for every row, not only matching ones.

## Checklist

- [x] Docs: enumerated `docs/` and `docs/spec/`; updated `docs/COMMUNICATION.md` (overview tier) for the shared drop, the accept-side file carry-over, and the empty-disclosure wording -- no `docs/spec/` change, as no wire format, constant, or algorithm step changed.
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` updated -- corrected the existing quick-path disclosure entry's empty-state clause; this redesign refines web features already listed under `[Unreleased]`, so no new entry is warranted pre-release.
- [x] Security review -- done: three independent reviewers (disclosure surface, client confidentiality / consent gate, injection / display boundary); all CLEAR TO MERGE, findings INFO/LOW only, no exploitable mechanism. Presentation-only disclosure (transmitted/token sets unchanged); consent gate proven intact; sanitization and intake bounds preserved.

author: mderdzinski
body:
## Summary

Adds the **Reminders** feature from the design system's new `guidelines/notifications.md` spec. Two opt-in notification types, gated by a permission-priming sheet, with a bell IconButton in the Capture header opening a pushed Reminders screen (the app's first Settings surface).

**Voice constraints honored:**
- Both reminders default OFF; neither fires until the user enables it.
- "A gentle invitation, never a nag."
- Priming sheet shows *before* the OS permission prompt the first time either reminder is enabled.

**The two reminder types:**
- **Notice reminders** — random fire(s) within active hours, capped at the chosen bucket (once or 2–3/day), spaced ≥60 min apart. Body: *"What are you noticing right now?"* → opens Capture.
- **Reflection reminders** — daily at a chosen time, fires *only when unreflected moments exist*. Body: *"{N} moments are waiting to be revisited."* → opens Path.

Watch is out of scope: iOS-scheduled notifications bridge to the paired watch automatically when the phone is locked.

## Commits

1. `feat(core): add CairnSwitch primitive` — sage-on pill switch mirroring the design's Switch.jsx.
2. `feat(core): add RemindersSettings value type + persistence helpers` — Codable struct backing one @AppStorage key.
3. `feat(core): add RemindersScheduler + tests` — pure-function scheduling engine; **9 new deterministic tests** (42 total).
4. `chore(ios): ship faceted cairn glyph in iOS asset catalog` — for NotifPreview.
5. `feat(ios): add Reminders screen scaffolding + sub-components` — five new files (RemindersView, ReminderCardHead, ValueRow, NotifPreview, TimePickerSheet).
6. `feat(ios): wire RemindersService for permission + scheduling` — UN integration, foreground gate for reflect reminders, deep-link extraction; RootTabView gains the cairn:// router for capture/path/patterns.
7. `feat(ios): add PrimingSheet and first-toggle priming flow` — intercepts the first toggle-on, defers settings mutation until the user taps Allow and the OS grants.
8. `feat(ios): add bell IconButton to Capture header → Reminders` — restructures header HStack, pushes RemindersView via NavigationStack.

## Working time pickers

Tapping "Active hours" or "Remind me at" opens a medium-detent sheet with iOS DatePicker(hourAndMinute) controls (start + end for the range, single for the daily time). Times persist as minutes-since-midnight inside the same RemindersSettings blob.

## Known tradeoffs

- **Pending-count gate only works in foreground.** When the app is backgrounded, iOS delivers the reflect reminder regardless; the willPresent gate suppresses it only when the user is actively in the app and has no pending moments. A UNNotificationServiceExtension could gate properly but adds a separate target + shared-app-group store. Deferred to a future PR.
- **iOS background scheduling latency.** UN delivery isn't guaranteed precise to the minute. Standard iOS behavior.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Watch Reminders surface (system bridging handles delivery).
- Per-day-of-week scheduling, snooze, per-category reminders, adaptive timing.
- UNNotificationServiceExtension for proper background reflect gating.

author: patmmccann
body:
### Motivation
- The custom `no-redundant-validated-condition` rule could report redundant conditionals when an identifier previously validated by an early guard was reassigned, updated, redeclared, or shadowed inside block/catch scopes.

### Description
- Stop truthy-fact propagation at `BlockStatement` and `CatchClause` boundaries by extending the scope node set in `plugins/eslint/noRedundantValidatedCondition.js`.
- Add `collectPatternIdentifiers` and `collectInvalidatedIdentifiers` to discover identifiers invalidated by `AssignmentExpression`, `UpdateExpression`, and `VariableDeclarator` and wire `sourceCode.visitorKeys` for traversal.
- Clear matching known-truthy facts before inspecting each statement so stale facts are not used to report redundant conditionals.
- Add `plugins/eslint/test/noRedundantValidatedCondition.test.js` with RuleTester cases covering reassignment invalidation, block-scoped shadowing, catch-parameter shadowing, and the original redundant-condition report.

### Testing
- Ran the RuleTester file with `node plugins/eslint/test/noRedundantValidatedCondition.test.js`, and the tests passed.
- Running `npx eslint plugins/eslint/noRedundantValidatedCondition.js plugins/eslint/test/noRedundantValidatedCondition.test.js` emitted ignored-file warnings because the `plugins/eslint` path is excluded by the repo ESLint config.
- Running `npx eslint --no-ignore plugins/eslint/noRedundantValidatedCondition.js plugins/eslint/test/noRedundantValidatedCondition.test.js` surfaced repository style rule errors unrelated to the plugin logic, so the RuleTester run is the targeted verification for this change.

author: swawdbot
body:
## Problem

Clicking from the workout list INTO an exercise lagged badly on slow/gym wifi — a full-page "Loading exercise..." spinner for 10–20s — **even when the exercise had been visited before and all heavy data was cached**.

Root cause: the load effect gated the whole render on `isInitialLoading`, which only flipped false at the end of an awaited `Promise.all` containing two network calls that fall back only on *failure*, not *slowness*:
- `api.getCurrentUser()` — used for exactly one thing: picking the program name.
- `LocalStorage.getOneRM()` — always `await`s `/api/one-rm` with no prefer-cache path.

A hung request kept `Promise.all` pending → spinner stayed up.

## Fix (stale-while-revalidate; mirrors PR #25's workout-page fix)

- **storage.ts** — add `getOneRMPreferCache()` (mirrors `getWorkoutProgressPreferCache`): serves the in-memory cache when warm, network only on a cold load.
- **exercise.tsx** —
  - Seed `selectedProgram` **synchronously** from `localStorage.getItem('selected-program')` (the same key the workout page uses), so the right program's exercise paints on the first render.
  - Resolve the exercise from that state instead of the awaited network user; drop `getCurrentUser` from the render-critical `Promise.all`.
  - Fetch `getCurrentUser` in a **background** effect that corrects the program (and persists it to localStorage) only when the server value actually differs — the functional `setState` returns the same reference otherwise, so an agreeing response triggers no re-render and no input-clobbering re-resolve. A hung/failed request can never hold up the spinner.

No change to swap resolution, the working-set count, optimistic completion, warm-up detection, or `getWorkoutProgressPreferCache`. Only: render from cache + don't block on the network user/1RM.

## Verification (real WebKit / iOS engine, 390×844)

All checks pass with **every** `/api/**` GET stalled 18s via route interception, using in-SPA navigation (cache persists like a real device):
- **Warm + stalled** → Deadlift detail (name + Complete button) paints at **75ms**, no "Loading exercise..." spinner; correct exercise.
- **Regression** → completing a set still optimistically advances (exercise/1 → exercise/3, skipping the warm-up).
- **Cold + stalled** → spinner shows (acceptable) and resolves once the network is released.
- No console errors.

`/code-review xhigh --fix` applied: hardened the background effect (correct-then-persist so a `setItem` throw can't block the program correction) and aligned the prefer-cache comment with the accepted `getWorkoutProgressPreferCache` design. Other findings (shared user/program hook, generic prefer-cache, workout.tsx still using blocking getOneRM) were out-of-scope refactors and noted, not applied.

TypeScript clean in touched files; production build green.

author: codyworsnop
body:
#### Description

**Summary of the change**:  

Fixes a connection leak in R2dbcConnectionImpl.withConnection when acquisition succeeds but beginTransaction() fails — including coroutine cancellation, transient BEGIN errors, or any other failure on the begin path.

**Detailed description**:
- **Why**:  If beginTransaction() throws or the coroutine is cancelled during BEGIN, the lambda aborts before assignment. localConnection stays null, cx goes out of scope, and the connection is leaked.

- **What**:  Acquire under NonCancellable so cancellation cannot strand a connection between awaitLast() and BEGIN; Wrap the begin/assign block in runCatching; on failure, call releaseConnection(cx) before rethrowing; Add releaseConnection() — NonCancellable + runCatching { connection.close() } — as the single release path; Change close() to atomically take-and-null localConnection under the lock, then release outside the lock (no re-entry into withConnection when nothing is held).

- **How**: withConnection now acquires under NonCancellable, wraps begin/assign in runCatching, and calls a new releaseConnection(cx) in onFailure before rethrowing. close() takes and nulls localConnection under the existing lock, then releases outside the lock — it no longer calls withConnection when nothing is held.

---

author: rahulsmahadev
body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

Follow-up to #2610. Addresses two review threads on that PR:
- @laskoviymishka: move the `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` off of the core `UnboundPartitionField` / `UnboundPartitionSpec` types and apply it only when these types are serialized as part of `CreateTableRequest`.
- @viirya (non-blocking): add a positive serialization test for `UnboundPartitionField::field_id` (set case).

## What changes are included in this PR?

#2610 added `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` to `UnboundPartitionField::field_id` and `UnboundPartitionSpec::spec_id` so that REST `CreateTableRequest` payloads would omit unset partition ids. The same core types are also serialized as part of `TableUpdate::AddSpec` on the commit path, where a missing `spec-id` would hard-fail a Java REST server (`PartitionSpecParser.fromJson` throws `IllegalArgumentException: Cannot parse missing int: spec-id`). The breakage is latent today only because `TableMetadataBuilder::add_partition_spec` always populates `spec_id` via `with_spec_id` before pushing the `AddSpec` change.

This PR moves the skip behavior out of the core spec types and into the REST layer:

1. Drop `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` from `UnboundPartitionField::field_id` and `UnboundPartitionSpec::spec_id`. The core types again emit `spec-id` / `field-id` as `null` when unset, matching the pre-#2610 wire format and preserving the `TableUpdate::AddSpec` contract.
2. Add a `serialize_with` helper on `CreateTableRequest::partition_spec` that serializes through private shadow types whose fields skip the ids when `None`. This preserves the externally visible REST payload shape (`partition-spec` omitted entirely when unset; inner `spec-id` / `field-id` omitted when unset) without coupling the core spec type to it.

The shadow-type approach was chosen over a public newtype wrapper to keep the change scope to the REST crate and avoid touching `iceberg::spec::partition`'s public surface beyond the revert.

## Are these changes tested?

Yes. Four new / updated tests:

- `crates/iceberg/src/catalog/mod.rs::test_add_spec_emits_spec_id_key`: regression guard that `TableUpdate::AddSpec` always emits the `spec-id` key, including when `spec_id` is `None`. This is the test that would have caught the latent bug if #2610 had been merged without the `add_partition_spec` always-populates-spec_id invariant.
- `crates/iceberg/src/spec/partition.rs::test_unbound_partition_field_field_id_set_is_serialized`: positive test that a set `field_id` round-trips under the kebab-case `field-id` key (viirya's follow-up ask).
- `crates/catalog/rest/src/types.rs::test_create_table_request_partition_spec_skips_inner_none_ids`: verifies that the REST shadow serializer omits inner `spec-id` and `field-id` when unset, and emits them when set.
- `crates/iceberg/src/spec/partition.rs::test_unbound_partition_spec_serialization_emits_none_as_null` replaces the previous skip-expectation test and documents the new contract on the core type.

All pre-existing tests in `iceberg` (1361) and `iceberg-catalog-rest` (45) still pass. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` are clean on both crates.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p iceberg --lib`
- [x] `cargo test -p iceberg-catalog-rest --lib`
- [x] `cargo fmt --check -p iceberg -p iceberg-catalog-rest`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p iceberg -p iceberg-catalog-rest --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

author: braedensc
body:
## Stage 3 PR4 — Priority grid + staging tray

Implements the free-canvas urgency × importance grid and its staging tray (EisenClaw parity), replacing the `GridView` stub. Part of Stage 3 Wave B.

### What's here

**Grid canvas** (`GridCanvas.tsx`)
- Quadrant background tints, 10×10 graph-paper lines, two center axes, and corner quadrant labels (each in its `quadrantMeta` color).
- Verbatim EisenClaw visual constants live in `grid-constants.ts`.

**Placed cards** (`GridCard.tsx`)
- 112px card centered at `(x, 1−y)` — screen-y is inverted from data-y, so high importance sits at the top.
- 3px top border = recurring-status color (`recurringStatus` + `RC_COLOR`) when recurring, else the quadrant color for `(x, y)`.
- Recurring status badge + `×N` badge once `doneCount ≥ 3`.
- Hover actions: inline rename, back-to-tray (`staged:true`), soft-delete. **Mark-done is intentionally deferred** — it needs the Done data-layer RPC from a parallel PR.

**Visibility filter** — a task renders on the grid only when active, `!staged`, not done today, has non-null `x`/`y`, and (for recurring tasks) its status is not `ok`.

**Drag + placement**
- Reposition placed cards via `useFreeDrag` with a live ghost; commit `x`/`y` on drop through `useUpdateTask`. **No collision resolution on drag** (clustering absorbs overlaps in a later PR).
- Tray → grid: desktop drag (`staged:false`) and mobile (< 720px) tap-select → tap-place, via a new `useIsMobile` hook + `toNormalized`.
- Empty states for both the grid and the tray.

### Scope / file ownership
Touches only `src/features/grid/**` and the new `src/hooks/use-is-mobile.ts`. `src/App.test.tsx` is updated to mock GridView's new hook dependencies (the shell smoke test renders the default Grid tab) — no change to `App.tsx` itself.

### Tests
RTL component tests with the data hooks mocked: placement filter (staged / done-today / ok-recurring hidden), y-inverted positioning, top-border color by quadrant/recurring, `×N` badge, and the hover-action mutations. Pointer-drag mechanics are already covered by `use-free-drag.test.ts`.

### Gates
`npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (66 passing) — all clean on Node 22.

body:
## What
SPEC-016 reality-check's requirements linked SPEC-011 at the pre-#83 path `specs/minspec/epic-backfill/requirements.md`, which dead-ends on disk. The #83 spec-directory renumbering moved it to `specs/minspec/SPEC-011-epic-backfill/requirements.md`. This repoints the link to the current path and verifies the target exists.

## Why
Closes #166. A stale cross-spec link in a never-wrong signpost artifact is a defect — it makes the reference lie.

**Root cause:** the #83 directory rename moved SPEC-011's folder but no gate re-pointed cross-spec relative links, and nothing asserts SPEC-016's relative link targets resolve on disk — so the dead link committed silently.

## Approval integrity
Link-path edits are hash-neutral (merged canonical hash collapses relative link paths, #252/SPEC-022). SPEC-016's canonical hash is unchanged (`d908933…`), so the committed approval sidecar (`.minspec/approvals/specs/agent-execute/SPEC-016-reality-check/requirements.md.json`) still resolves to **approved** — verified via `scripts/hooks/canonical.py --hash`.

## Tests
- `packages/minspec/tests/spec016-links.test.ts` — T3 regression: scans every relative markdown link in SPEC-016 and fails if any target does not exist. Written failing-first (caught the stale link), now passing.
